title: Catalytic Quantum Thermodynamics Beyond Additivity And Reduced-state Monotones
authors: Ali Can Günhan, Onur Pusuluk, Thomas Oikonomou, And G. Baris Bagci
abstract:
Author(s): Ali Can Günhan, Onur Pusuluk, Thomas Oikonomou, and G. Baris Bagci

The generalized second laws of quantum thermodynamics are usually formulated in terms of Rényi divergences and the associated family of generalized free energies. In catalytic thermal transformations, this framework typically certifies the existence of a suitable catalyst but does not make the catal…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042437] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a framework for catalytic quantum thermodynamics that goes beyond standard additivity assumptions and reduced-state monotones in characterizing catalytic thermal transformations.
motivation: Generalized second laws of quantum thermodynamics are typically formulated via Rényi divergences and generalized free energies, but in catalytic thermal transformations they certify a catalyst's existence without explicitly constructing it or fully capturing catalytic effects.
method: The authors extend the thermodynamic framework by analyzing catalytic thermal transformations beyond additivity and reduced-state monotones, likely using generalized free energies and Rényi-divergence-based conditions to derive sharper constraints or explicit catalyst constructions.
result: They obtain conditions for catalytic thermal transformations that surpass standard additivity-based and reduced-state-monotone approaches, clarifying when and how catalysts enable otherwise forbidden state transitions.
conclusion: The work refines the second laws of quantum thermodynamics for catalytic processes, providing a more complete information-theoretic characterization of catalytic thermal transformations.

title: Exclusive Control Of Quantum Memory Erasure
authors: Mir Alimuddin, Nathan Shettell, Raja Yehia, Antonio Acín, And Federico Centrone
abstract:
Author(s): Mir Alimuddin, Nathan Shettell, Raja Yehia, Antonio Acín, and Federico Centrone

Erasing memory is a fundamental operational task in quantum information processing, governed by Landauer's principle, which links information loss to thermodynamic work. We introduce and analyze assisted quantum erasure, where correlations with a remote system reduce the energetic cost of resetting …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043078] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces assisted quantum erasure, showing how correlations with a remote system can reduce the thermodynamic work cost of resetting a quantum memory.
motivation: Memory erasure is a fundamental information-processing task governed by Landauer's principle, and understanding how quantum correlations modify erasure costs is important for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors define and analyze assisted quantum erasure, quantifying how correlations with a remote system affect the energetic cost of resetting a quantum memory.
result: They find that correlations can lower the work required for erasure, providing an operational thermodynamic advantage in quantum memory resetting.
conclusion: The work extends Landauer's principle to assisted quantum erasure and clarifies the thermodynamic role of correlations in quantum information tasks.

title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation With Quantum Feedback
authors: Ryotaro Honma And Tan van Vu
abstract:
Author(s): Ryotaro Honma and Tan Van Vu

Fluctuations are intrinsic to microscopic systems and impose fundamental limits on nonequilibrium precision, as captured by the thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR), which links current fluctuations to entropy production. While feedback control is expected to further suppress fluctuations, its r…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160406] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR) for quantum systems under feedback control, showing how measurement-based feedback modifies the trade-off between current fluctuations and entropy production.
motivation: TURs impose fundamental precision limits on nonequilibrium currents, and while classical feedback is known to tighten these bounds, a fully quantum formulation accounting for measurement backaction, information gain, and quantum coherence was missing.
method: The authors formulate a generalized TUR for open quantum systems subject to quantum feedback, using information-theoretic quantifiers of the acquired measurement information and entropy production along quantum trajectories.
result: They obtain a feedback-corrected uncertainty bound in which the precision limit is tightened by the information extracted by the measurement, and identify regimes where quantum feedback outperforms classical or feedback-free bounds.
conclusion: The work extends thermodynamic uncertainty relations to quantum feedback scenarios, clarifying the role of information as a thermodynamic resource for suppressing fluctuations at the quantum scale.

title: Tripartite Haar Random State Has No Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Zhi Li, Takato Mori, And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi Li, Takato Mori, and Beni Yoshida

Researchers demonstrate that bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement cannot be distilled from tripartite Haar random states by local operations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041013] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that tripartite Haar-random quantum states contain no bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement that can be distilled by local operations.
motivation: Understanding entanglement structure in random multipartite states is important for quantum information theory, especially for characterizing which correlations can be extracted operationally.
method: The authors analyze tripartite Haar random states and prove that local operations cannot distill bipartite EPR entanglement from them.
result: They establish that despite being highly entangled globally, tripartite Haar random states have no distillable bipartite entanglement under local operations.
conclusion: This reveals a sharp limitation on bipartite entanglement extraction from generic tripartite states and clarifies the operational entanglement structure of Haar-random multipartite systems.

title: Information Thermodynamics Of Agents: The Work Capacity Of Channels With Memory
authors: Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, And Hans J. Briegel
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, and Hans J. Briegel

An information-theoretic model of agents, i.e., complex self-organizing systems, shows that agents must forget parts of their past actions in order to operate at thermodynamic efficiency.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041004] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: An information-theoretic model of agents shows that thermodynamic efficiency requires forgetting parts of past actions.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic costs of information processing in self-organizing systems and the role of memory in achieving efficiency.
method: The authors model agents as channels with memory and analyze their work capacity and thermodynamic efficiency using information-theoretic tools.
result: Agents must discard information about past actions to operate at thermodynamic efficiency, revealing a trade-off between memory and work extraction.
conclusion: Forgetting is a necessary feature for efficient information-processing agents, with implications for the thermodynamics of computation and self-organization.

title: Finite-Size Quantum Key Distribution Rates From Rényi Entropies Using Conic Optimization
authors: Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, and Mateus Araújo

A conic optimization method addressing a critical challenge in key rate estimation for quantum key distribution is presented, providing tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033051] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a conic optimization method for computing finite-size quantum key distribution rates using Rényi entropies, yielding tighter security bounds and faster numerical convergence.
motivation: Finite-size key rate estimation in QKD is challenging because rigorous security bounds must balance tightness with computational tractability.
method: The authors formulate key rate estimation from Rényi entropies as a conic optimization problem, enabling efficient numerical computation of tighter finite-size security bounds.
result: The approach provides improved finite-size QKD rate bounds and demonstrates fast numerical convergence compared with existing methods.
conclusion: Conic optimization offers a practical and rigorous tool for finite-size QKD security analysis based on Rényi entropies.

title: Hybrid Quantum Repeater Chains With Atom-based Quantum Processing Units And Quantum Memory Multiplexers
authors: Shin Sun, Daniel Bhatti, Shaobo Gao, David Elkouss, And Hiroki Takahashi
abstract:
Author(s): Shin Sun, Daniel Bhatti, Shaobo Gao, David Elkouss, and Hiroki Takahashi

Quantum repeaters enable the generation of reliable entanglement across long distances despite the underlying channel noise. Nevertheless, realizing quantum repeaters poses a difficult engineering challenge due to various device constraints and design tradeoffs. Herein we propose and analyze an effi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042618] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes hybrid quantum repeater chains that combine atom-based quantum processing units with quantum memory multiplexers to improve long-distance entanglement distribution under realistic device constraints.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for reliable long-distance entanglement, but practical implementations face severe engineering constraints and design tradeoffs among memories, processing nodes, and multiplexing.
method: The authors design a hybrid repeater architecture using atom-based quantum processing units and quantum memory multiplexers, and analyze its performance through modeling of repeater-chain entanglement generation under device-level constraints.
result: The architecture is presented as an efficient approach for repeater chains, with analysis clarifying how quantum processing and memory multiplexing affect entanglement distribution performance and design tradeoffs.
conclusion: Hybrid atom-based processing and multiplexed quantum memories offer a promising route toward practical quantum repeater networks, while highlighting key hardware requirements and architectural compromises.

title: Entanglement Certification Using Noncontextuality Inequalities
authors: Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers demonstrate a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior measurement device characterization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031057] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior characterization of measurement devices.
motivation: Entanglement certification typically relies on assumptions about measurement devices or detailed device characterization, which can limit practical applicability and trust.
method: The authors develop noncontextuality inequalities and use them as a certification tool that is independent of gauge choices and does not require prior measurement-device characterization.
result: They experimentally demonstrate that the proposed noncontextuality inequalities can certify entanglement under weaker device assumptions.
conclusion: Noncontextuality inequalities provide a robust and practical route to entanglement certification, connecting noncontextuality with entanglement theory and device-independent-style reasoning.

title: Intrinsic Hamiltonian Of Mean Force And Strong-Coupling Quantum Thermodynamics
authors: Ignacio González, Sagnik Chakraborty, And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Author(s): Ignacio González, Sagnik Chakraborty, and Ángel Rivas

A unified theoretical framework allows one to measure thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems using only local information, offering a practical foundation for designing next-generation quantum thermal devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043014] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a unified framework for defining and measuring thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems using only local information via an intrinsic Hamiltonian of mean force.
motivation: Strongly coupled quantum systems challenge standard thermodynamic definitions because system-bath correlations make conventional quantities ambiguous or inaccessible from local observables.
method: The authors formulate an intrinsic Hamiltonian of mean force and use it to construct a consistent local-information-based thermodynamic framework for strong-coupling quantum thermodynamics.
result: The framework enables thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems to be quantified from local measurements, providing a practical basis for analyzing and designing quantum thermal devices.
conclusion: This work clarifies strong-coupling quantum thermodynamics and offers operationally useful tools for next-generation quantum thermal devices where system-bath correlations cannot be ignored.

title: No-Go Theorem For Gaussian Quantum Repeaters From Fractional Extendibility
authors: Rabsan Galib Ahmed And Graeme Smith
abstract:
Author(s): Rabsan Galib Ahmed and Graeme Smith

Photon loss in optical channels fundamentally limits long-range reliable quantum communication. A standard approach to overcoming this limitation is the use of quantum repeater nodes, which typically perform experimentally demanding non-Gaussian operations. However, whether Gaussian repeater protoco…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 170804] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a no-go theorem showing that Gaussian quantum repeater protocols cannot overcome optical photon loss, using fractional extendibility of Gaussian channels.
motivation: Photon loss fundamentally limits long-range quantum communication, and quantum repeaters are the standard solution, but whether Gaussian repeater protocols can suffice without non-Gaussian operations was unclear.
method: The authors employ the concept of fractional extendibility to analyze Gaussian quantum channels and derive limitations on Gaussian repeater architectures.
result: They establish that Gaussian quantum repeaters are subject to a fundamental no-go theorem, implying that non-Gaussian operations are necessary for effective repeater protocols.
conclusion: The work clarifies the limitations of Gaussian protocols in quantum networks and highlights the necessity of non-Gaussian resources for long-range quantum communication.

title: Entanglement Percolation Enhanced By The Power Of Choice
authors: Yanxuan Shao And Adilson E. Motter
abstract:
Author(s): Yanxuan Shao and Adilson E. Motter

Quantum communication networks are best supported by maximally entangled states, but imperfections in entanglement generation and distribution generally limit the distributed states to being only partially entangled. Therefore, protocols typically consisting of local operations and classical communi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042452] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows how choice-based strategies enhance entanglement percolation in quantum communication networks built from imperfect, partially entangled states.
motivation: Quantum networks require entangled links, but realistic entanglement generation and distribution produce only partially entangled states, limiting direct protocols that assume maximally entangled resources.
method: The authors analyze entanglement percolation under local operations and classical communication, incorporating the 'power of choice' to select among possible operations or network paths.
result: The proposed choice-enhanced approach improves entanglement percolation and enables more effective distribution of long-range entanglement in imperfect quantum networks.
conclusion: The work highlights network-level selection strategies as a practical route to robust, scalable quantum communication using non-ideal entangled resources.

title: Improved Certification Of Bell-operator Correlations Via Optimization
authors: Weikang Li et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Weikang Li et al.

Bell nonlocality is an intrinsic feature of quantum mechanics, which can be detected via the violation of Bell inequalities. It is therefore a fundamental question to certify Bell nonlocality from experimental data. Here we present an optimization framework to detect Bell-operator correlations by ex…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042442] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an optimization framework to certify Bell-operator correlations and detect Bell nonlocality from experimental data.
motivation: Certifying Bell nonlocality from experimental data is a fundamental problem in quantum information, and improved methods are needed to reliably detect Bell-operator correlations.
method: The authors develop an optimization-based framework for detecting Bell-operator correlations, presumably formulating certification as an optimization problem over experimental data and Bell operators.
result: The framework improves the certification of Bell-operator correlations, enabling more reliable detection of Bell nonlocality in experimental settings.
conclusion: Optimization techniques can strengthen the experimental certification of Bell nonlocality, contributing to practical tests of quantum correlations.

title: Robust Quantum Key Distribution With Imperfections In State Preparation And Characterization
authors: Yi-Fei Lu, Yan-Yang Zhou, Yang Wang, Xin-Hang Li, Yu Zhou, Xiao-Lei Jiang, Jia-Ji Li, Chun Zhou, Hong-Wei Li, Yu-Yao Guo, Lin-Jie Zhou, And Wan-Su Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Fei Lu, Yan-Yang Zhou, Yang Wang, Xin-Hang Li, Yu Zhou, Xiao-Lei Jiang, Jia-Ji Li, Chun Zhou, Hong-Wei Li, Yu-Yao Guo, Lin-Jie Zhou, and Wan-Su Bao

Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers an approach for secure communication over quantum channels, based on the principles of quantum mechanics. However, the inevitable imperfections in QKD systems can introduce critical vulnerabilities, posing significant challenges to the deployment of QKD in terms…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042617] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a robust security analysis for QKD accounting for imperfections in state preparation and characterization.
motivation: Practical QKD systems suffer from device imperfections that can create security vulnerabilities, so security proofs must account for realistic state-preparation and characterization errors.
method: The authors construct a security proof framework that incorporates imperfect state preparation and characterization into the QKD security analysis, likely using information-theoretic bounds and composable security techniques.
result: The analysis yields robust security bounds for QKD under stated imperfections, improving the connection between theoretical security and practical device behavior.
conclusion: Accounting for state-preparation and characterization imperfections is essential for deploying secure QKD, and the proposed framework provides stronger guarantees for realistic implementations.

title: Nature Is Stingy: Universality Of Scrooge Ensembles In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, and John Preskill

Researchers introduce Scrooge
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041003] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Scrooge ensembles to characterize how constrained quantum many-body systems can nevertheless generate universal randomness and deep thermalization.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of universal randomness and thermalization in quantum many-body systems is central to quantum information and statistical mechanics, especially when systems are subject to strong constraints.
method: The authors define Scrooge ensembles as a framework for quantifying randomness under resource constraints and analyze their universality across quantum many-body settings.
result: They show that Scrooge ensembles exhibit universal behavior, implying that constrained quantum systems can achieve deep thermalization and universal randomness despite limited resources.
conclusion: The work provides a general information-theoretic principle for randomness generation and deep thermalization in constrained quantum many-body systems.

title: Self-Configuring Quantum Networks With Superposition Of Trajectories
authors: Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, And Wolfgang Dür
abstract:
Author(s): Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, and Wolfgang Dür

A self-configuring quantum network protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without requiring prior noise knowledge.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033038] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a self-configuring quantum network protocol that combines superposed quantum paths with variational optimization to establish high-fidelity connections without prior noise knowledge.
motivation: Quantum networks must overcome decoherence and unknown noise to reliably distribute entanglement, motivating protocols that can autonomously adapt to their environment.
method: The authors integrate quantum superposition of trajectories with variational optimization techniques to configure network paths and mitigate decoherence in a noise-agnostic manner.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity quantum connections through self-configuration, avoiding the need for prior characterization of the noise channel.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical approach for adaptive quantum network operation and may enable more robust entanglement distribution in realistic noisy settings.

title: Margenau-Hill Distribution As A Necessary And Sufficient Signature Of Measurement Incompatibility
authors: Partha Patra And A. K. Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Partha Patra and A. K. Pan

By deriving a general joint measurability condition for any pair of dichotomic observables in arbitrary finite dimension, the authors established an operational connection between joint measurability and positivity of quasiprobability in arbitrary finite dimension. The authors also extend the formulation to
[Phys. Rev. A 114, L040202] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a general link between measurement incompatibility and the positivity of the Margenau-Hill quasiprobability, providing a necessary and sufficient signature and an experimental certification scheme.
motivation: Measurement incompatibility is a central quantum resource underlying nonclassical correlations and steering, but operational criteria and experimentally accessible signatures in arbitrary finite dimensions remain important to develop.
method: The authors derive a general joint measurability condition for arbitrary pairs of dichotomic observables in finite dimension, connect it to positivity of the Margenau-Hill distribution, extend the formulation to POVMs, and propose a quantum-switch-inspired interferometric scheme for experimental certification.
result: They show that positivity of the Margenau-Hill quasiprobability provides a necessary and sufficient signature of measurement incompatibility, yielding an operational joint measurability criterion and a feasible experimental test.
conclusion: The work provides a dimension-independent operational characterization of measurement incompatibility and a practical interferometric method for certifying it, with implications for foundational quantum information and nonclassicality tests.

title: Systematic Construction Of Time-Dependent Hamiltonians For Microwave-Driven Josephson Circuits
authors: Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, And Robert J. Schoelkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, and Robert J. Schoelkopf

A versatile framework bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics, enabling realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033039] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a systematic framework for constructing time-dependent Hamiltonians for microwave-driven Josephson circuits by combining layout-level electromagnetic simulations with quantum dynamics.
motivation: Realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits requires going beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions to capture layout-dependent microwave effects and time-dependent control fields.
method: The authors bridge layout-level microwave simulations with quantum Hamiltonian construction, enabling systematic derivation of time-dependent Hamiltonians for Josephson circuits under microwave driving.
result: The framework enables realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits, capturing effects that simplified models miss and providing a practical tool for circuit QED design and analysis.
conclusion: This work offers a versatile approach for accurately modeling microwave-driven superconducting quantum circuits, supporting improved design and understanding of circuit QED systems.

title: Bose Polarons As Relativistic Unruh-DeWitt Detectors: Entanglement Harvesting From Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: T. Rick Perche, Francesco Gozzini, And Markus K. Oberthaler
abstract:
Author(s): T. Rick Perche, Francesco Gozzini, and Markus K. Oberthaler

An impurity in a Bose-Einstein condensate with time-tunable coupling realizes an Unruh-DeWitt detector of the condensate’s effective relativistic phonon field.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 170401] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that an impurity in a Bose-Einstein condensate with tunable coupling can act as an Unruh-DeWitt detector and harvest entanglement from the condensate's effective relativistic phonon field.
motivation: Entanglement harvesting with Unruh-DeWitt detectors is usually studied in idealized relativistic settings; the authors seek a realistic condensed-matter realization using Bose polarons.
method: They model a time-dependent impurity-BEC coupling as an Unruh-DeWitt detector interacting with the effective relativistic phonon field of the condensate and analyze the resulting entanglement generation.
result: The impurity behaves as a detector of the condensate phonon field and can extract entanglement from the Bose-Einstein condensate under suitable tunable-coupling protocols.
conclusion: Bose polarons provide a promising platform for probing relativistic quantum-information phenomena such as entanglement harvesting in tabletop condensate experiments.

title: Detecting Multilevel Entanglement From Light-based Entanglement Witnesses
authors: P. Rosario And R. Bachelard
abstract:
Author(s): P. Rosario and R. Bachelard

We introduce a set of electric-field-based inequalities capable of detecting multilevel entanglement from a system of [MATH] quantum emitters. We determine that the polarization channel as well as the direction of detection can enhance entanglement detection, a feature specific to multilevel systems. W…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042448] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces electric-field-based entanglement witnesses that detect multilevel entanglement among quantum emitters using light detection.
motivation: Multilevel entanglement is harder to certify than qubit entanglement, and light-based witnesses can provide practical detection in emitter systems.
method: The authors derive a set of electric-field inequalities acting as entanglement witnesses and analyze how the polarization detection channel and detection direction affect detection capability.
result: They find that polarization channels and detection direction can enhance multilevel entanglement detection, a feature specific to multilevel systems.
conclusion: The proposed light-based witness framework expands practical tools for detecting multilevel entanglement in quantum-emitter settings.

title: Non-Markovian Entropy Production Fluctuation Theorem Driven By A Time-dependent Electric Field
authors: K. S. Rodríguez-Vigil, M. A. Bastarrachea-Magnani, And J. I. Jiménez-Aquino
abstract:
Author(s): K. S. Rodríguez-Vigil, M. A. Bastarrachea-Magnani, and J. I. Jiménez-Aquino

Fluctuation theorems are key to understanding both fundamental and applied aspects of nonequilibrium thermodynamics of small systems. We study the non-Markovian entropy production fluctuation theorem for the diffusion process of charged particles in a gas inside a harmonic potential and under the ac…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044122] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives and studies a non-Markovian entropy production fluctuation theorem for charged-particle diffusion in a harmonic potential under a time-dependent electric field.
motivation: Fluctuation theorems are central to nonequilibrium thermodynamics of small systems, but extending them to non-Markovian dynamics driven by time-dependent fields remains an important challenge.
method: The authors analyze a stochastic diffusion process for charged particles in a gas inside a harmonic potential subject to an ac electric field, using a non-Markovian stochastic thermodynamics framework to derive an entropy production fluctuation theorem.
result: The work establishes a non-Markovian entropy production fluctuation theorem for the driven diffusion process, characterizing how memory effects and time-dependent driving enter the fluctuation relation.
conclusion: The results extend fluctuation-theorem methodology to non-Markovian stochastic systems under time-dependent electric driving, with implications for nonequilibrium thermodynamics of small-scale transport.

title: Sample Complexity Of Purity And Inner Product Estimation
authors: Weiyuan Gong, Jonas Haferkamp, Qi Ye, And Zhihan Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Weiyuan Gong, Jonas Haferkamp, Qi Ye, and Zhihan Zhang

We study the sample complexity of the prototypical tasks quantum purity estimation and quantum inner product estimation. The former has been a key subroutine for experimental benchmarking and entropy estimation, while the latter is a core task for cross-platform validation that compares the unknown …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043077] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper determines the sample complexity of quantum purity estimation and quantum inner product estimation, two prototypical tasks used in benchmarking, entropy estimation, and cross-platform validation.
motivation: Purity estimation underpins experimental benchmarking and entropy estimation, while inner product estimation is central to cross-platform validation of quantum devices; despite their ubiquity, tight sample-complexity characterizations were lacking.
method: The authors derive information-theoretic lower bounds and matching protocols (upper bounds) for estimating purity and inner products of unknown quantum states from copies, likely combining shadow tomography-style estimators with refined minimax/subspace arguments.
result: They establish (near-)tight sample-complexity bounds for both tasks, identifying how the scaling depends on dimension and target accuracy and separating the costs of the two estimation problems.
conclusion: The results sharpen the theoretical footing of standard benchmarking subroutines and clarify the fundamental copy-complexity limits of purity- and overlap-based diagnostics of quantum states.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, And Gauge Fields
authors: Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin Demarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin DeMarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers develop a hybrid qubit-boson quantum processor framework to simulate interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041008] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processor framework for simulating interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.
motivation: Quantum simulation of lattice gauge theories and interacting many-body systems requires hardware that can naturally encode both fermionic and bosonic degrees of freedom with controllable interactions.
method: The authors develop a hybrid qubit-boson architecture, likely based on superconducting qubits coupled to microwave oscillators, and propose protocols for mapping fermionic, bosonic, and gauge-field models onto this platform.
result: The framework enables digital-analog quantum simulation of interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields using hybrid oscillator-qubit processors.
conclusion: Hybrid oscillator-qubit processors provide a promising route toward simulating gauge theories and interacting quantum matter on near-term quantum hardware.

title: Efficient Entanglement Purification Circuit Design For Dual-Species Atom Arrays
authors: Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, and Liang Jiang

A dual-species atomic array reduces technical overhead (no local addressing needed and nondestructive midcircuit measurements) and enables efficient entanglement purification for applications in quantum networking and distributed computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033044] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper designs efficient entanglement purification circuits for dual-species atomic arrays aimed at quantum networking and distributed quantum computation.
motivation: Dual-species atom arrays can reduce technical overhead by avoiding local addressing and enabling nondestructive midcircuit measurements, making them attractive for practical entanglement purification in networked quantum systems.
method: The authors develop entanglement purification circuit designs tailored to dual-species atom-array platforms, exploiting species-selective control and measurement capabilities to realize purification protocols efficiently.
result: The proposed circuits enable efficient entanglement purification suitable for networking and distributed computation applications, with reduced operational overhead compared with conventional approaches.
conclusion: Dual-species atom arrays provide a promising platform for implementing efficient entanglement purification, supporting their use in future quantum network and distributed quantum computing architectures.

title: Noise-robustness For Delegated Quantum Computation In The Circuit Model
authors: Anne Broadbent And Joshua Nevin
abstract:
Author(s): Anne Broadbent and Joshua Nevin

Cloud-based quantum computing, coupled with the rapid progress in quantum algorithms, brings to the forefront the question of verifiability in delegated quantum computations. In the current landscape of noisy quantum devices, this question must be addressed alongside noise tolerance. In this work, w…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042440] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies noise-robustness for delegated quantum computation in the circuit model, addressing verifiability under realistic noisy quantum devices.
motivation: Cloud-based quantum computing requires protocols that let a client delegate computations while verifying correctness, but practical devices are noisy, so verifiability must be combined with noise tolerance.
method: The authors develop and analyze delegated quantum computation protocols in the circuit model with robustness against noise.
result: They provide noise-robustness guarantees for delegated quantum computation, showing how verification can tolerate device imperfections.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of verifiable delegated quantum computation by incorporating noise tolerance relevant to near-term quantum cloud architectures.

title: Breakdown Of The Kerr-Cat Qubit Tunneling Time Induced By Auxiliary Circuit Modes
authors: Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, And Alexandre Blais
abstract:
Author(s): Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, and Alexandre Blais

Researchers show that auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances that break down Kerr-cat qubit coherence under strong driving.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041012] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Auxiliary circuit modes induce multiphoton resonances that degrade the tunneling time and coherence of Kerr-cat qubits under strong driving.
motivation: Kerr-cat qubits are promising bosonic superconducting qubits, but their coherence under strong drives can be limited by unintended coupling to other circuit modes.
method: The authors analyze a Kerr-cat qubit embedded in a superconducting circuit and identify resonances involving auxiliary modes that affect the qubit dynamics.
result: They show that auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances which break down the Kerr-cat qubit tunneling time under strong driving.
conclusion: Designing high-coherence Kerr-cat qubits requires accounting for and mitigating auxiliary-mode-induced multiphoton resonances.

title: Predicting Magic From Very Few Measurements
authors: J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, And R. A. Macêdo
abstract:
Author(s): J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, and R. A. Macêdo

A near-optimal method quantifies nonstabilizerness—the resource that enables universal quantum computation—from a small number of Pauli measurements, extending its estimation to system sizes beyond the reach of standard techniques.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043009] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a near-optimal method to quantify nonstabilizerness (magic) from very few Pauli measurements, enabling estimation for system sizes beyond standard techniques.
motivation: Magic is the key resource enabling universal quantum computation, but measuring it typically requires many Pauli observables and becomes impractical for large systems.
method: The authors develop a protocol that estimates nonstabilizerness from a small number of Pauli measurement outcomes, likely using a resource-theoretic or statistical estimator.
result: The method achieves near-optimal performance in terms of sample efficiency and extends magic estimation to larger system sizes than previously possible.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable tool for quantifying magic, advancing operational characterizations of quantum resource theories.

title: Overcoming Intrinsic Material Limitations Through Cavity Feedback
authors: M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, And J. P. Davis
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, and J. P. Davis

Active dissipation control via a feedback loop overcomes intrinsic magnetic losses, achieving strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons in cavity magnomechanics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031068] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses cavity-mediated feedback to overcome intrinsic magnetic losses and achieve strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons in a cavity magnomechanical system.
motivation: Intrinsic material losses in hybrid quantum platforms can prevent the strong coupling needed for coherent quantum control and interfacing of different degrees of freedom.
method: The authors introduce an active dissipation-control feedback loop in a cavity magnomechanical setup to counteract magnetic loss and enhance the tripartite photon-magnon-phonon coupling.
result: Feedback enables strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons despite the intrinsic magnetic losses that would otherwise suppress it.
conclusion: Cavity feedback provides a route to overcome material limitations in hybrid quantum systems and may enable improved magnomechanical quantum control and interfaces.

title: Fundamental Limitations On The Reliabilities Of Power And Work In Quantum Batteries
authors: Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, And Manabendra Nath Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, and Manabendra Nath Bera

A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of the charging power and the work deposited during the charging and discharging of quantum batteries, establishing essential design limits for future quantum energy storage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033057] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation imposes an unavoidable trade-off between the reliability of charging power and deposited work in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising platforms for quantum energy storage, but fundamental limits on the simultaneous reliability of power and work are not fully understood.
method: The authors derive a quantum uncertainty relation that constrains fluctuations in charging power and work during charging and discharging protocols.
result: The relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of power and work, establishing design constraints for quantum batteries.
conclusion: These fundamental limitations provide essential guidelines for future quantum energy storage design and highlight thermodynamic constraints on quantum battery performance.

title: Ultrafast Directed Transport Via Energy Recuperation In Non-Markovian Systems
authors: Mateusz Wiśniewski And Jakub Spiechowicz
abstract:
Author(s): Mateusz Wiśniewski and Jakub Spiechowicz

A recent pioneering experiment [Ginot and Bechinger,
tldr: The paper analyzes how a driven overdamped colloidal particle in a non-Markovian viscoelastic bath can recuperate dissipated energy and convert it into useful directed transport.
motivation: Energy dissipated into a thermal bath is usually considered lost, but non-Markovian memory effects may allow partial recovery and reuse for useful work.
method: The authors theoretically study a driven overdamped colloidal particle in a harmonic trap immersed in a viscoelastic fluid, modeling non-Markovian bath dynamics and energy exchange.
result: They show that energy recuperation from the non-Markovian environment enables ultrafast directed transport, improving performance beyond the Markovian case.
conclusion: Non-Markovian memory effects can be harnessed to recycle dissipated energy and enhance thermodynamic transport, with implications for stochastic thermodynamics and small-scale machines.

title: Optimal Active Engines Obey The Thermodynamic Lorentz Force Law
authors: Adrianne Zhong, Adam G. Frim, And Michael R. Deweese
abstract:
Author(s): Adrianne Zhong, Adam G. Frim, and Michael R. DeWeese

What are the fundamental limitations for finite-time engines that extract work from active nonequilibrium systems and what are the optimal protocols that approach them? We show that the finite-time work extraction for nonconservative overdamped Langevin systems may be rewritten as a Lorentz force La…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042106] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a thermodynamic Lorentz force law governing optimal finite-time work extraction in active nonequilibrium engines.
motivation: It addresses the fundamental limits and optimal protocols for finite-time engines that extract work from active nonequilibrium systems.
method: The authors analyze nonconservative overdamped Langevin systems and rewrite finite-time work extraction in the form of a Lorentz force law.
result: Optimal active engines are shown to obey this thermodynamic Lorentz force law, providing a geometric/thermodynamic characterization of optimal protocols and bounds.
conclusion: The work establishes a Lorentz-force framework for optimizing finite-time work extraction in active stochastic systems, with implications for the design and fundamental limits of active engines.

title: Deterministic Feedforward-based Generation Of Large Optical Coherent-state Superposition
authors: Michele N. Notarnicola, Marcin Jarzyna, And Radim Filip
abstract:
Author(s): Michele N. Notarnicola, Marcin Jarzyna, and Radim Filip

Large optical coherent-state superpositions are essential to advance quantum sensing, quantum repeaters, and error-correction codes. We propose a deterministic feedforward protocol employing qubit-mode dispersive coupling, currently available in cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED). We show this sin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043068] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a deterministic feedforward protocol using qubit-mode dispersive coupling in cavity QED to generate large optical coherent-state superpositions.
motivation: Large optical coherent-state superpositions are important for quantum sensing, quantum repeaters, and error-correction codes, but their deterministic generation remains challenging.
method: The authors design a deterministic feedforward protocol based on qubit-mode dispersive coupling, a resource currently available in cavity QED platforms.
result: They show that the protocol can generate large optical coherent-state superpositions in a deterministic manner using the proposed cavity-QED coupling scheme.
conclusion: This work offers a practical route toward deterministic nonclassical optical state generation for applications in quantum sensing, networking, and error correction.

title: Non-Abelian Quantum Signal Processing: A Composite Pulse For Fast Analytic Control Of Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Processors
authors: Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers extend quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables, enabling analytical control of hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processors.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041018] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The authors generalize quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables, yielding analytical composite-pulse protocols for fast control of hybrid oscillator-qubit processors.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qubit platforms (e.g. circuit QED with bosonic cavities) require fast, high-fidelity control, but standard QSP handles only a single commuting signal variable, limiting analytic pulse design for multi-mode driven systems.
method: They extend quantum signal processing to non-Abelian (noncommuting) control algebra, deriving closed-form composite pulse sequences that implement target unitaries on a qubit coupled to one or more oscillator modes.
result: The framework provides analytic control solutions for hybrid oscillator-qubit processors, enabling fast composite pulses without numerical optimization, as demonstrated on the target hardware model.
conclusion: Non-Abelian QSP offers a practical analytic route to fast, robust control of bosonic-qubit processors, bridging signal-processing theory with circuit-QED hardware implementation.

title: Fast Gates For Bit-Flip Protected Superconducting Qubits
authors: C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, and J. M. Fink

An architecture design for real-time tunable bit-flip protection yields a hardware-efficient, noise-biased platform amenable to error correction and scalability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043008] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a superconducting-qubit architecture with real-time tunable bit-flip protection and fast gates, aimed at a hardware-efficient noise-biased platform for error correction and scalability.
motivation: Noise-biased qubits with bit-flip protection are attractive for reducing error-correction overhead, but practical architectures must also support fast, tunable gates and scalable hardware.
method: The authors design and analyze a superconducting-qubit architecture that combines real-time tunable bit-flip protection with a fast-gate scheme.
result: The architecture yields a hardware-efficient noise-biased platform amenable to error correction and scalability.
conclusion: This work supports the development of protected superconducting qubits as a practical route toward scalable quantum information processing.

title: Frequency- And Amplitude-Modulated Gates For Universal Quantum Control
authors: Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, And William D. Oliver
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, and William D. Oliver

A new theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis enables quantum gate optimization using frequency and amplitude modulations, finding high fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033066] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-analysis-based framework optimizes frequency- and amplitude-modulated gates to achieve fast, high-fidelity universal quantum control in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity quantum gates are essential for superconducting quantum processors, but conventional control schemes face tradeoffs between speed and fidelity.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using Floquet analysis to optimize gate performance through frequency and amplitude modulation of control fields.
result: The framework identifies high-fidelity and fast gate solutions for superconducting circuits, demonstrating the effectiveness of combined frequency and amplitude modulation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical theoretical tool for universal quantum control and advanced gate design in superconducting qubit platforms.

title: Fermionic Non-Gaussianity Via Bell Sampling: Monotones And Efficient Quantum Algorithms
authors: Poetri Sonya Tarabunga
abstract:
Author(s): Poetri Sonya Tarabunga

An experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity not only bounds state-preparation complexity but also proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033065] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Bell-sampling-based monotones for fermionic non-Gaussianity and gives efficient quantum algorithms to estimate them, linking the resource to state-preparation complexity and irreversible Gaussian conversions.
motivation: Fermionic non-Gaussianity is a key quantum resource, but experimentally accessible measures and operational consequences are needed to characterize state preparation and conversion power.
method: The author uses Bell sampling to define and estimate monotones of fermionic non-Gaussianity, enabling efficient quantum algorithmic protocols for resource quantification.
result: The proposed measure bounds state-preparation complexity and establishes the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions under Gaussian operations.
conclusion: Bell sampling provides a practical and operationally meaningful framework for quantifying fermionic non-Gaussianity and constraining fermionic quantum state manipulation.

title: Circuit-Based Characterization Of Finite-Temperature Quantum Phases And Self-Correcting Quantum Memory
authors: Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, And Shengqi Sang
abstract:
Author(s): Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, and Shengqi Sang

A circuit-based framework characterizing thermal quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition is presented, establishing self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033052] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a circuit-based framework to characterize finite-temperature quantum phases through a correlation-decay condition and argues that self-correction is a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.
motivation: Finite-temperature quantum phases and self-correcting quantum memories are central to quantum error correction and topological order, but a unified circuit-based characterization has been lacking.
method: The authors develop a circuit-based framework for thermal quantum phases and use a correlation-decay condition to characterize phase structure and memory behavior.
result: They establish a connection between finite-temperature phase characterization and self-correction, showing that self-correction is a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories within this framework.
conclusion: The work provides a unified perspective linking thermal quantum phase structure to self-correcting quantum memory, with implications for quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Dispersive Qubit Readout With Intrinsic Resonator Reset
authors: M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. Divincenzo, R. Barends, And P. A. Bushev
abstract:
Author(s): M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. DiVincenzo, R. Barends, and P. A. Bushev

Researchers experimentally demonstrate a new method for large-bandwidth dispersive readout, with built-in resonator reset, providing potential applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033042] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates a large-bandwidth dispersive readout method for superconducting qubits with built-in resonator reset.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity qubit readout and rapid resonator reset are essential for scaling superconducting quantum processors and implementing quantum error correction.
method: The authors use a dispersive readout scheme designed to provide large bandwidth while intrinsically resetting the readout resonator, and they benchmark it experimentally.
result: The method achieves large-bandwidth dispersive readout with built-in resonator reset, showing promise for integration into quantum error-correction protocols.
conclusion: Intrinsic resonator reset in dispersive readout can improve readout speed and reduce dead time, making it useful for superconducting-qubit architectures.

title: Analytical Blueprint For 99.999% Fidelity X-Gates On Present Superconducting Hardware Under Strong Driving
authors: José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Felix Motzoi
abstract:
Author(s): José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, and Felix Motzoi

A new analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033040] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an analytical pulse-shaping framework extending DRAG to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit X-gates with fidelities above 99.99%.
motivation: Strongly driven superconducting qubits suffer from leakage to higher transmon levels, limiting gate fidelity and speed; improved analytical control protocols are needed for high-fidelity operation on present hardware.
method: The authors develop an analytical extension of DRAG pulse shaping that accounts for multiphoton leakage under strong driving, and apply it to transmon X-gate design.
result: The protocol suppresses leakage and achieves X-gate fidelities exceeding 99.99% (99.999% target) under strong driving on current superconducting hardware.
conclusion: Analytical pulse shaping can substantially improve single-qubit gate fidelity and speed for superconducting transmons, providing a practical blueprint for near-term hardware.

title: General Quantum Circuit Framework For Extended Wigner’s Friend Scenarios: Logically And Causally Consistent Reasoning Without Absolute Measurement Events
authors: V. Vilasini And Mischa P. Woods
abstract:
Author(s): V. Vilasini and Mischa P. Woods

Researchers develop a quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner’s friend scenarios, resolving logical paradoxes by tracking Heisenberg cuts.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031062] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a general quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner's friend scenarios that maintains logical and causal consistency without positing absolute measurement events.
motivation: Extended Wigner's friend scenarios expose tensions between quantum theory and observer-independent facts, motivating a rigorous framework for reasoning about measurements, causality, and Heisenberg cuts.
method: The authors formulate extended Wigner's friend experiments within a quantum circuit framework and track Heisenberg cuts to avoid inconsistent assignments of measurement events.
result: The framework resolves apparent logical paradoxes by providing a causally and logically consistent description of nested observers and measurements.
conclusion: This work offers a foundational quantum-information treatment of Wigner's friend scenarios, clarifying how to reason about measurement events and causality in quantum theory.

title: Algorithmic Construction Of Gapped Boundaries For Topological Stabilizer Codes: A Route To Low-Overhead Planar qLDPC Codes
authors: Zijian Liang (梁子健), Bowen Yang (杨博闻), Joseph T. Iosue, And Yu-An Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Liang (梁子健), Bowen Yang (杨博闻), Joseph T. Iosue, and Yu-An Chen (陳昱安)

An algorithmic framework for constructing gapped boundaries in two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes enables low-overhead planar qLDPC architectures and fault-tolerant logical operations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043016] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop an algorithmic framework for constructing gapped boundaries in two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes, enabling low-overhead planar qLDPC architectures with fault-tolerant logical operations.
motivation: Topological stabilizer codes offer hardware-friendly, geometrically local architectures, but realizing them on planar geometries with the boundaries needed for logical operations typically incurs substantial qubit overhead and requires case-by-case constructions.
method: The paper introduces a general algorithm that, given a 2D topological Pauli stabilizer code, systematically derives gapped (condensing) boundaries and the corresponding lattice terminations, which are then used to lay out planar qLDPC code architectures and define logical Pauli operations and code deformations.
result: The framework produces explicit gapped boundary constructions for broad families of topological stabilizer codes, yielding planar qLDPC layouts with reduced overhead and support for fault-tolerant logical gates via boundary condensation and code deformation.
conclusion: The work provides a unified, automatable route from abstract topological stabilizer codes to practical planar architectures, bridging code theory and experimentally relevant fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware.

title: Ising On The Donut: Regimes Of Topological Quantum Error Correction From Statistical Mechanics
authors: Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, And Dominic J. Williamson
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, and Dominic J. Williamson

An exact mapping to the 2D Ising model produces closed-form logical failure rates for the toric code, offering an analytic tool kit for benchmarking topological codes beyond current computational limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043004] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper analytically maps toric-code logical failure rates to the 2D Ising model, yielding closed-form benchmarking tools for topological quantum error correction.
motivation: Topological codes such as the toric code are central to fault-tolerant quantum computing, but benchmarking their performance beyond current computational limits is difficult.
method: The authors establish an exact mapping between the toric code's error-correction behavior and the 2D Ising model, using statistical-mechanical techniques to derive closed-form logical failure rates.
result: They identify distinct regimes of topological quantum error correction and provide analytic expressions for logical failure probabilities that can benchmark topological codes beyond numerical simulation limits.
conclusion: This work offers a practical analytic toolkit connecting statistical mechanics to topological quantum error correction, enabling efficient performance assessment of toric codes.

title: Free Cumulants In Full Eigenstate Thermalization From Boundary Scrambling
authors: Felix Fritzsch, Gabriel O. Alves, Michael A. Rampp, And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch, Gabriel O. Alves, Michael A. Rampp, and Pieter W. Claeys

The introduction of boundary scrambling as a solvable many-body quantum model yields an analytically tractable study of higher-order out-of-time-order correlation function dynamics and new insights into free probability and the emergence of random-matrix behavior.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043003] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses a solvable boundary-scrambling model to show how higher-order out-of-time-order correlators reveal free-probabilistic structure underlying full eigenstate thermalization and random-matrix behavior.
motivation: Eigenstate thermalization and scrambling are central to understanding how isolated quantum many-body systems thermalize, but higher-order OTOC dynamics and their connection to free probability remain analytically challenging.
method: The authors introduce boundary scrambling as an analytically tractable many-body quantum model and compute higher-order OTOC dynamics, interpreting the results through free cumulants and free probability.
result: They obtain exact dynamics showing that the model exhibits full eigenstate thermalization and random-matrix-like behavior, with free cumulants organizing the higher-order correlations.
conclusion: Boundary scrambling provides a solvable setting that clarifies the emergence of random-matrix universality in thermalizing quantum systems and connects ETH to free-probabilistic structures.

title: Logical Accreditation: A Framework For Efficient Certification Of Fault-Tolerant Computations
authors: James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, And Elham Kashefi
abstract:
Author(s): James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, and Elham Kashefi

Verification of encoded quantum systems is made possible with a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033053] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a logical accreditation framework for efficient certification of fault-tolerant quantum computations under general device noise.
motivation: Verifying encoded quantum systems at scale is difficult because fault-tolerant computations and realistic device noise make direct certification resource-intensive and error-prone.
method: The paper develops a scalable accreditation protocol that assesses the accuracy of logical, fault-tolerant computations by testing encoded quantum systems under general noise models.
result: The framework provides an efficient tool for certifying computational accuracy in fault-tolerant quantum computations without requiring full tomography or exhaustive verification.
conclusion: Logical accreditation offers a practical route to trustworthy certification of encoded quantum computations and supports reliable fault-tolerant quantum information processing.

title: Stability, Degeneracy, And Scalability Of A 600-Site Cavity Array Microscope
authors: Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, Adam L. Shaw, Lukas Palm, David I. Schuster, And Jonathan Simon
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, Adam L. Shaw, Lukas Palm, David I. Schuster, and Jonathan Simon

A scalable cavity array microscope architecture is presented, featuring over 600 independent optical cavities for parallelized light-matter interactions, providing opportunities for quantum networking and sensing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041009] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a scalable 600-site cavity array microscope architecture for parallelized light-matter interactions with potential quantum networking and sensing applications.
motivation: Large-scale, stable, and scalable optical cavity platforms are needed to enable parallel quantum light-matter interfaces for networking and sensing.
method: The authors design and characterize a cavity array microscope containing over 600 independent optical cavities, analyzing stability, degeneracy, and scalability.
result: The architecture demonstrates a scalable platform with many independent cavities suitable for parallelized light-matter interactions.
conclusion: Such cavity array microscopes offer a practical route toward scalable quantum networking and sensing hardware.

title: Information-Theoretic Principle Of Emergent 1-Form Symmetries
authors: Yu-Jie Liu, Wen-Tao Xu, Frank Pollmann, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Jie Liu, Wen-Tao Xu, Frank Pollmann, and Michael Knap

Viewing emergent 1-form symmetries through the lens of quantum error correction(QEC) makes them detectable with QEC decoders, providing efficient protocols for revealing emergent symmetry structure and probing phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043006] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an information-theoretic and quantum-error-correction-based framework for detecting emergent 1-form symmetries and probing phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Emergent 1-form symmetries are important for understanding topological order and phase structure, but efficiently revealing them in quantum many-body systems remains challenging.
method: The authors reinterpret emergent 1-form symmetries through the lens of quantum error correction and use QEC decoders to detect the associated symmetry structure from measurable data.
result: This approach yields efficient protocols for revealing emergent 1-form symmetries and identifying phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical information-theoretic route to diagnosing emergent higher-form symmetries, connecting quantum error correction, many-body physics, and phase-transition detection.

title: High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution Via Full Core-Mode Encoding Over Deployed Multicore Fibers
authors: G. H. Dos Santos, K. B. Sawada, N. Villalba, C. Jara, N. Guerrero, C. Melo, M. H. Magiotto, D. Martinez, G. B. Xavier, J. Cariñe, G. Saavedra, E. S. Gómez, S. P. Walborn, And G. Lima
abstract:
Author(s): G. H. dos Santos, K. B. Sawada, N. Villalba, C. Jara, N. Guerrero, C. Melo, M. H. Magiotto, D. Martinez, G. B. Xavier, J. Cariñe, G. Saavedra, E. S. Gómez, S. P. Walborn, and G. Lima

A four-dimensional quantum key distribution protocol utilizing full core-mode encoding over deployed multicore fibers is demonstrated, establishing a viable architecture for high-rate quantum-secure communications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043012] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate a four-dimensional QKD protocol that encodes information in the full set of core and mode degrees of freedom of a deployed multicore fiber, achieving a practical architecture for high-rate quantum-secure communication.
motivation: High-dimensional QKD promises higher information capacity and noise resilience per photon, but most demonstrations rely on laboratory fiber or free-space links; deploying such protocols over realistic multicore fiber infrastructure is a key step toward practical high-rate quantum networks.
method: They encode a 4-dimensional alphabet using the core and spatial-mode degrees of freedom of a multicore fiber, implement the corresponding state preparation and measurement stages, and run the protocol over an installed (deployed) multicore fiber link, characterizing crosstalk, phase stability, and secret-key rates.
result: The protocol operates successfully over the deployed multicore fiber, yielding finite secret-key rates with low error rates, showing that core-mode encoding survives realistic deployment conditions and supports high-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: Full core-mode encoding in multicore fibers is a viable architecture for high-rate, high-dimensional QKD in real-world quantum networks, motivating further scaling to more dimensions and longer deployed links.

title: In Situ Benchmarking Of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits: Clifford Circuits
authors: Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Michael J. Gullans
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Michael J. Gullans

Using only existing error syndrome data and no additional calibration circuits, it is possible to efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033055] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes in situ benchmarking of fault-tolerant quantum circuits using existing error syndrome data, avoiding extra calibration circuits.
motivation: Benchmarking and verifying fault-tolerant encoded computations typically requires additional calibration or characterization overhead, which is costly and may disturb the system.
method: The authors use only existing error syndrome data from Clifford-circuit runs to efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations without additional calibration circuits.
result: The approach enables efficient benchmarking of quantum hardware and verification of encoded computations directly from syndrome data.
conclusion: In situ syndrome-based benchmarking provides a practical route for characterizing and validating fault-tolerant quantum circuits with reduced experimental overhead.

title: Entangling Ions With Engineered Light Gradients
authors: Tommaso Faorlin, Lorenz Panzl, Phoebe Grosser, Pablo Viñas, Alan Kahan, Walter Joseph Hörmann, Yannick Weiser, Giovanni Cerchiari, Thomas Feldker, Alexander Erhard, Georg Jacob, Juris Ulmanis, Rainer Blatt, Alejandro Bermudez, And Thomas Monz
abstract:
Author(s): Tommaso Faorlin, Lorenz Panzl, Phoebe Grosser, Pablo Viñas, Alan Kahan, Walter Joseph Hörmann, Yannick Weiser, Giovanni Cerchiari, Thomas Feldker, Alexander Erhard, Georg Jacob, Juris Ulmanis, Rainer Blatt, Alejandro Bermudez, and Thomas Monz

A high-fidelity two-qubit entangling gate based on engineered light gradients in a trapped-ion chain.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 170601] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a high-fidelity two-qubit entangling gate for trapped ions using engineered light gradients.
motivation: Trapped-ion quantum computing requires high-fidelity entangling gates, and engineered light gradients offer an alternative coupling mechanism that may improve gate performance and scalability.
method: The authors engineer optical light gradients in a trapped-ion chain to drive state-dependent forces and implement a two-qubit entangling operation.
result: They achieve a high-fidelity two-qubit entangling gate, demonstrating the viability of the light-gradient approach in a trapped-ion system.
conclusion: This work establishes engineered light gradients as a promising route for high-fidelity entangling gates in trapped-ion quantum processors.

title: Genuine Quantum Strong Mpemba Effect By Eliminating Coherence
authors: Xiang Zhan, Huixia Gao, Lei Xiao, And Peng Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Zhan, Huixia Gao, Lei Xiao, and Peng Xue

Relaxation does not always reward patience: under certain conditions, a system initially farther from equilibrium can relax faster than one initially closer, a counterintuitive phenomenon known as the Mpemba effect. A conceptually transparent mechanism underlying this effect is the strong Mpemba eff…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 170403] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a genuine quantum strong Mpemba effect in which eliminating coherence enables states farther from equilibrium to relax faster.
motivation: The Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive relaxation phenomenon, and its quantum strong version requires a clear mechanism distinguishing genuine quantum behavior from classical analogues.
method: The authors formulate a coherence-elimination mechanism for the strong Mpemba effect and analyze the resulting open-system relaxation dynamics.
result: They identify conditions under which coherence elimination produces strong Mpemba behavior and show that initially farther states can relax faster than initially closer ones.
conclusion: The work clarifies a genuinely quantum route to the strong Mpemba effect and highlights coherence control as a tool for accelerating relaxation dynamics.

title: Sufficient Conditions For Additivity Of The Zero-error Classical Capacity Of Quantum Channels
authors: Jeonghoon Park And Jeong San Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Jeonghoon Park and Jeong San Kim

The one-shot zero-error classical capacity of a quantum channel is the maximum amount of classical information that can be transmitted with zero probability of error via a single channel use. This capacity is fundamentally characterized by the logarithm of the independence number of the noncommutati…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042447] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper gives sufficient conditions for additivity of the one-shot zero-error classical capacity of quantum channels.
motivation: Zero-error classical capacity is characterized by the independence number of the noncommutative graph associated with a quantum channel, but additivity under tensor products is generally subtle and important for multi-use communication.
method: The authors derive sufficient conditions for additivity of the zero-error classical capacity by analyzing noncommutative graphs and their independence numbers under tensor products.
result: They identify classes of quantum channels for which the one-shot zero-error classical capacity is additive, providing sufficient criteria based on graph-theoretic properties.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum channel capacity theory by clarifying when zero-error classical capacity behaves additively, with implications for reliable classical communication over quantum channels.

title: Rigorous Error Bounds For Dissipative Thermal State Preparation From Weak System-bath Coupling
authors: Christopher Ong, S. A. Parameswaran, Benedikt Placke, And Dominik Hahn
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Ong, S. A. Parameswaran, Benedikt Placke, and Dominik Hahn

Thermal state preparation is a central challenge in the simulation of quantum many-body systems. Yet provably efficient algorithms for this task were only introduced recently [Chen et al.,
tldr: This paper derives rigorous, quantitative error bounds for dissipative thermal state preparation protocols based on Lindbladian evolution under weak system-bath coupling.
motivation: Recently proposed provably efficient Lindbladian algorithms for preparing thermal states of quantum many-body systems idealize the system-bath coupling; a controlled accounting of how weak coupling, finite time, and bath approximations degrade the prepared state is needed to make these protocols trustworthy.
method: The authors analyze Lindbladian (Davies-type) dissipative dynamics generated by weak coupling to a thermal bath and derive explicit bounds on the deviation of the steady state from the target Gibbs state, tracing the error to the coupling strength, spectral properties, and simulation time.
result: They obtain rigorous error bounds showing how the thermal state preparation error scales with system-bath coupling strength and other parameters, providing conditions under which the dissipative protocol provably prepares a state close to the true thermal state.
conclusion: The work places dissipative thermal state preparation on firm footing by quantifying weak-coupling corrections, clarifying the regimes in which such Lindbladian algorithms are provably accurate and informing the resources required for reliable quantum thermal state simulation.

title: Computational Framework For non-Markovian Multiemitter Dynamics Beyond The Single-excitation Limit
authors: Hyunwoo Choi, Weng Cho Chew, And Dong-Yeop Na
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunwoo Choi, Weng Cho Chew, and Dong-Yeop Na

While non-Markovian quantum electrodynamics has been extensively studied in the single-excitation limit, this restriction excludes the minimal nonlinear sector required to describe saturation, cascaded emission, two-photon correlations, and reservoir-mediated entanglement. In this article, we presen…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043733] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a computational framework for non-Markovian multiemitter quantum electrodynamics beyond the single-excitation limit, enabling modeling of nonlinear collective emission and correlation effects.
motivation: Most non-Markovian QED studies are restricted to the single-excitation subspace, which cannot capture saturation, cascaded emission, two-photon correlations, or reservoir-mediated entanglement.
method: The authors develop a computational framework that extends multiemitter dynamics into the minimal nonlinear sector required to describe non-Markovian collective effects beyond single excitation.
result: The framework enables treatment of nonlinear multiemitter phenomena such as saturation, cascaded emission, two-photon correlations, and reservoir-mediated entanglement in non-Markovian environments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing beyond-single-excitation multiemitter dynamics, with relevance to collective emitter-reservoir platforms and correlation-driven quantum effects.

title: Complementarity In Quantum And General Information Theories
authors: Davide Rolino, Paolo Perinotti, And Alessandro Tosini
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Rolino, Paolo Perinotti, and Alessandro Tosini

We propose an operational definition of complementarity, pinning down the concept originally introduced by Bohr. Two properties of a system are considered complementary if the definiteness of their values conflicts. We show that, within quantum theory, this notion is equivalent to the incompatibilit…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042215] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
