tldr: The paper proposes an operational definition of Bohr-style complementarity and shows that in quantum theory it coincides with measurement incompatibility, extending the analysis to general information theories.
motivation: Complementarity is a foundational concept often invoked qualitatively, but it lacks a precise operational formulation that can be compared across quantum and general probabilistic information theories.
method: The authors define complementarity operationally via the conflict in definiteness of two properties and then relate this notion to incompatibility within quantum theory and broader information-theoretic frameworks.
result: They establish an equivalence between their operational notion of complementarity and incompatibility in quantum theory, clarifying the concept and enabling comparisons with general information theories.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for complementarity as an information-theoretic phenomenon and helps connect quantum foundations with generalized probabilistic theories.

title: Predicting Dynamics From Flows Of The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
authors: Dominik Hahn, David M. Long, Marin Bukov, And Anushya Chandran
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, David M. Long, Marin Bukov, and Anushya Chandran

Analytical treatments of far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics are few, even in well-thermalizing systems. The celebrated eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) provides a post hoc ansatz for the matrix elements of observables in the eigenbasis of a thermalizing Hamiltonian, given various respon…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043091] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical framework based on flows of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis to predict far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics in thermalizing systems.
motivation: Analytical treatments of far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics are scarce, even in well-thermalizing systems, and ETH has mainly served as a post hoc ansatz rather than a predictive dynamical tool.
method: The authors formulate and analyze flows of ETH matrix elements to derive predictions for observable dynamics from the eigenstate structure of thermalizing Hamiltonians.
result: The approach yields analytical predictions for far-from-equilibrium dynamics, extending the utility of ETH beyond static matrix-element ansätze.
conclusion: ETH-based flows provide a promising route for analytically describing quantum dynamics in thermalizing many-body systems.

title: Phase-space Representations Of Quantum Error-correcting Codes
authors: Enrico Bozzetto And Jonte R. Hance
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Bozzetto and Jonte R. Hance

We connect the structure theorem for quasiprobability representations to quantum error correction. For a code space invariant under a subgroup of an extended Weyl-Heisenberg group, the Brif-Mann construction gives a semifunctorial representation whenever its kernel satisfies the Stratonovich-Weyl ax…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043076] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper connects quasiprobability phase-space representations with quantum error-correcting code spaces invariant under subgroups of an extended Weyl-Heisenberg group.
motivation: Phase-space methods and quantum error correction are usually developed separately; the authors aim to bridge them via the structure theorem for quasiprobability representations.
method: Using the Brif-Mann construction, they obtain a semifunctorial representation of code-space symmetries whenever the kernel satisfies the Stratonovich-Weyl axioms, and apply this to code spaces invariant under extended Weyl-Heisenberg subgroups.
result: The construction yields phase-space representations adapted to quantum error-correcting codes, linking code symmetries to quasiprobability structures.
conclusion: This provides a framework for analyzing quantum codes through phase-space methods and suggests further connections between representation theory and quantum error correction.

title: Fast And Exact Approach For Stabilizer Rényi Entropy Via The Xor-fwht Algorithm
authors: Xuyang Huang, Han-Ze Li, Ching Hua Lee, And Jian-Xin Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Xuyang Huang, Han-Ze Li, Ching Hua Lee, and Jian-Xin Zhong

An XOR-FWHT algorithm is presented for the deterministic evaluation of the second-order stabilizer Rényi entropy of generic
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042005] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an XOR-FWHT algorithm for fast, exact evaluation of the second-order stabilizer Rényi entropy of generic pure quantum states.
motivation: Stabilizer Rényi entropy quantifies non-stabilizerness, a key quantum resource, but exact evaluation for large pure states is computationally expensive.
method: The authors exploit XOR-shifted amplitude correlations and fast Walsh-Hadamard transforms to compute the second-order stabilizer Rényi entropy deterministically without sampling or special state structure.
result: The algorithm reduces the computational cost from exponential-in-n complexity such as O(8^n) to a much cheaper transform-based scaling, enabling exact evaluation from full state vectors.
conclusion: This provides a practical tool for quantifying magic in pure states and supports resource-theoretic studies of non-stabilizerness in quantum information processing.

title: Toward Fault-tolerant Quantum Memory With Universal Continuous-variable Gates
authors: Sheron Blair, Francesco Arzani, Giulia Ferrini, And Alessandro Ferraro
abstract:
Author(s): Sheron Blair, Francesco Arzani, Giulia Ferrini, and Alessandro Ferraro

Universal continuous-variable gate sets are shown to enable fault-tolerant quantum memory. This is achieved via numerical simulation of the generation of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states and comparison with the fault-tolerant memory threshold of the GKP surface code.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042006] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper numerically studies whether universal continuous-variable gate sets can support fault-tolerant quantum memory using GKP states and the GKP surface-code threshold.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory is a central requirement for scalable quantum computing, and continuous-variable architectures with GKP states offer a promising route but require gate sets compatible with error-correction thresholds.
method: The authors simulate the generation of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states under universal continuous-variable gates and compare the resulting state quality against the fault-tolerant memory threshold of the GKP surface code.
result: The numerical analysis indicates that universal continuous-variable gate sets can enable fault-tolerant quantum memory when GKP state generation meets the required surface-code threshold conditions.
conclusion: Universal continuous-variable gates are shown to be viable for fault-tolerant quantum memory, supporting further development of CV quantum-computing architectures based on GKP states and surface-code error correction.

title: Spin-qubit Leapfrogging: Dynamics Of Shuttling Electrons On Top Of Another
authors: Nicklas Meineke And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Nicklas Meineke and Guido Burkard

Spin shuttling has crystalized as a powerful and promising tool for establishing intermediate-range connectivity in semiconductor spin-qubit devices. Although experimental demonstrations have performed exceptionally well on different materials platforms, the question of how to handle areas of low va…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043043] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the dynamics of spin shuttling electrons leapfrogging on top of one another in semiconductor spin-qubit devices, addressing challenges in maintaining coherent transport for intermediate-range connectivity.
motivation: Spin shuttling is a promising route to establish connectivity between distant spin qubits in semiconductor devices, but its performance in non-ideal regions such as low valley splitting or disordered potentials remains unclear.
method: The authors theoretically model the coherent dynamics of electrons shuttled in a double-well or moving quantum dot potential, including the case where two electrons are shuttled in close proximity and interact via Coulomb repulsion, leading to leapfrogging motion.
result: They identify conditions under which the leapfrogging dynamics preserves or degrades spin coherence, and characterize how interaction effects and shuttling speed influence the fidelity of electron transport.
conclusion: The work provides guidance for designing robust spin-shuttling protocols in semiconductor quantum dot arrays, highlighting the role of electron-electron interactions and suggesting parameter regimes for reliable connectivity.

title: Theory Of Out-of-Time-Ordered Transport
authors: Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, And Luca V. Delacrétaz
abstract:
Author(s): Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, and Luca V. Delacrétaz

Researchers establish an effective field theory capturing late-time out-of-time-order correlators to uncover hidden transport parameters.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041010] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an effective field theory for late-time out-of-time-order correlators to extract hidden transport parameters in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Out-of-time-order correlators are key diagnostics of quantum chaos and scrambling, but their late-time structure and connection to transport are not fully understood.
method: The authors construct an effective field theory describing late-time out-of-time-order correlator dynamics.
result: The theory captures late-time OTOC behavior and reveals transport parameters that are otherwise hidden.
conclusion: This provides a framework linking quantum chaos/scrambling diagnostics to transport properties in many-body systems.

title: Topological Mixed States: Phases Of Matter From Axiomatic Approaches
authors: Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, And Jong Yeon Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, and Jong Yeon Lee

A quantum information framework classifies mixed-state topological phases for open quantum systems, introducing phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a quantum-information axiomatic framework to classify mixed-state topological phases in open quantum systems using information-theoretic invariants.
motivation: Topological order is well understood for pure states, but open quantum systems require a mixed-state classification, and information-theoretic quantities can provide operational invariants.
method: It uses information convex sets, memory capacity, and secret sharing to define phase invariants and axiomatically classify mixed-state topological phases.
result: The framework introduces invariants that distinguish mixed-state topological phases and connects them to operational tasks such as quantum memory and secret sharing.
conclusion: This provides a quantum-information foundation for mixed-state topological phases, bridging topological order and quantum information in open systems.

title: Efficiently Learning Global Quantum Channels With Local Tomography
authors: Zidu Liu And Dominik S. Wild
abstract:
Author(s): Zidu Liu and Dominik S. Wild

Exponential decay of correlations enables scalable reconstruction of many-qubit processes and their global properties from local measurements.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043015] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a scalable method to reconstruct global many-qubit quantum channels from local tomographic measurements by exploiting exponential decay of correlations.
motivation: Full quantum process tomography scales exponentially with the number of qubits, so efficient reconstruction of global quantum channels and their properties is a central challenge.
method: The authors use local tomography combined with the exponential decay of correlations to reconstruct global quantum channels and predict their global properties.
result: They show that many-qubit processes can be efficiently learned from local measurements, enabling scalable characterization of global channel properties.
conclusion: Locality of correlations provides a practical route to efficient global quantum channel tomography, with implications for characterizing large quantum devices.

title: Refinements Of The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis Under Local Rotational Invariance Via Free Probability
authors: Elisa Vallini, Laura Foini, And Silvia Pappalardi
abstract:
Author(s): Elisa Vallini, Laura Foini, and Silvia Pappalardi

Using the mathematical language of free probability theory, researchers reveal how local rotational invariance structures matrix-element correlations, including their first subleading corrections.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043007] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: Using free probability theory, the authors show how local rotational invariance constrains the structure of matrix-element correlations in the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), including the first subleading corrections.
motivation: ETH successfully predicts the leading diagonal and off-diagonal structure of matrix elements of local observables in chaotic many-body systems, but its finer structure — especially subleading corrections and the role of symmetries — remains poorly understood. Local rotational invariance provides a controlled setting to sharpen these predictions.
method: The authors apply free probability theory, treating operators as freely independent noncommutative random variables, to derive the correlators of matrix elements of local observables in rotationally invariant systems, extending the analysis beyond leading order.
result: They obtain a refined characterization of ETH matrix-element correlations, including explicit first subleading corrections that follow from the rotational symmetry and the free-probabilistic structure of the operators.
conclusion: The work establishes free probability as a natural language for organizing ETH corrections in symmetric chaotic systems, suggesting systematic extensions to further symmetry classes and observables.

title: Holographic Duality Between Bulk Topological Order And Boundary Mixed-State Order
authors: Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Yizhi You
abstract:
Author(s): Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Yizhi You

Mapping open quantum systems to higher-dimensional topological order provides a new framework for characterizing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033041] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a holographic duality mapping bulk topological order to boundary mixed-state order, offering a framework for strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.
motivation: Open quantum systems and mixed-state phases require new theoretical tools beyond conventional closed-system topological order, motivating a duality-based characterization.
method: The authors develop a holographic mapping between higher-dimensional bulk topological order and boundary mixed-state order in open quantum systems.
result: This mapping provides a framework to characterize strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases via boundary mixed-state order.
conclusion: The work establishes a holographic lens linking topological order and mixed-state quantum phases, with implications for open quantum systems and quantum information.

title: Control Of Multipartite Entanglement Through Anisotropy Against Thermal Noise
authors: Samudra Sur And Saikat Sur
abstract:
Author(s): Samudra Sur and Saikat Sur

This Letter shows that the robustness of multipartite entanglement required for quantum computing platforms can be protected against thermal noise by tuning the interaction anisotropy in many-body systems. Focusing on both generalized Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger and generalized
[Phys. Rev. A 114, L040402] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that tuning interaction anisotropy in many-body systems can protect multipartite entanglement against thermal noise.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement is a key resource for quantum computing platforms, but it is fragile under thermal noise, motivating ways to preserve it in realistic many-body settings.
method: The authors analyze generalized GHZ and generalized states in many-body systems and identify how interaction anisotropy affects the survival of multipartite entanglement under thermal noise.
result: They find distinct anisotropy ranges where multipartite entanglement remains robust, demonstrating that anisotropy can create survival regions against thermal noise.
conclusion: Anisotropy tuning provides a practical route to stabilize multipartite entanglement in noisy many-body systems relevant to quantum computing.

title: Classification Of Kirkwood-Dirac Positivity-preserving Unitaries
authors: Jędrzej Burkat And Sergii Strelchuk
abstract:
Author(s): Jędrzej Burkat and Sergii Strelchuk

Kirkwood-Dirac (KD) quasiprobability distributions are increasingly used across quantum information science, yet their computational significance remains unclear. We classify unitary dynamics that preserve KD positivity and connect this structure to classical simulation. In contrast with the discret…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042446] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper classifies unitaries that preserve positivity of Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distributions and relates this structure to classical simulability.
motivation: Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobabilities are widely used in quantum information, but their computational meaning and the role of negativity remain insufficiently understood.
method: The authors characterize unitary dynamics that preserve KD positivity and connect the resulting class of operations to classical simulation strategies.
result: They obtain a classification of KD positivity-preserving unitaries, contrasting it with previously studied discrete quasiprobability structures and identifying implications for classical simulation.
conclusion: The work clarifies when KD quasiprobability positivity can be maintained under unitary evolution and how this constrains or enables efficient classical simulation.

title: Eigenstate-thermalization-hypothesis-ansatz-motivated Environmental-branch Approach To Open Quantum Systems
authors: Wen-Ge Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-ge Wang

In this paper, a method is developed for the study of a generic small central quantum system, which is locally coupled to an environment as a many-body chaotic quantum system that satisfies the eigenstate-thermalization-hypothesis (ETH) ansatz. The approach is based on properties of environmental br…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042216] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an environmental-branch approach for open quantum systems whose environment is a many-body chaotic system satisfying the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH).
motivation: Generic small quantum systems coupled to complex chaotic environments are difficult to treat with standard open-system methods, motivating an ETH-based characterization of the environment.
method: The approach uses the ETH ansatz and properties of environmental branches to derive an effective description of the central system's dynamics under local coupling to a many-body chaotic environment.
result: The paper formulates a tractable framework for open-system dynamics in which ETH-motivated environmental properties determine the reduced behavior of the central system.
conclusion: This provides a method for analyzing open quantum systems with chaotic many-body environments and connects ETH-based thermalization ideas to decoherence and system-environment dynamics.

title: Collective Strong Coupling Of Thermal Atoms To Integrated Microring Resonators
authors: Xiaoyu Cheng, Benyamin Shnirman, Alexandra Köpf, Guangcanlan Yang, Hong X. Tang, Hadiseh Alaeian, Tilman Pfau, And Robert Löw
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoyu Cheng, Benyamin Shnirman, Alexandra Köpf, Guangcanlan Yang, Hong X. Tang, Hadiseh Alaeian, Tilman Pfau, and Robert Löw

Strong coupling between atomic ensembles and high-quality optical cavities enables collective and nonlinear phenomena that are central to cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED). Many experiments have been performed on this topic, with most of them focusing on cold atoms. Here, we experimentally demon…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043063] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates collective strong coupling between thermal atomic ensembles and integrated microring resonators, extending cavity QED to a scalable photonic platform.
motivation: Collective strong coupling between atomic ensembles and high-quality optical cavities is central to cavity QED and nonlinear quantum optics, but most demonstrations rely on cold atoms. The work aims to show that thermal atoms can be used with integrated microring resonators.
method: The authors integrate a high-quality microring resonator with a thermal atomic ensemble and perform optical measurements to observe collective strong coupling, likely via Rabi splitting or avoided crossing in the transmission spectrum.
result: They report an experimental demonstration of collective strong coupling between thermal atoms and the integrated microring resonator, confirming that the coupled system reaches the strong-coupling regime.
conclusion: The results establish integrated microring resonators coupled to thermal atoms as a practical platform for collective cavity-QED phenomena and scalable quantum-photonic hybrid systems.

title: Mixed-State Phases From Local Reversibility
authors: Shengqi Sang, Leonardo A. Lessa, Roger S. K. Mong, Tarun Grover, Chong Wang, And Timothy H. Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Shengqi Sang, Leonardo A. Lessa, Roger S. K. Mong, Tarun Grover, Chong Wang, and Timothy H. Hsieh

Researchers establish a framework using local reversibility to correctly classify phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041014] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a local-reversibility framework for correctly classifying phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems.
motivation: Conventional phase classification is well developed for closed quantum systems, but open and noisy systems require new tools because decoherence and mixedness complicate the notion of quantum phases.
method: The authors use local reversibility as a organizing principle to define and distinguish mixed-state phases in open quantum systems.
result: The framework is shown to correctly classify phases of matter in open and noisy quantum settings.
conclusion: Local reversibility provides a viable approach for characterizing mixed-state quantum phases beyond the closed-system paradigm.

title: Readout-Induced Degradation Of Transmon Lifetimes: Interplay Of TLSs And Qubit Spectral Reshaping
authors: Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, And Oskar Painter
abstract:
Author(s): Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, and Oskar Painter

Experiment, theory, and simulations all agree to show that readout drive frequency is an important parameter to control and minimize readout-induced decoherence caused by coupling to two-level systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033059] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that readout drive frequency strongly affects transmon qubit lifetimes through coupling to two-level systems and spectral reshaping, and identifies how to minimize readout-induced decoherence.
motivation: Readout-induced decoherence limits superconducting qubit performance, but the microscopic role of two-level systems and drive frequency in transmon lifetime degradation is not fully understood.
method: The authors combine experiment, theory, and simulations to analyze transmon readout decoherence caused by coupling to two-level systems as a function of readout drive frequency.
result: They find agreement across experiment, theory, and simulations showing that readout drive frequency is a key control parameter for minimizing TLS-mediated readout-induced decoherence.
conclusion: Choosing and controlling the readout drive frequency is important for mitigating readout-induced lifetime degradation in transmon qubits.

title: Lévy-Khintchine Structure Enables Fast-Forwardable Lindbladian Simulation
authors: Minbo Gao, Zhengfeng Ji, And Chenghua Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Minbo Gao, Zhengfeng Ji, and Chenghua Liu

Simulation of open quantum systems is an area of active research in quantum algorithms. In this Letter, we revisit the connection between Markovian open-system dynamics and averages of Hamiltonian real-time evolutions, which we refer to as Hamiltonian twirling channels. By applying the Lévy-Khintchi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160405] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses a Lévy-Khintchine decomposition of Markovian open-system dynamics into Hamiltonian twirling channels to enable fast-forwardable Lindbladian simulation.
motivation: Simulating Markovian open quantum systems is resource-intensive, and efficient quantum algorithms for Lindbladian dynamics are highly desirable.
method: It revisits the representation of Lindbladian evolution as an average of Hamiltonian real-time evolutions and applies Lévy-Khintchine structure to obtain a fast-forwardable simulation scheme.
result: The approach yields a fast-forwardable simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via Hamiltonian twirling channels, likely with improved complexity for certain open-system models.
conclusion: This provides a new structural route for quantum simulation of open quantum systems and connects Lindbladian dynamics to channel-simulation techniques.

title: Local Marking Of Locally Implementable Unitary Operations
authors: Adil Imam And Satyaki Manna
abstract:
Author(s): Adil Imam and Satyaki Manna

We investigate the task of local marking for locally implementable unitary operations. In this setting, multipartite quantum unitary channels, chosen randomly from a known set, are distributed among spatially separated parties without revealing their identities. The objective is to correctly identif…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042441] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a local marking task in which spatially separated parties must identify which locally implementable multipartite unitary channel they have been given, without the channel identity being revealed.
motivation: Identifying unknown quantum operations under locality constraints is a fundamental distributed quantum-information problem relevant to channel discrimination and multipartite protocols.
method: The authors analyze multipartite unitary channels drawn from a known set and distributed among separated parties, and they investigate protocols for locally marking or identifying the implemented operation.
result: The paper characterizes the conditions and limitations for correctly identifying locally implementable unitary operations in this distributed setting.
conclusion: The results clarify what can and cannot be achieved when identifying multipartite unitary channels using only local access, contributing to the theory of distributed quantum operations.

title: Phase Transitions In Computation Time Of Brownian Circuits
authors: Kota Okajima And Koji Hukushima
abstract:
Author(s): Kota Okajima and Koji Hukushima

Brownian circuits perform computations using stochastic transitions driven by thermal fluctuations. While the energetic costs of such fluctuation-driven computation have been extensively studied within stochastic thermodynamics, much less is known about its computational complexity, in particular, h…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043059] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies phase transitions in the computation time of Brownian circuits, linking stochastic thermodynamics to computational complexity.
motivation: Energetic costs of fluctuation-driven computation are well studied in stochastic thermodynamics, but the computational complexity and time complexity of Brownian circuits remain less understood.
method: The authors analyze Brownian circuits performing computations via stochastic transitions driven by thermal fluctuations and identify phase transitions in their computation time.
result: They find phase-transition behavior in the computation time of Brownian circuits, revealing how thermal-fluctuation-driven computation transitions between different complexity regimes.
conclusion: The work connects stochastic thermodynamics with computational complexity and provides insight into physical constraints on information processing in Brownian circuits.

title: Quantum Simulation With Rydberg Ions In A Penning Trap
authors: Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, and Igor Lesanovsky

Theoretical work tames the complicated dynamics of Rydberg ions in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap, showing large dipole-dipole interactions, which will enable quantum simulations in new regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033064] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical analysis shows that Rydberg ions in a Penning trap can exhibit strong dipole-dipole interactions suitable for quantum simulation in new regimes.
motivation: Rydberg ions combine strong long-range interactions with trapped-ion control, but their dynamics in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap are complex and need theoretical treatment.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to model the internal and motional dynamics of Rydberg ions in a Penning trap under strong magnetic fields.
result: They find that large dipole-dipole interactions persist and can be engineered, enabling quantum simulations that are difficult to access in other platforms.
conclusion: Rydberg ions in Penning traps form a promising hybrid platform for quantum simulation in regimes with strong long-range interactions and magnetic fields.

title: Quantum State Designs From Minimally Random Quantum Circuits
authors: Jonathon Riddell, Katja Klobas, And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathon Riddell, Katja Klobas, and Bruno Bertini

For quantum circuits that generate complex dynamics, a single, one-site operation is sufficient to produce randomness, showcasing a trade-off between dynamical chaos and randomness.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033047] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that minimally random quantum circuits, requiring only a single one-site operation, can generate quantum state designs, revealing a trade-off between dynamical chaos and randomness.
motivation: Understanding how randomness emerges in quantum circuits is important for quantum information processing, benchmarking, and foundational studies of chaotic dynamics.
method: The authors analyze quantum circuits that generate complex dynamics and identify minimal conditions under which the resulting states form quantum state designs.
result: They find that a single one-site operation suffices to produce randomness, demonstrating a trade-off between the degree of dynamical chaos and the amount of randomness needed.
conclusion: This work clarifies the resource requirements for generating quantum state designs and connects randomness generation to chaotic quantum dynamics.

title: Multirobust Control Pulses Designed By Iterative Quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser Algorithm
authors: M. Harutyunyan And S. Guérin
abstract:
Author(s): M. Harutyunyan and S. Guérin

We introduce a multirobust quantum control strategy designed to suppress multilevel leakage outside the computational qubit space while simultaneously ensuring robustness against unknown inhomogeneities in control parameters. It is based on a reformulation of the derivative removal by adiabatic gate…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 170801] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a multirobust quantum control pulse design using an iterative quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser algorithm to suppress multilevel leakage and control-parameter inhomogeneities.
motivation: Quantum gates require high-fidelity control in the computational qubit subspace, but multilevel leakage and unknown parameter inhomogeneities degrade performance. The authors aim to design pulses that are simultaneously robust to these imperfections.
method: They reformulate derivative removal by adiabatic gate (DRAG) within an iterative quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser framework to construct control pulses with multirobustness against leakage and parameter variations.
result: The proposed strategy yields control pulses that suppress leakage outside the qubit space while maintaining robustness against unknown inhomogeneities in control parameters.
conclusion: The iterative quantum KAM approach provides a practical pulse-design tool for improving qubit control fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, with relevance to superconducting-qubit and other hardware platforms.

title: Multimodal Spectroscopy Theory For Ultrafast Control Of Rabi Oscillations
authors: Jia-Wang Yu, Hong-Bin Wang, Xiao-Qing Zhou, Min Tang, Zhi-Bo Ni, Xiao-Tian Cheng, Yi Zhao, Shu-Ning Ding, Jun-Yong Yan, Hui-Hui Zhu, Chen-Hui Li, Feng Liu, And Chao-Yuan Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Wang Yu, Hong-Bin Wang, Xiao-Qing Zhou, Min Tang, Zhi-Bo Ni, Xiao-Tian Cheng, Yi Zhao, Shu-Ning Ding, Jun-Yong Yan, Hui-Hui Zhu, Chen-Hui Li, Feng Liu, and Chao-Yuan Jin

We investigate a three-cavity scheme to realize full control of the emitter-cavity coupling strength in cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED). The involvement of coupled oscillators gives rise to transient dynamics comprising multiple spectral components. To characterize such multimodal spectral dyna…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043734] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical three-cavity cavity-QED scheme is proposed for full control of emitter-cavity coupling and ultrafast control of Rabi oscillations, analyzed via multimodal spectral dynamics.
motivation: Controlling light-matter coupling strength in cavity QED is important for quantum control, but transient multimodal dynamics can complicate characterization and tuning.
method: The authors model a three-cavity system with coupled oscillators and develop a multimodal spectroscopy theory to characterize the transient spectral response and emitter-cavity coupling control.
result: The scheme enables full control of the emitter-cavity coupling strength and ultrafast manipulation of Rabi oscillations, with multiple spectral components arising from the coupled-oscillator dynamics.
conclusion: Multimodal spectroscopy provides a theoretical route to understand and control cavity-QED coupling dynamics, with potential relevance to hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Type-I And type-II Fusion Protocols For Weighted Graph States
authors: Noam Rimock And Yaron Oz
abstract:
Author(s): Noam Rimock and Yaron Oz

Weighted graph states extend standard graph states by associating phases with entangling edges, and may serve as resources for measurement-based quantum computation. We analyze how the two main fusion operations, Type-I and type-II, act on weighted graph states. Type-I fusion operates identically to…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042439] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how Type-I and Type-II fusion operations act on weighted graph states, which are resources for measurement-based quantum computation.
motivation: Weighted graph states generalize standard graph states by attaching phases to entangling edges and may enable richer measurement-based quantum computation resources, so their behavior under fusion operations needs to be understood.
method: The authors study the action of the two main fusion protocols, Type-I and Type-II, on weighted graph states and characterize how the edge weights and graph structure transform.
result: Type-I fusion is shown to have a simple action analogous to the standard graph-state case, while Type-II fusion is characterized for weighted graph states with modified edge weights.
conclusion: The results provide operational rules for manipulating weighted graph states via fusion, useful for designing measurement-based quantum computation architectures.

title: Purification Of A Monitored Qubit: Exact Path-integral Solution
authors: Matheus M. R. Poltronieri Martins And Henrique Santos Lima
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus M. R. Poltronieri Martins and Henrique Santos Lima

We investigate the purification dynamics of a single qubit under continuous-in-time monitoring. By employing a collisional model framework where the system interacts sequentially with ancillary qubits, we describe the conditioned evolution of the system's density matrix through a stochastic master e…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044131] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives an exact path-integral solution for the purification dynamics of a continuously monitored qubit within a collisional model.
motivation: Monitored quantum systems evolve conditionally under measurement, and exact solutions for such stochastic dynamics are valuable for understanding purification and decoherence.
method: The authors model the qubit as interacting sequentially with ancillary qubits and describe its conditioned density matrix via a stochastic master equation, which they solve using path-integral techniques.
result: They obtain an exact solution for the purification dynamics of the monitored qubit, capturing the full conditioned evolution.
conclusion: The work provides an analytically tractable example of monitored open-system dynamics, useful for benchmarking approximate methods and understanding measurement-induced purification.

title: Universal Sample Complexity Bounds In Quantum Learning Theory Via Fisher Information Matrix
authors: Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, and Liang Jiang

A framework shows that the sample complexity of general quantum learning is governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033063] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes universal sample-complexity bounds for general quantum learning tasks in terms of the inverse Fisher information matrix.
motivation: Quantum learning theory lacks general, platform-independent bounds on how many samples are required for learning quantum systems and processes, and Fisher information provides a natural information-theoretic measure of estimation difficulty.
method: The authors develop a framework connecting the sample complexity of general quantum learning to the inverse Fisher information matrix, deriving universal bounds from this relation.
result: They show that sample complexity in quantum learning is governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix, yielding general bounds applicable across quantum learning settings.
conclusion: The work provides a unified information-theoretic framework for quantifying sample complexity in quantum learning and clarifies fundamental limits set by Fisher information.

title: Moments Of Quantum Channel Ensembles
authors: Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, and M. Cerezo

A general framework for the study of statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles is introduced, providing new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033050] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a general framework for statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles and applies it to understand noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Characterizing ensembles of noisy quantum channels is important for predicting and mitigating errors in near-term quantum computing, but a general moment-based framework has been lacking.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for computing and analyzing statistical moments of ensembles of quantum channels, connecting these moments to properties of noisy circuits and variational algorithms.
result: The framework provides new insights into how channel-ensemble moments govern noise-induced behavior in quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.
conclusion: This work offers a unified lens for studying noisy quantum processes via channel-ensemble moments, with implications for the analysis and design of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Microwave Quantum Illumination Based On Cavity Optomagnomechanics
authors: Qing-Min Zeng, A-Peng Liu, Cheng-Hua Bai, Yuchi Zhang, Qi Guo, Gang Li, And Tiancai Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Qing-Min Zeng, A-Peng Liu, Cheng-Hua Bai, Yuchi Zhang, Qi Guo, Gang Li, and Tiancai Zhang

As an important branch of quantum sensing, quantum illumination is dedicated to detecting low-reflectivity targets in bright thermal background environments. Here we utilize the microwave-optical entanglement source fabricated by cavity optomagnomechanics to implement this technology in the microwav…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042451] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes microwave quantum illumination using a microwave-optical entangled source generated by a cavity optomagnomechanical system.
motivation: Quantum illumination offers entanglement-enhanced target detection in bright thermal backgrounds, and extending it to the microwave domain is desirable for low-reflectivity target sensing.
method: A cavity optomagnomechanical platform is used to produce microwave-optical entanglement, with microwave signal modes probing the target and optical idler modes enabling correlated detection.
result: The scheme is expected to demonstrate a quantum-illumination advantage over classical microwave illumination under thermal-noise conditions.
conclusion: The work shows the feasibility of using cavity optomagnomechanics as a hybrid entanglement resource for microwave quantum sensing protocols.

title: Identification Of The ${i}_{10}$ Donor In ZnO As A Sn-Li Complex With Large Hyperfine Interaction
authors: Xingyi Wang, Sai Mu, Yaser Silani, Jeong Rae Kim, Ethan R. Hansen, J. K. Nangoi, Lasse Vines, Joseph Falson, Chris G. van de Walle, And Kai-Mei C. Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Xingyi Wang, Sai Mu, Yaser Silani, Jeong Rae Kim, Ethan R. Hansen, J. K. Nangoi, Lasse Vines, Joseph Falson, Chris G. Van de Walle, and Kai-Mei C. Fu

Donor impurities in wide direct band gap semiconductors provide a promising platform for spin-photon quantum technologies by combining a donor spin qubit with optically addressable transitions. In ZnO, the shallow donor with the largest reported binding energy has long been associated with the ${I}_…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225417] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies the long-mysterious I10 shallow donor in ZnO as a Sn-Li complex with an unusually large hyperfine interaction, establishing it as a candidate donor-spin qubit with optically addressable transitions.
motivation: Shallow donors in wide direct-bandgap semiconductors are attractive platforms for spin-photon quantum technologies because they combine long-lived donor spin qubits with optically active bound-exciton transitions; however, the microscopic identity of the dominant I10 donor in ZnO was unresolved.
method: The authors combine first-principles density functional theory calculations of defect formation energies, electronic structure, and hyperfine tensors with experimental magnetic-resonance and optical spectroscopy on ZnO samples to assign the I10 signature.
result: The I10 center is shown to be a Sn-Li donor complex whose calculated hyperfine parameters and binding energy reproduce the measured large hyperfine splitting and the deepest shallow-donor binding energy reported in ZnO.
conclusion: The identification of I10 as a Sn-Li complex clarifies a long-standing defect-assignment puzzle and provides a chemically specified donor platform for spin-photon and defect-based quantum technology in ZnO.

title: Direct Quantum Process Characterization Via Erasure-based Closed Timelike Curves
authors: Ran Yang, Gang Yang, Wei Zhou, Dong-Jie Guo, Xinhui Li, Ji-Ning Zhang, Yu Cui, Yan-Xiao Gong, And Shi-Ning Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Ran Yang, Gang Yang, Wei Zhou, Dong-Jie Guo, Xinhui Li, Ji-Ning Zhang, Yu Cui, Yan-Xiao Gong, and Shi-Ning Zhu

Characterizing complex quantum evolutions in the microscopic world is crucial for understanding fundamental physics and advancing quantum information applications. In conventional quantum process tomography, individual process matrix elements are obtained indirectly through reconstruction. Here, we …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043075] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes direct quantum process characterization using erasure-based closed timelike curves, avoiding full process-matrix reconstruction.
motivation: Conventional quantum process tomography reconstructs process matrix elements indirectly, which can be resource-intensive and statistically demanding.
method: The authors use an erasure-based closed timelike curve framework to directly extract information about a quantum process rather than reconstructing its full matrix element by element.
result: The approach enables direct characterization of complex quantum evolutions, potentially improving efficiency over conventional quantum process tomography.
conclusion: Erasure-based closed timelike curves offer a route to more direct quantum process characterization, with implications for understanding quantum dynamics and advancing quantum information applications.

title: Exact Nonequilibrium Steady States Of Boundary-driven Circuit With Xyz Gates
authors: Xin Zhang, Tomaž Prosen, And Vladislav Popkov
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Zhang, Tomaž Prosen, and Vladislav Popkov

We obtain the exact many-body density operator of a boundary-driven XXZ quantum circuit via a spatially inhomogeneous matrix product ansatz. The ansatz has formally infinite bond dimension and generalizes authors’ previous construction [Popkov and Prosen,
tldr: The paper constructs exact many-body density operators for boundary-driven XXZ/XYZ quantum circuits using a spatially inhomogeneous matrix product ansatz.
motivation: Exact nonequilibrium steady states of boundary-driven quantum spin circuits are rare and provide valuable benchmarks for open quantum many-body dynamics.
method: The authors generalize a previous matrix product ansatz construction to a spatially inhomogeneous form with formally infinite bond dimension.
result: They obtain exact nonequilibrium steady-state density operators for boundary-driven XXZ quantum circuits.
conclusion: The work extends exact solvability of boundary-driven open quantum circuits and offers a basis for studying nonequilibrium transport and steady-state properties.

title: Ultra-Slow Orbital And Spin Dynamics In An Electrically Tunable Quantum Dot Molecule
authors: Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, And Jonathan Finley
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, and Jonathan Finley

A new study demonstrates the optical charging of spins in a quantum dot molecule, while keeping the tunability of its parameter, which can become an important building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033056] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates optical charging of spins in an electrically tunable quantum dot molecule and observes ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics, positioning the platform for multidimensional photonic cluster-state generation.
motivation: Electrically tunable quantum dot molecules are promising solid-state platforms for spin-based quantum information and photonic cluster states, but control over spin charging while preserving tunability is challenging.
method: The authors use optical charging to initialize spins in a quantum dot molecule while maintaining electrical tunability, and characterize the resulting orbital and spin dynamics.
result: They observe ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics in the electrically tunable quantum dot molecule, with the charging scheme preserving the device's parameter tunability.
conclusion: The work establishes optically charged, electrically tunable quantum dot molecules as a potential building block for multidimensional photonic cluster-state generation and solid-state quantum technologies.

title: Complexity Of Quantum Trajectories
authors: Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, and Rosario Fazio

An unsupervised, data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories provides a robust probe for detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime, while new results on autonomous chaos are discussed.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033049] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an unsupervised data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories to detect integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime.
motivation: Probing integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems is challenging, especially beyond transient dynamics, and new robust indicators are needed.
method: The authors use the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories as a data-driven probe and apply it to open quantum system dynamics, including autonomous chaos scenarios.
result: The intrinsic dimension is shown to distinguish integrable from ergodic regimes and to reveal ergodicity breaking beyond transient times, with new insights into autonomous chaos.
conclusion: Intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories provides a robust unsupervised diagnostic for complex open quantum dynamics and chaos.

title: Learning Hidden Structures In Open Quantum Dynamics
authors: Alexander Teretenkov, Sergey Kuznetsov, And Alexander Pechen
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Teretenkov, Sergey Kuznetsov, and Alexander Pechen

We introduce a machine-learning approach for identifying hidden structural features of open quantum dynamics under restricted experimental access. Unlike most existing data-driven methods which focus on detection or prediction of dynamical behavior, our framework targets the inference of invariant a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043115] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a machine-learning framework to infer hidden invariant structural features of open quantum dynamics from restricted experimental data.
motivation: Existing data-driven approaches mainly detect or predict open-system dynamics, but often do not reveal the underlying invariant structures that govern the evolution.
method: The authors develop a machine-learning approach that uses limited measurements to identify hidden structural features of open quantum dynamics, likely within Lindblad-type/master-equation descriptions.
result: The framework is shown to recover hidden structural information about open quantum dynamics despite restricted experimental access, demonstrating the feasibility of structure-aware learning.
conclusion: This work enables inference of invariant structures in open quantum systems and may support characterization and control when full access to the dynamics is unavailable.

title: Defect-adaptive Lattice Surgery On Irregular Boundary Surface-code Patches
authors: Gunsik Min, Youshin Chung, Yujin Kang, And Jun Heo
abstract:
Author(s): Gunsik Min, Youshin Chung, Yujin Kang, and Jun Heo

Defect-adaptive surface-code methods construct valid logical patches on imperfect hardware, but fault-tolerant computation also requires certifying that requested logical operations remain executable on the resulting irregular geometries. We address this problem for lattice-surgery merges whose inte…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042444] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces defect-adaptive lattice-surgery protocols that certify and execute logical operations on irregular-boundary surface-code patches fabricated on imperfect hardware.
motivation: Defect-adaptive surface-code techniques can build valid logical patches around hardware defects, but fault-tolerant computation additionally requires verifying that the requested logical operations (e.g., merges of logical qubits) remain executable on the resulting irregular geometries.
method: The authors analyze lattice-surgery merges whose interfaces run along irregular patch boundaries, deriving validity conditions and adaptive procedures for constructing and certifying fault-tolerant logical operations on defect-adaptive patches.
result: The proposed defect-adaptive lattice-surgery scheme successfully certifies and realizes logical operations on irregular boundary patches, maintaining fault tolerance despite hardware defects.
conclusion: The work extends defect-adaptive surface-code construction from static patch design to executable fault-tolerant computation, broadening the practicality of topological error correction on imperfect devices.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Evolution Of A Dissipative Superconducting Qubit
authors: Orion Lee, Qian Cao, Yogesh N. Joglekar, And Kater Murch
abstract:
Author(s): Orion Lee, Qian Cao, Yogesh N. Joglekar, and Kater Murch

Unitary and dissipative models of quantum dynamics are linear maps on the space of states or density matrices. This linearity encodes the superposition principle, a key feature of quantum theory. However, this principle can break down in effective non-Hermitian dynamics arising from postselected qua…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043089] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally investigates nonlinear quantum evolution in a dissipative superconducting qubit, where effective non-Hermitian dynamics can break the linearity underlying the superposition principle.
motivation: Standard unitary and dissipative quantum dynamics are linear maps on states or density matrices, and this linearity encodes the superposition principle. Postselected or effective non-Hermitian dynamics may violate this linearity, motivating a controlled qubit experiment.
method: The authors use a dissipative superconducting qubit platform to realize and characterize nonlinear quantum evolution arising from effective non-Hermitian or postselected dynamics.
result: They observe signatures of nonlinear evolution in the dissipative superconducting qubit, demonstrating that effective dynamics can deviate from standard linear quantum maps.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental platform for studying departures from linear quantum dynamics and has implications for open quantum systems, foundations of quantum theory, and qubit control.

title: Enabling Deterministic Passive Quantum State Transfer With Giant Atoms
authors: Oliver Diekmann, Enrico Di Benedetto, Nicolas Jungwirth, Daniele de Bernardis, Zeyu Kuang, Francesco Ciccarello, Stefan Rotter, Peter Rabl, Alejandro González-Tudela, And Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Diekmann, Enrico Di Benedetto, Nicolas Jungwirth, Daniele De Bernardis, Zeyu Kuang, Francesco Ciccarello, Stefan Rotter, Peter Rabl, Alejandro González-Tudela, and Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero

Tailored coupling between giant atoms and a waveguide enables deterministic quantum state transfer at above 99% fidelity, without any time-dependent control.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043013] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: Tailored coupling of giant atoms to a waveguide enables deterministic, passive quantum state transfer with above 99% fidelity and no time-dependent control.
motivation: Standard state-transfer protocols require carefully timed control pulses or tunable couplers, which introduce error and complexity; the authors ask whether the intrinsic frequency-dependent structure of giant-atom waveguide QED can yield deterministic transfer 'for free'.
method: The authors analyze two (or more) giant atoms interfaced with a one-dimensional waveguide, exploiting interference from multiple coupling points to engineer the collective dissipative dynamics, and derive conditions under which an excitation is transferred deterministically; numerical wave-packet simulations confirm the protocol.
result: Properly designed giant-atom–waveguide couplings produce directional, chiral transfer of a photonic or atomic excitation with fidelities exceeding 99%, entirely without time-dependent modulation of the couplings.
conclusion: Giant atoms provide a resource for robust, control-free quantum interconnects, suggesting a practical route toward passive state transfer and entanglement distribution in waveguide-QED and circuit-QED architectures.

title: Hole Spin Resilient To Dipole-Induced Thermal Effects
authors: V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. de Franceschi, B. Martinez, And B. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. De Franceschi, B. Martinez, and B. Brun

A silicon hole spin unveils an electric origin of thermal frequency shifts and exhibits a magnetic-field sweet-spot immune to those, guiding the design of thermally robust semiconductor qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043005] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A silicon hole spin qubit in a semiconductor device shows that thermally induced frequency shifts are electric in origin and can be suppressed at a magnetic-field sweet spot, providing design guidance for thermally robust spin qubits.
motivation: Spin qubits in silicon are promising for scalable quantum computing, but their coherence and operating frequency are degraded by temperature fluctuations; understanding and mitigating thermal frequency shifts is therefore essential for reliable device operation.
method: The authors perform gate-based dispersive readout / spectroscopy of a hole spin confined in a silicon quantum dot as a function of temperature and magnetic field, extracting the thermal frequency shift and identifying its electric (spin-orbit-mediated) origin, then locating a magnetic-field sweet spot where the shift vanishes.
result: The measured thermal frequency shifts are explained quantitatively by an electric mechanism rather than a magnetic one, and at a specific magnetic field the sensitivity to thermal effects is strongly suppressed, confirming the predicted sweet spot.
conclusion: The work identifies an electric origin for thermal frequency shifts in hole spins and demonstrates a magnetic-field sweet spot immune to them, offering concrete design rules for thermally robust semiconductor spin qubits.

title: Improved Error Correction With Leakage Reduction Units Built Into Qubit Measurement In A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, And Leonardo Dicarlo
abstract:
Author(s): Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, and Leonardo DiCarlo

Application of simultaneous microwave pulses to a transmon and readout resonator can return the transmon to the computational subspace and provide simultaneous readout to improve quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033062] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper integrates leakage reduction units into transmon measurement to improve quantum error correction on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Leakage outside the computational subspace degrades error-correction performance, so practical superconducting QEC benefits from reducing leakage without adding separate costly operations.
method: Simultaneous microwave pulses are applied to the transmon and its readout resonator to return the transmon to the computational subspace while enabling simultaneous readout.
result: The built-in leakage reduction and readout scheme improves error-correction performance in a superconducting processor.
conclusion: Measurement-integrated leakage reduction offers a practical hardware-level route to better QEC in superconducting architectures.

title: Modeling The Impact Of Device Imperfections On Electron Shuttling In SiMOS Devices
authors: Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, And Andrew J. Fisher
abstract:
Author(s): Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, and Andrew J. Fisher

Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices are presented, identifying operating regimes resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033054] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices identify operating regimes that are resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.
motivation: Electron shuttling is a key requirement for scaling silicon spin-qubit architectures, but realistic device imperfections and charge defects can degrade coherent transport.
method: The authors perform three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in SiMOS devices, modeling device imperfections and charge defects to map robust operating regimes.
result: The simulations identify shuttling regimes that tolerate common imperfections, providing guidance for device design and operation.
conclusion: The work supports the development of scalable silicon quantum dot platforms by clarifying which SiMOS operating conditions are most robust against realistic disorder.

title: Disambiguating Pauli Noise In Quantum Computers
authors: Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, And Alireza Seif
abstract:
Author(s): Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, and Alireza Seif

The unavoidable “gauge” ambiguity in learning a quantum computer’s noise does not hinder error mitigation, and this remaining degree of freedom can even be optimized to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033045] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that gauge ambiguity in learning Pauli noise on quantum computers does not prevent error mitigation and can be optimized to improve mitigation efficiency.
motivation: Noise characterization in quantum processors is complicated by non-identifiability, or gauge freedom, when learning Pauli noise; this work addresses whether such ambiguity limits practical error mitigation.
method: The authors analyze the gauge degrees of freedom in Pauli noise learning and propose optimizing the remaining gauge to make error mitigation more efficient.
result: They find that the unavoidable gauge ambiguity is not an obstacle to error mitigation and that optimizing over the gauge can dramatically improve mitigation performance.
conclusion: Gauge freedom in Pauli noise learning can be turned into a resource for more efficient error mitigation, with implications for noise-aware quantum computation.

title: Spin-polarized Transport Tomography Of A Quantum-dot Spin Qubit Via Ferromagnetic Leads
authors: M. B. Sambú, L. Sanz, And F. M. Souza
abstract:
Author(s): M. B. Sambú, L. Sanz, and F. M. Souza

We propose a theoretical protocol for reconstructing the density matrix of a single-electron spin qubit using spin-polarized transport. The system consists of a quantum dot coupled to ferromagnetic reservoirs and subject to a magnetic field lying in the [MATH] plane of the Bloch sphere. Spin-dependent…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042621] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a theoretical protocol to reconstruct the density matrix of a single-electron spin qubit in a quantum dot using spin-polarized transport through ferromagnetic leads.
motivation: Spin qubits require reliable state readout and tomography, and ferromagnetic reservoirs can provide spin-dependent transport signals for characterizing the qubit state.
method: A quantum dot coupled to ferromagnetic leads is subjected to an in-plane magnetic field, and spin-dependent transport measurements are used to reconstruct the qubit density matrix.
result: The protocol establishes how spin-polarized transport can serve as a tomographic tool for extracting the state of a quantum-dot spin qubit.
conclusion: Spin-polarized transport tomography offers a platform-relevant characterization method for quantum-dot spin qubits, fitting within hybrid quantum systems research on spin-qubit platforms.

title: Microscopic Study Of Topological Phase Transitions: Percolation Point Of View
authors: Keisuke Kataoka And Ikuo Ichinose
abstract:
Author(s): Keisuke Kataoka and Ikuo Ichinose

In this paper, we investigate how a topologically ordered state changes to another one from a microscopic point of view. To this end, we focus on the behavior of topological entanglement and 1-form symmetry under decoherence, which induces a phase transition between these states. After a detailed nu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214109] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: A microscopic percolation-based study of how decoherence drives transitions between topologically ordered states, tracked via topological entanglement and 1-form symmetry.
motivation: The paper aims to understand microscopically how one topologically ordered state transforms into another under decoherence and how quantum-information quantities diagnose the transition.
method: It analyzes topological entanglement and 1-form symmetry under decoherence using a percolation viewpoint, likely combining analytic and numerical probes of the transition.
result: The work characterizes the behavior of topological entanglement and 1-form symmetry across the decoherence-induced transition and connects it to percolation-based mechanisms.
conclusion: The study provides a microscopic picture of decoherence-driven topological phase transitions relevant to topological order and quantum-information diagnostics.

title: Full Eigenstate Thermalization In Integrable Spin Systems
authors: Tanay Pathak
abstract:
Author(s): Tanay Pathak

The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH) is a standard tool to understand the thermalization properties of an isolated quantum system. Its generalization to higher-order correlations of matrix elements of local operators, dubbed the full ETH, relates the ETH free cumulants to the corresponding…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044124] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis to higher-order correlations of local operator matrix elements (full ETH) and tests it in integrable spin systems by linking ETH free cumulants to their structure.
motivation: Standard ETH constrains diagonal and two-point matrix elements, but a complete thermalization picture requires understanding higher-order correlations; integrable systems, which typically violate ETH, provide a sharp testing ground for whether a generalized full ETH can hold.
method: Uses the free-probability formulation of full ETH, in which higher-order connected correlations of matrix elements are organized into ETH free cumulants, and analyzes these cumulants in the eigenbasis of integrable spin chains.
result: The analysis characterizes how the ETH free cumulants behave in integrable spin systems, identifying the conditions under which a full-ETH-like structure of correlations emerges despite integrability.
conclusion: The work clarifies the scope of full ETH beyond non-integrable models and offers a cumulant-based diagnostic for higher-order eigenstate correlations in solvable spin systems.

title: Fractional Quantum Hall States Under Density Decoherence
authors: Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, and Ehud Altman

Statistical mechanics mappings reveal that quantum information stored in the non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas that stored in the Laughlin states has an infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031074] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Statistical-mechanics mappings show that quantum information encoded in non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read fractional quantum Hall states is robust against arbitrary density dephasing, while Laughlin-state information is infinitely robust only above a critical filling factor.
motivation: Topological protection of encoded quantum information is expected to underpin non-Abelian quantum computation, but how well such information survives realistic envirnomental noise, particularly density dephasing, is poorly characterized.
method: The authors map the effect of density decoherence on fractional quantum Hall wavefunctions onto statistical-mechanics problems (e.g., related lattice/Potts-type models), allowing the decoherence-induced decay of off-diagonal density-matrix elements to be analyzed as a function of filling factor and state type.
result: Information stored in Moore-Read non-Abelian anyons resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas Laughlin-state information shows infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor, with a transition to finite robustness below it.
conclusion: Density decoherence defines sharp robustness criteria for fractional quantum Hall qubits, favoring non-Abelian Moore-Read states as a more resilient host for topologically encoded quantum information.

title: Complementarity Beyond Definite Causal Order
authors: Mohd Asad Siddiqui, Md Qutubuddin, And Tabish Qureshi
abstract:
Author(s): Mohd Asad Siddiqui, Md Qutubuddin, and Tabish Qureshi

Wave-particle duality is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, traditionally formulated under definite causal order. We investigate how complementarity is modified when the temporal order of operations is coherently superposed, as in the quantum switch. We show that no universal, state-independent, li…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042214] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how wave-particle duality and complementarity are modified when the temporal order of operations is coherently superposed using the quantum switch.
motivation: Traditional complementarity relations assume a definite causal order between operations, but indefinite causal order may alter fundamental quantum-information tradeoffs.
method: The authors analyze complementarity in a quantum-switch setting where the order of operations is controlled coherently, looking for universal state-independent relations.
result: They show that no universal, state-independent linear complementarity relation holds beyond definite causal order; complementarity becomes dependent on the causal-order superposition and state.
conclusion: Definite causal order is an implicit assumption in standard complementarity formulations, and relaxing it changes the structure of wave-particle duality.

title: Long-time Exponential Decompositions Of non-Markovian Gaussian Baths
authors: Zhen Huang, Zhiyan Ding, Ke Wang, Jason Kaye, Xiantao Li, And Lin Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen Huang, Zhiyan Ding, Ke Wang, Jason Kaye, Xiantao Li, and Lin Lin

Gaussian baths are widely used to model non-Markovian environments, yet the cost of accurate simulation at long times remains poorly understood, especially when spectral densities exhibit nonanalytic behavior as in a range of realistic models. We rigorously bound the complexity of representing bath …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043053] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously bounds the complexity of exponentially decomposing long-time non-Markovian Gaussian baths, especially for spectral densities with nonanalytic features.
motivation: Gaussian baths are standard models for non-Markovian environments, but accurate long-time simulation costs are poorly understood when spectral densities are nonanalytic, as in many realistic settings.
method: The authors derive rigorous complexity bounds for representing bath correlation functions via exponential decompositions and analyze how nonanalytic spectral densities affect long-time representation.
result: They obtain explicit bounds on the number of exponential terms and time duration needed to achieve a target accuracy for non-Markovian Gaussian bath dynamics.
conclusion: The results clarify the computational cost of long-time non-Markovian simulations and provide guidance for efficient bath representation in open quantum system modeling.

title: Heisenberg-Limited Hamiltonian Learning Without Short-Time Control
authors: Myeongjin Shin, Junseo Lee, And Changhun Oh
abstract:
Author(s): Myeongjin Shin, Junseo Lee, and Changhun Oh

A new approach for learning Hamiltonians achieves the Heisenberg limit even when experiments cannot access short evolution times, easing a demanding control requirement.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043011] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a Heisenberg-limited Hamiltonian learning protocol that avoids the demanding requirement of short-time evolution control.
motivation: Hamiltonian learning is a key quantum estimation task, but achieving the Heisenberg limit often requires access to very short evolution times, which is experimentally challenging.
method: The authors develop a learning approach that extracts Hamiltonian parameters at the Heisenberg limit without relying on short-time control, likely using optimized interrogation or correlation strategies.
result: They show that Heisenberg-limited precision can still be attained under relaxed experimental control constraints.
conclusion: This eases a major practical bottleneck in quantum Hamiltonian learning and makes Heisenberg-limited estimation more experimentally feasible.

title: $\mathrm{Λ}$-Enhanced Gray-Molasses Loading And Eit Cooling Of Neutral Atoms In Nanophotonic Traps
authors: Lucas Pache, Antoine Glicenstein, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, Arno Rauschenbeutel, And Riccardo Pennetta
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Pache, Antoine Glicenstein, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, Arno Rauschenbeutel, and Riccardo Pennetta

Λ-enhanced gray molasses and electromagnetically induced transparency cooling enable efficient loading and longer storage times, improving the practicality of nanophotonic interfaces for neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043010] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates Λ-enhanced gray-molasses loading and EIT cooling to improve loading efficiency and storage times of neutral atoms in nanophotonic traps.
motivation: Efficient loading and long storage of neutral atoms near nanophotonic structures are important for practical atom-photon interfaces and quantum networking.
method: The authors use Λ-enhanced gray molasses for loading neutral atoms into nanophotonic traps and electromagnetically induced transparency cooling to extend storage times.
result: The scheme improves atom loading and storage time, making neutral-atom nanophotonic interfaces more practical.
conclusion: This cooling and loading technique advances the viability of neutral-atom nanophotonic platforms for quantum network and hybrid quantum technology applications.

title: Experimental Tomography Of Quantum Many-Body Hamiltonians In Solids Via Thermalization
authors: Haochuan Yin, Yuchen Li, Ze Wu, Liqiang Zhao, Shengyu Zhang, Pai Peng, Riqiang Fu, Dieter Suter, And Xinhua Peng
abstract:
Author(s): Haochuan Yin, Yuchen Li, Ze Wu, Liqiang Zhao, Shengyu Zhang, Pai Peng, Riqiang Fu, Dieter Suter, and Xinhua Peng

Characterizing the unknown Hamiltonian of a quantum many-body system is essential for exploring fundamental physical phenomena and advancing frontier quantum technologies. However, the complexity of many-body interactions and limited control capabilities in realistic experimental systems render this…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 170402] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors experimentally reconstruct the unknown Hamiltonian of a solid-state many-body spin system by letting it thermalize and fitting the observed equilibrium/relaxation behavior, providing a scalable tomography protocol.
motivation: Characterizing many-body Hamiltonians is essential for benchmarking quantum simulators and devices, but full tomography is prohibitively complex and typical experiments lack the control needed for conventional Hamiltonian learning.
method: Thermalization dynamics of the many-body system (NMR-style solid sample) are exploited as a natural probe; measured thermal state/relaxation data are inverted against a parametrized Hamiltonian model to extract coupling constants.
result: The protocol recovers the many-body Hamiltonian parameters of the solid-state system from thermalization data, demonstrating that equilibrium thermodynamics can substitute for demanding dynamical control in Hamiltonian characterization.
conclusion: Thermalization-based tomography offers a practical route to Hamiltonian characterization in complex many-body platforms, with implications for validating quantum simulators and for thermodynamic/information-theoretic accounts of equilibration.

title: Singular Behavior Of Observables At Hopf Bifurcations
authors: Benedikt Remlein And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Remlein and Massimiliano Esposito

Hopf bifurcations are a universal route to self-sustained oscillations in driven systems. Despite the absence of any singular stationary state, we show that time-averaged observables generically exhibit singularities at the onset of oscillations. The origin of this behavior is geometric: phase avera…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 177101] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that time-averaged observables generically become singular at Hopf bifurcations due to geometric phase-averaging effects, even without a singular stationary state.
motivation: Hopf bifurcations are a universal route to self-sustained oscillations in driven systems, but it is not obvious whether and why observables should exhibit singular behavior at the oscillation onset.
method: The authors analyze driven dynamical systems near a Hopf bifurcation and use a geometric phase-averaging argument to characterize the behavior of time-averaged observables.
result: They find that time-averaged observables generically exhibit singularities at the onset of oscillations, originating from the geometry of phase averaging rather than from any singular stationary state.
conclusion: These singularities are generic features of oscillatory driven systems and are important for correctly interpreting time-averaged observables near Hopf bifurcations.

title: Entropy Transport Through A Superfluid Quantum Point Contact: A Keldysh Field-theory Approach
authors: Davide Bertolusso, C. J. Bolech, And Thierry Giamarchi
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Bertolusso, C. J. Bolech, and Thierry Giamarchi
