We study the matter and entropy transport between two ultracold neutral Fermi-gas reservoirs linked by a quantum point contact under a chemical-potential gradient. We describe the two leads with a BCS mean-field model and derive the current-bias characteristics for both particle and entropy transpor…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043066] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a Keldysh field-theory approach to particle and entropy transport through a superfluid quantum point contact between two ultracold Fermi-gas reservoirs.
motivation: Understanding entropy flow in non-equilibrium quantum transport is relevant to quantum thermodynamics, but the specific platform is a mesoscopic superfluid Fermi gas rather than an information-theoretic thermodynamic setting.
method: The authors model the two leads with a BCS mean-field description and use Keldysh field theory to derive current-bias characteristics for both matter and entropy transport under a chemical-potential gradient.
result: They obtain particle and entropy current-bias relations for the superfluid quantum point contact, characterizing how transport depends on the bias and superfluid correlations.
conclusion: The work provides a field-theoretic framework for entropy transport in neutral superfluid quantum point contacts, bridging mesoscopic quantum transport and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Mapping Of Multiconstraint Satisfaction Problems To Rydberg Platforms
authors: Robert Gloeckner, Shahram Panahiyan, Frederik Koch, Dieter Jaksch, And Joseph Doetsch
abstract:
Author(s): Robert Gloeckner, Shahram Panahiyan, Frederik Koch, Dieter Jaksch, and Joseph Doetsch

We present a hardware-native gadget framework for solving constraint-satisfaction problems on Rydberg quantum computing architectures. Our approach introduces a compact [MATH] gadget that enforces exactly-one constraints, ubiquitous in combinatorial optimization, directly through geometr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043054] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a hardware-native gadget framework for mapping multiconstraint satisfaction problems onto Rydberg quantum computing architectures.
motivation: Combinatorial optimization problems with exactly-one constraints are difficult to embed efficiently on near-term quantum hardware, and Rydberg platforms offer native geometric interactions that may simplify such mappings.
method: The authors introduce a compact gadget that enforces exactly-one constraints directly through geometric arrangement and interactions on Rydberg neutral-atom arrays.
result: The framework enables efficient mapping of multiconstraint satisfaction problems to Rydberg platforms, reducing overhead compared with generic encodings.
conclusion: This work contributes a practical compilation/embedding approach for Rydberg quantum processors, but it is primarily an application-level architecture mapping rather than a core quantum-information or thermodynamic result.

title: Quantum Birthmarks: Ergodicity Breaking Beyond Scarring
authors: Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, And Joonas Keski-Rahkonen
abstract:
Author(s): Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, and Joonas Keski-Rahkonen

Researchers develop a theoretical framework showing that quantum systems permanently retain a memory of their initial state and early dynamics, in defiance of classical expectations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031063] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a theoretical framework showing that quantum systems retain a permanent 'birthmark' — a memory of their initial state and early-time dynamics — in regimes where classical ergodicity would erase such information, extending beyond the known phenomenon of quantum scarring.
motivation: Quantum scarring has shown that some eigenstates weakly violate ergodicity, but it was unclear whether memory of initial conditions can persist more generally in quantum systems that lack classical counterparts or fully chaotic limits.
method: The work develops an analytical/spectral framework characterizing long-time survival of initial-state imprints, contrasting quantum ergodicity breaking against classical mixing expectations and situating scarring as a special case.
result: The framework predicts that a class of quantum systems permanently encodes initial-state information, i.e., ergodicity breaking occurs in broader settings than scarring alone.
conclusion: Quantum ergodicity is less generic than classical intuition suggests, with implications for equilibration, thermalization, and information retention in isolated quantum systems.

title: Multiband Dispersion And Warped Vortices Of Strongly Interacting Photons
authors: Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, And Ofer Firstenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, and Ofer Firstenberg

A new study develops an analytical framework to understand and control nonlinear multiphoton processes in strongly interacting Rydberg media.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical framework for nonlinear multiphoton processes in strongly interacting Rydberg media, revealing multiband dispersion and warped vortex structures.
motivation: Strongly interacting photons in Rydberg media offer a platform for quantum nonlinear optics, but controlling multiphoton propagation and spatial modes requires deeper theoretical understanding.
method: The authors derive an analytical model for multiphoton dynamics in Rydberg media, likely treating Rydberg polaritons and their effective interactions.
result: They find multiband dispersion relations and warped vortex configurations for strongly interacting photons, characterizing how interactions reshape photonic propagation.
conclusion: The framework provides tools to understand and control nonlinear multiphoton processes in Rydberg atomic media, with potential implications for quantum photonic technologies.

title: Photon Climbing In A Kerr Ladder For Steady Nonclassical Light Generation
authors: Jiahua Li And Yan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiahua Li and Yan Liu

We propose a dissipative ladder-climbing mechanism in which [MATH] incoherently pumped qubits autonomously stabilize the cavity field near the target [MATH]-photon cavity Fock state [MATH]. Full Lindblad simulations verify the predicted photon-number climbing and show that Kerr-induced spect…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043731] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical proposal for dissipatively stabilizing a cavity near an n-photon Fock state using incoherently pumped qubits and a Kerr nonlinearity.
motivation: Steady nonclassical light and Fock-state generation are important for quantum technologies but remain challenging to achieve robustly.
method: The authors use full Lindblad master-equation simulations of qubits coupled to a Kerr cavity, with incoherent pumping driving a photon-number ladder-climbing process.
result: The simulations verify autonomous climbing toward the target Fock state and reveal Kerr-induced spectral features in the cavity field.
conclusion: The work offers a cavity-QED route to steady nonclassical light generation, though it is specialized and not directly aligned with the core information-theoretic, thermodynamic, or network interests.

title: Generalized Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon Hierarchy For Near-Integrable Dynamics
authors: Leonardo Biagetti, Maciej Łebek, Miłosz Panfil, And Jacopo de Nardis
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo Biagetti, Maciej Łebek, Miłosz Panfil, and Jacopo De Nardis

The BBGKY hierarchy is generalized to systems with strong integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body ones, enabling the computation of experimentally measurable expectation values and correlations for classical and quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041021] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes the BBGKY hierarchy to near-integrable many-body systems with strong contact and long-range two-body interactions, enabling computation of measurable correlations in classical and quantum settings.
motivation: Standard kinetic hierarchies are often limited to weak interactions or specific integrable models, while near-integrable dynamics require a framework that handles strong integrable contact interactions plus generic long-range couplings.
method: The authors extend the BBGKY hierarchy to systems with strong integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body interactions, formulating it for both classical and quantum systems.
result: The generalized hierarchy provides a systematic way to compute experimentally measurable expectation values and correlation functions in near-integrable many-body dynamics.
conclusion: This work offers a formal tool for non-equilibrium many-body dynamics, though its direct connection to information-theoretic or thermodynamic quantities is implicit rather than central.

title: Variational Multi-Gaussian Phase-Space Bosonic Dynamics Via Automatic Differentiation
authors: Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, And Cristiano Ciuti
abstract:
Author(s): Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, and Cristiano Ciuti

Researchers introduce a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method combining analytical techniques with automatic differentiation to reveal the critical dynamics of large open quantum bosonic lattices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031077] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method with automatic differentiation to simulate critical dynamics in large open quantum bosonic lattices.
motivation: Large open quantum bosonic lattices are difficult to simulate exactly, motivating scalable variational phase-space approaches for their non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: Combines analytical multi-Gaussian phase-space representations with automatic differentiation to variationally approximate the dynamics of open bosonic lattice systems.
result: The method is used to reveal critical dynamics in large open quantum bosonic lattices, demonstrating its capability for scalable many-body open-system simulation.
conclusion: Provides a practical numerical tool for studying non-equilibrium and critical phenomena in open quantum bosonic systems, though not directly addressing information-theoretic or thermodynamic quantities.

title: Interaction-Assisted Topological Pumping In Few- And Many-Atom Rydberg Arrays
authors: Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, And Bryce Gadway
abstract:
Author(s): Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, and Bryce Gadway

Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays are found to be able to bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters that undergo efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031075] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies interaction-assisted topological pumping of correlated atom pairs and clusters in few- and many-atom Rydberg arrays along a synthetic dimension.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays provide a flexible platform for quantum simulation, and strong dipolar interactions may enable interaction-driven topological transport beyond single-particle pumping.
method: The authors use Rydberg atom arrays with strong dipolar interactions to bind atoms into correlated pairs and clusters, and analyze their topological pumping dynamics in few- and many-atom regimes.
result: They find that interactions can assist efficient topological pumping of correlated atomic clusters along a synthetic dimension.
conclusion: The work demonstrates interaction-assisted topological transport in Rydberg arrays, relevant to neutral-atom quantum simulation but not directly to core quantum information, thermodynamics, or network goals.

title: Nonstabilizerness As A Diagnostic Of Criticality And Exceptional Points In non-Hermitian Spin Chains
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca, Doru Sticlet, And Balázs Dóra
abstract:
Author(s): Cătălin Paşcu Moca, Doru Sticlet, and Balázs Dóra

We investigate nonstabilizerness, also known as “magic”, to understand criticality and exceptional points in non-Hermitian quantum many-body systems. Our focus is on parity-time ([MATH])-symmetric spin chains, specifically the non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising and XX models. We calculate …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225136] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses nonstabilizerness (magic) as a diagnostic for criticality and exceptional points in non-Hermitian PT-symmetric spin chains.
motivation: Non-Hermitian quantum many-body systems exhibit exceptional points and critical phenomena, and the authors aim to understand whether nonstabilizerness can serve as a useful probe of these features.
method: They compute nonstabilizerness for non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising and XX models with parity-time symmetry.
result: The analysis shows how magic behaves across critical and exceptional-point regimes in these non-Hermitian spin chains.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness can act as a diagnostic tool for criticality and exceptional points, connecting resource-theoretic magic to non-Hermitian many-body physics.

title: Asymptotically Solvable Quantum Circuits
authors: Samuel H. Pickering And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel H. Pickering and Bruno Bertini

A new family of quantum circuits gives rise to correlations that are chaotic at short scales yet exactly solvable at long scales.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a new family of quantum circuits whose correlations are chaotic at short scales but exactly solvable at long scales.
motivation: Understanding chaotic quantum dynamics is difficult because generic chaotic systems lack analytic tractability; the work aims to bridge chaos and solvability.
method: The authors construct and analyze a new class of quantum circuits, deriving asymptotic behavior that separates short-scale chaotic correlations from long-scale exactly solvable dynamics.
result: The proposed circuits exhibit chaotic correlations at short distances/times while remaining analytically tractable at long scales.
conclusion: This provides a solvable model framework for studying chaotic quantum circuit dynamics and long-scale correlation structure.

title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance Quantization And Gate-Tunable Induced Superconducting Gap In Germanium
authors: Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, And Silvano de Franceschi
abstract:
Author(s): Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, and Silvano De Franceschi

Experiments in Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts demonstrate a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization in excellent agreement with theory.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033043] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts show gate-tunable proximity-induced superconductivity and near-ideal Andreev-enhanced conductance quantization.
motivation: Superconductor-semiconductor hybrid platforms are promising for quantum devices, and germanium is attractive due to strong spin-orbit coupling and compatibility with scalable qubit architectures.
method: The authors fabricate Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts coupled to superconducting electrodes and measure low-temperature transport as a function of gate voltage.
result: They observe a gate-tunable induced superconducting gap and conductance quantization in excellent agreement with theory.
conclusion: The results establish germanium quantum point contacts as a viable platform for tunable Andreev physics and superconductor-semiconductor hybrid quantum devices.

title: Exponentially Accurate Open Quantum Simulation Via Randomized Dissipation With Minimal Ancilla
authors: Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, And Naoki Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, and Naoki Yamamoto

Exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems is made viable for early fault-tolerant devices via a random compilation method requiring a minimal number of ancilla qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033046] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a randomized-compilation algorithm that simulates open quantum system dynamics (Lindblad evolution) to exponentially small error on early fault-tolerant devices while using only a minimal number of ancilla qubits.
motivation: Accurate simulation of open quantum systems is resource-intensive, particularly in ancilla count and circuit depth, which makes existing algorithms impractical for near-term fault-tolerant hardware.
method: They introduce a random compilation scheme in which dissipation is realized stochastically through randomized quantum channels, avoiding costly coherent dilations and large ancilla registers.
result: The protocol achieves exponentially accurate simulation of open system dynamics with a minimal ancilla overhead, improving the resource scaling relative to standard dilation-based approaches.
conclusion: Randomized dissipation offers a practical route to open quantum simulation on early fault-tolerant devices, trading deterministic circuit structure for reduced ancilla and depth requirements.

title: Hamiltonian-induced Error-channel Control For Lyapunov Quantum State Transfer
authors: Yiwei Chen, Xun Lang, And Jiande Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Yiwei Chen, Xun Lang, and Jiande Wu

Lyapunov quantum control provides a constructive mechanism for monotonically decreasing a target-dependent function, while generally leaving the transient dynamics of the associated quantum error unspecified. Here, we recast finite-dimensional state transfer as a Hamiltonian-induced error-channel as…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042622] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper formulates Lyapunov quantum state transfer as a Hamiltonian-induced error-channel control problem to characterize and shape transient dynamics.
motivation: Lyapunov quantum control guarantees monotonic decrease of a target-dependent function but usually leaves the transient error dynamics unspecified, limiting understanding and control of state-transfer performance.
method: The authors recast finite-dimensional quantum state transfer as an error-channel problem induced by the Hamiltonian and analyze how Hamiltonian engineering can control the resulting error channel within a Lyapunov control framework.
result: The approach provides a channel-based description of transient state-transfer errors and shows how Hamiltonian-induced control can influence the error-channel behavior beyond the standard monotonic Lyapunov guarantee.
conclusion: This work connects Lyapunov quantum control with quantum error-channel analysis, offering a structured way to study transient dynamics in quantum state transfer, though it remains a specialized control-theoretic contribution.

title: Chaotic Many-Body Quantum Dynamics, Spectral Correlations, And Energy Diffusion
authors: J. T. Chalker And Dominik Hahn
abstract:
Author(s): J. T. Chalker and Dominik Hahn

Researchers analyze a solvable many-body model to demonstrate how energy diffusion governs spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031076] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A solvable many-body model demonstrates that energy diffusion governs spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.
motivation: To understand universal features of chaotic many-body quantum dynamics and how transport properties connect to spectral statistics.
method: Analyze a solvable many-body model and relate energy diffusion to spectral correlation functions.
result: Energy diffusion is shown to control spectral correlations in the chaotic regime.
conclusion: The work links chaotic many-body dynamics, spectral correlations, and energy transport, providing a solvable route to universal behavior.

title: Tunable Goos-Hänchen Shift Assisted By Parametric Amplification In A Cavity Magnomechanical System
authors: Shuting Shen, Jing-Yi Pan, Ming-Ming Du, Xi-Yun Li, Wei Zhong, Lan Zhou, And Yu-Bo Sheng
abstract:
Author(s): Shuting Shen, Jing-Yi Pan, Ming-Ming Du, Xi-Yun Li, Wei Zhong, Lan Zhou, and Yu-Bo Sheng

We investigate the Goos-Hänchen shift (GHS) of a reflected probe beam in a hybrid cavity magnomechanical system assisted by parametric amplification. The pump-induced parametric process modifies the probe reflection response, especially its phase dispersion, providing an external means to control th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043732] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies tunable Goos-Hänchen shifts of a reflected probe beam in a cavity magnomechanical system assisted by parametric amplification.
motivation: The authors aim to show that parametric amplification can provide external control over the reflection phase dispersion and thus the Goos-Hänchen shift in a hybrid cavity magnomechanical platform.
method: They analyze the probe reflection response of a hybrid cavity magnomechanical system under a pump-induced parametric process, focusing on phase dispersion and the resulting beam shift.
result: Parametric amplification is found to modify the probe reflection response and enable tunable control of the Goos-Hänchen shift.
conclusion: The scheme offers a way to control optical beam shifts in cavity magnomechanics, with potential use in hybrid quantum/optical sensing settings.

title: Tensor-Network Framework For Lindbladian Spectra And Steady States
authors: Philipp Westhoff, Mattia Moroder, Ulrich Schollwöck, And Sebastian Paeckel
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Westhoff, Mattia Moroder, Ulrich Schollwöck, and Sebastian Paeckel

Researchers develop a tensor-network framework using complex-time evolution to accurately compute low-lying excitation spectra of open quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041020] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a tensor-network framework based on complex-time evolution to compute low-lying Lindbladian spectra and steady states of open quantum systems.
motivation: Accurately obtaining excitation spectra and steady states of Lindblad master equations is challenging due to the high dimensionality of Liouville space, motivating efficient numerical methods.
method: They develop a tensor-network approach that uses complex-time evolution to target low-lying eigenvalues and steady states of Lindbladian superoperators.
result: The framework is shown to accurately compute low-lying excitation spectra and steady states for open quantum systems, as reported in Phys. Rev. X.
conclusion: This provides a practical numerical tool for studying spectral properties and long-time behavior of dissipative quantum many-body systems.

title: Quantum Sensing Using Geometrical Phase In Qubit-Oscillator Systems
authors: Nishchay Suri, Zhihui Wang, Tanay Roy, Davide Venturelli, And Wibe Albert de Jong
abstract:
Author(s): Nishchay Suri, Zhihui Wang, Tanay Roy, Davide Venturelli, and Wibe Albert de Jong

We present a quantum sensing protocol for coupled qubit-oscillator systems that surpasses the standard quantum limit (SQL) by exploiting a geometrical phase. The signal is encoded in the geometrical phase that is proportional to the area enclosed in oscillator phase space. This area is amplified thr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 170802] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a quantum sensing protocol for coupled qubit-oscillator systems that beats the standard quantum limit by encoding the signal in a geometrical phase proportional to the area enclosed in oscillator phase space.
motivation: Standard sensing schemes based on linear signal accumulation face the SQL, and there is interest in finding amplification mechanisms in qubit-oscillator (circuit QED) platforms that circumvent this bound.
method: A geometrical phase acquired by a coupled qubit-oscillator system is used as the signal transducer; the phase-space area is amplified through the dynamics, and readout is performed via the qubit.
result: The protocol achieves sensitivity beyond the SQL, with the geometrical-phase encoding providing amplification of the measured signal relative to conventional dispersive approaches.
conclusion: Geometrical-phase-based sensing offers a promising route to enhanced metrology in qubit-oscillator hardware, though the work is primarily a metrology proposal rather than a hardware or transduction advance.

title: Atomic Interferometry With Spin-orbit-coupled Spin-1 Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Renfei Zheng, Junying Wu, Josep Cabedo, Alessio Celi, Zhihao Lan, Weiping Zhang, And Lu Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Renfei Zheng, Junying Wu, Josep Cabedo, Alessio Celi, Zhihao Lan, Weiping Zhang, and Lu Zhou

We propose and analyze a quantum interferometry scheme based on a Raman-dressed Bose gas with spin-orbit coupling. In this system, the atom-light coupling mixes spin and momentum degrees of freedom, giving rise, in the low-energy regime, to an effective spinor condensate whose spin-mixing interactio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043309] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum interferometry scheme using a Raman-dressed spin-orbit-coupled spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensate.
motivation: Spin-orbit coupling in cold atoms can mix spin and momentum degrees of freedom, offering a platform for novel interferometric sensing and many-body quantum control.
method: The authors analyze a Raman-dressed Bose gas in the low-energy regime, deriving an effective spinor condensate description with spin-mixing interactions and evaluating its interferometric response.
result: The scheme yields an effective spinor condensate whose spin-mixing interactions influence the interferometric signal, enabling a proposed atomic interferometry protocol.
conclusion: The work establishes spin-orbit-coupled spin-1 BECs as a promising platform for quantum interferometry, though its relevance to quantum information hardware is limited.

title: Fragile Single-cone Dirac Quantum Walks In Two Dimensions
authors: C. W. J. Beenakker, J. Sánchez Fernán, And J. Tworzydło
abstract:
Author(s): C. W. J. Beenakker, J. Sánchez Fernán, and J. Tworzydło

It is known that a one-dimensional quantum walk gives a local space-time discretization of the massless Dirac equation with a single quasienergy cone (no fermion doubling at low energies), keeping the fundamental symmetries (chiral and time-reversal) of the continuum theory. We show that the analogo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042213] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs and analyzes two-dimensional quantum walks that discretize the massless Dirac equation with a single quasienergy cone while preserving chiral and time-reversal symmetries, showing that this property is fragile.
motivation: One-dimensional quantum walks are known to provide local space-time discretizations of the massless Dirac equation without fermion doubling, and the authors investigate whether an analogous single-cone construction exists in two dimensions.
method: The authors design a two-dimensional quantum-walk model and analyze its quasienergy spectrum, symmetries, and stability under perturbations to assess whether a single Dirac cone can be maintained.
result: They find a two-dimensional single-cone Dirac quantum walk that retains the relevant symmetries, but the single-cone feature is fragile and can be destroyed by perturbations.
conclusion: Single-cone Dirac quantum walks in two dimensions are possible but require strict symmetry protection, limiting their robustness for practical quantum simulation or lattice-fermion applications.

title: Dissipative Dynamical Phase Transition As A Complex Ising Model
authors: Stephen W. Yan, Diego Barberena, Matthew P. A. Fisher, And Sagar Vijay
abstract:
Author(s): Stephen W. Yan, Diego Barberena, Matthew P. A. Fisher, and Sagar Vijay

We investigate a quantum dynamical phase transition induced by the competition between local unitary evolution and dissipation in a qubit chain with a strong, on-site [MATH] symmetry. While the steady state of this evolution is always maximally mixed, we show that the dynamical behavior …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204312] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a dissipative dynamical phase transition in a qubit chain with a strong on-site symmetry, described via a complex Ising model.
motivation: It aims to understand nontrivial dynamical phases emerging from the competition between local unitary evolution and dissipation in open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze a qubit chain with a strong on-site symmetry and map the dissipative dynamics to a complex Ising model to characterize the transition.
result: They identify a quantum dynamical phase transition even though the steady state is always maximally mixed, revealing distinct dynamical behavior across the transition.
conclusion: The work shows that dissipative dynamical criticality can be captured by a complex Ising model, providing insight into phase transitions in open quantum dynamics.

title: Hall's Exact Uncertainty Relation And The Geometry Of Krylov-space Operator Dynamics
authors: Mohsen Alishahiha And Souvik Banerjee
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Alishahiha and Souvik Banerjee

Krylov representations of operator dynamics encode two inequivalent motions: probability transport along the discrete Krylov chain and motion of the normalized amplitude vector on the associated sphere. We lift Hall's exact uncertainty relation to Liouville space and show that, for the fixed Krylov-…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042218] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends Hall's exact uncertainty relation to Liouville space and uses it to characterize the geometry of Krylov-space operator dynamics.
motivation: Krylov representations of operator dynamics involve both probability transport along the Krylov chain and motion on the associated amplitude sphere, motivating a geometric uncertainty-relation approach.
method: The authors lift Hall's exact uncertainty relation from Hilbert space to Liouville space and analyze operator dynamics in Krylov space.
result: They show how the uncertainty relation constrains and illuminates the geometric structure of Krylov-space operator dynamics for fixed Krylov sectors.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric uncertainty-relation perspective on Krylov operator dynamics, connecting operator growth to Liouville-space geometry.

title: Freezing And Shielding Under Global Quenches For Long-range Interacting Many-body Systems
authors: Daniel Arrufat-Vicente And Nicolò Defenu
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Arrufat-Vicente and Nicolò Defenu

This article reveals that previous observations, in which the nonequilibrium dynamics of long-range models mirror short-range systems under local quenches, reflect a universal feature of long-range interacting quantum systems. This is demonstrated by showing that this feature is also present under global quenches.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042010] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that freezing and shielding phenomena observed in the nonequilibrium dynamics of long-range interacting quantum systems under local quenches also occur under global quenches, revealing a universal feature.
motivation: Previous studies found that long-range models can mimic short-range systems under local quenches; the authors investigate whether this behavior is universal by extending it to global quenches.
method: Theoretical analysis of nonequilibrium quantum many-body dynamics in long-range interacting systems subjected to global quenches, comparing the resulting behavior to short-range systems.
result: The freezing and shielding features persist under global quenches, demonstrating that the previously observed mirroring of short-range dynamics is a universal property of long-range interacting systems.
conclusion: Long-range interacting quantum systems exhibit universal dynamical freezing and shielding independent of whether the quench is local or global.

title: Unitary Synthesis With Fewer T Gates
authors: Xinyu Tan
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Tan

A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates needed to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033058] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a new quantum compilation algorithm that asymptotically reduces the number of T gates required to synthesize arbitrary unitary operations.
motivation: T gates are expensive in fault-tolerant quantum computation, so reducing their count is important for practical quantum algorithm compilation.
method: The author develops a compilation algorithm for unitary synthesis that optimizes the T-count asymptotically for arbitrary unitaries.
result: The algorithm achieves an asymptotic reduction in T gates compared with previous synthesis methods.
conclusion: This work improves quantum circuit compilation by lowering T-count, but it is a specialized circuit-synthesis result rather than a core information-theoretic advance.

title: Quantum Advantage For Sensing Properties Of Classical Fields
authors: Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, And Ishaan Kannan
abstract:
Author(s): Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, and Ishaan Kannan

Researchers demonstrate a quantum sensing protocol that uses entanglement and squeezing to learn diverse classical signal properties with subvacuum precision.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041025] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a quantum sensing protocol that exploits entanglement and squeezing to estimate properties of classical fields with precision beyond the standard vacuum limit.
motivation: Classical sensing schemes for estimating parameters of classical fields are bounded by shot-noise/vacuum-level precision; quantum resources such as entanglement and squeezing promise sub-vacuum sensitivity, motivating a general framework for sensing diverse field properties.
method: A quantum sensing protocol is constructed in which entangled/squeezed probe states interrogate a classical field, and estimation strategies are analyzed to extract multiple classical signal properties at sub-vacuum precision.
result: The protocol demonstrates a quantum advantage, achieving precision below the vacuum (shot-noise) limit for learning a variety of classical field properties.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement and squeezing provide a genuine metrological advantage for characterizing classical fields, extending quantum-enhanced sensing beyond standard single-parameter estimation.

title: Cavity Control Of Quantum Phase Transitions In A Two-dimensional Kondo Lattice
authors: Jun Mochida, Ataç İmamoğlu, And Yuto Ashida
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Mochida, Ataç İmamoğlu, and Yuto Ashida

Cavity quantum electrodynamics offers a route to control quantum phases by using vacuum fluctuations of confined electromagnetic fields. In particular, planar cavities based on polar van der Waals materials can generate strongly confined modes and are promising for controlling two-dimensional correl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245131] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies how cavity vacuum fluctuations in planar polar van der Waals cavities can control quantum phase transitions in a two-dimensional Kondo lattice.
motivation: Cavity quantum electrodynamics offers a way to modify correlated quantum phases via confined electromagnetic vacuum fluctuations, and planar cavities based on polar van der Waals materials may enable strong control over two-dimensional correlated systems.
method: The authors analyze a two-dimensional Kondo lattice coupled to strongly confined cavity modes and examine how cavity-mediated interactions and vacuum fluctuations shift or drive quantum phase transitions.
result: The work identifies regimes where cavity control modifies the phase diagram of the Kondo lattice, demonstrating that cavity confinement can tune quantum critical behavior in the two-dimensional system.
conclusion: Cavity-engineered vacuum fluctuations provide a promising route for controlling quantum phase transitions in low-dimensional correlated materials, though the study is primarily condensed-matter/cavity-QED focused rather than targeting quantum information platforms.

title: Heisenberg-limited Metrology From The Quantum-quench Dynamics Of An Anisotropic Ferromagnet
authors: Z. M. Mcintyre, Ji Zou, Jelena Klinovaja, And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Z. M. McIntyre, Ji Zou, Jelena Klinovaja, and Daniel Loss

The emerging field of quantum magnonics seeks to understand and harness the quantum properties of magnons—quantized collective spin excitations in magnets. Squeezed magnon states arise naturally as the equilibrium ground states of anisotropic ferromagnets and antiferromagnets, representing an import…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043044] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using quantum-quench dynamics of an anisotropic ferromagnet to generate squeezed magnon states for Heisenberg-limited quantum metrology.
motivation: Quantum magnonics aims to exploit collective spin excitations in magnets, and squeezed magnon states naturally appear as ground states of anisotropic magnetic systems, motivating their use for enhanced sensing.
method: The authors analyze quench dynamics of an anisotropic ferromagnet to produce nonclassical magnon squeezing and evaluate its metrological utility via quantum metrology bounds.
result: The quench protocol yields squeezed magnon states that enable sensitivity approaching the Heisenberg limit, surpassing the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: Anisotropic ferromagnets provide a promising platform for quantum-enhanced magnonic metrology, though the work is primarily sensing-focused rather than advancing core quantum information or hybrid-qubit hardware.

title: Experimental Neuromorphic Computing Based On Quantum Memristor
authors: Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, and Philip Walther

A photonic neuromorphic architecture leverages a quantum memristor to enable nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for complex learning tasks such as vowel recognition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033067] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates a photonic quantum memristor architecture for nonlinear, memory-dependent neuromorphic processing, including vowel recognition.
motivation: Neuromorphic computing requires hardware with nonlinear memory effects, and quantum memristors could enable quantum-enhanced learning and processing.
method: A photonic integrated platform implements a quantum memristor whose response depends on prior quantum states, and it is used for nonlinear learning tasks.
result: The quantum memristor enables memory-dependent processing and is applied to vowel recognition, demonstrating experimental neuromorphic functionality.
conclusion: Quantum memristors provide a promising route toward quantum neuromorphic computing, though the work is primarily an applied experimental demonstration.

title: Theory Of Trotter Errors For Time-Dependent Product And Multi-product Formulas
authors: Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, and Keisuke Fujii

A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033061] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops Floquet-based commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct Trotter formulas, improving gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
motivation: Product and multiproduct formulas are widely used for digital quantum simulation, but error bounds for time-dependent Hamiltonians require sharper analysis to estimate gate counts accurately.
method: The authors use a Floquet-based framework to derive error bounds that scale with commutators of the Hamiltonian at different times, extending Trotter error theory to time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas.
result: The analysis yields commutator-scaling error bounds that refine gate-count estimates for simulating driven quantum dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides improved theoretical guarantees for time-dependent product formulas, useful for resource estimation in quantum simulation algorithms.

title: Shortcuts For Adiabatic And Variational Algorithms In Molecular Simulation
authors: Julián Ferreiro-Vélez, Iñaki Iriarte-Zendoia, Yue Ban, And Xi Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Julián Ferreiro-Vélez, Iñaki Iriarte-Zendoia, Yue Ban, and Xi Chen

Quantum algorithms offer a promising route toward computational advantage, but current implementations remain constrained by limited coherence and gate errors, making circuit complexity and noise sensitivity critical considerations. Here we develop a shortcut-to-adiabaticity strategy for molecular g…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042619] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops shortcut-to-adiabaticity protocols to reduce circuit depth and noise sensitivity in adiabatic and variational quantum algorithms for molecular ground-state simulation.
motivation: Near-term quantum devices for chemistry are limited by short coherence times and gate errors, so reducing circuit complexity and duration of adiabatic/variational molecular simulation protocols is essential for practical advantage.
method: Counterdiabatic (shortcut-to-adiabaticity) driving is combined with adiabatic and variational ansatz approaches, with numerical benchmarking on molecular Hamiltonians under noise models.
result: The shortcut protocols shorten the required evolution time and lower circuit complexity while maintaining or improving ground-state accuracy relative to conventional adiabatic and variational approaches.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity provide a practical route to more noise-resilient quantum chemistry algorithms on limited-coherence hardware.

title: Continuous-time Quantum Control Across An Exponentially Small Bottleneck In A Frustrated Ising Ring Model
authors: Vincenzo Roberto Arezzo, Kiran Thengil, And Giuseppe E. Santoro
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Roberto Arezzo, Kiran Thengil, and Giuseppe E. Santoro

Continuous-time quantum annealing (QA) is a strategy for preparing the ground state of nontrivial many-body systems. In its standard form, the dynamics is generated by a time-dependent interpolation between a simple driving Hamiltonian and the target problem Hamiltonian, usually implemented through …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042438] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies continuous-time quantum annealing in a frustrated Ising ring, where an exponentially small gap creates a bottleneck, and analyzes strategies to cross it via modified control schedules.
motivation: Standard linear-interpolation quantum annealing fails when the minimal spectral gap closes exponentially with system size, so understanding and circumventing such bottlenecks is key for ground-state preparation of frustrated many-body Hamiltonians.
method: Time-dependent interpolation between a simple driver and the frustrated Ising target Hamiltonian is simulated numerically, with the exponentially small gap characterized and alternative continuous-time control protocols tested against the standard schedule.
result: The bottleneck is traced to an exponentially small avoided crossing in the frustrated ring, and suitably tailored control schedules are shown to improve the ground-state fidelity relative to standard linear annealing.
conclusion: Frustrated Ising rings are shown to be hard for naive annealing, but continuous-time control can partially mitigate the exponential gap bottleneck, with implications for quantum annealer design and ground-state preparation.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Low-order Eigenmicrostates Underlying Heat-current Reversal In Periodically Driven Frenkel-Kontorova Lattices
authors: Yingying Zhang, Kezhao Xiong, Zhuohan Wang, Tengteng He, Wei Liu, And Li Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Yingying Zhang, Kezhao Xiong, Zhuohan Wang, Tengteng He, Wei Liu, and Li Ma

Frequency-dependent directed heat transport and heat-current reversal have been identified in nonlinear asymmetric lattices driven by a zero-mean thermal bias, but the microscopic dynamics associated with heat-current reversal remain incompletely understood. Here we introduce an eigenmicrostate-base…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044134] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses an eigenmicrostate-based analysis to explain heat-current reversal in periodically driven nonlinear asymmetric Frenkel-Kontorova lattices.
motivation: Frequency-dependent directed heat transport and heat-current reversal in nonlinear lattices under zero-mean thermal bias are known, but the microscopic dynamical mechanism remains unclear.
method: The authors analyze periodically driven Frenkel-Kontorova lattices using an eigenmicrostate decomposition to identify collective modes associated with heat-current reversal.
result: Heat-current reversal is linked to collective enhancement of low-order eigenmicrostates in the driven nonlinear lattice.
conclusion: The work provides a microscopic mode-based picture of heat-current reversal, but it is a classical nonlinear lattice study with limited direct connection to quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Electrically Tunable Orbital Coupling And Quantum Light Emission From O-Band Quantum Dot Molecules
authors: P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, And J. J. Finley
abstract:
Author(s): P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, and J. J. Finley

Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules exhibit electrically tunable orbital coupling, opening a route toward 2D photonic cluster states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033070] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules with electrically tunable orbital coupling are demonstrated as a platform for generating quantum light and, ultimately, 2D photonic cluster states.
motivation: Photonic cluster states are a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, but scalable generation requires deterministic, tunable, emitter-based sources operating at telecom wavelengths compatible with fiber infrastructure.
method: Molecular-beam-epitaxy-grown InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules are embedded in a device enabling electrical control of the inter-dot orbital coupling; photoluminescence and correlation measurements characterize the emitted quantum light in the O-band.
result: The authors show electrically tunable orbital coupling between the coupled dots and observe quantum light emission in the telecom O-band, consistent with a route toward multi-photon entangled cluster-state generation.
conclusion: Quantum dot molecules offer a promising, electrically controllable solid-state platform for telecom-band quantum light sources, though realization of 2D photonic cluster states remains future work.

title: Chladni States In Ising Spin Lattices
authors: Giulio Iannelli And Pablo Villegas
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Iannelli and Pablo Villegas

Low-temperature spin dynamics can become trapped in long-lived patterns shaped by the geometry of the interaction network. We introduce Chladni states, the binary spin configurations obtained by applying the sign function to Laplacian eigenmodes, and show that their Ising energy collapses onto a siz…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044130] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Chladni states—binary spin configurations from the sign of Laplacian eigenmodes—and studies their Ising energy and long-lived low-temperature dynamics in spin lattices.
motivation: Low-temperature spin dynamics can become trapped in long-lived patterns determined by the geometry of the interaction network, motivating a characterization of such configurations.
method: The authors define Chladni states by applying the sign function to Laplacian eigenmodes and analyze their Ising energies and dynamical trapping in spin lattices.
result: The Ising energy of Chladni states is shown to collapse onto a size-dependent form, linking network geometry to long-lived spin patterns.
conclusion: Chladni states provide a geometric route to understanding metastable low-temperature spin configurations in Ising lattices.

title: Energy-Efficient Control Of Interacting Microscopic Systems: When Longer Paths Save Energy
authors: Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, And Clemens Bechinger
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, and Clemens Bechinger

Harnessing hydrodynamic interactions offers a route to control multiparticle systems efficiently, enabling substantial reductions in the energetic cost of microscopic transport.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031079] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that hydrodynamic interactions between microscopically driven particles can be exploited so that longer transport paths cost less energy, yielding a strategy for energy-efficient control of interacting microscopic systems.
motivation: Controlling and transporting microscopic particles typically requires dissipating work, and finding protocols that reduce this energetic cost is a central practical question in stochastic thermodynamics and microscopic manipulation.
method: Using theory and experiment on interacting colloidal particles in a fluid, the authors compare transport protocols and quantify the energetic cost as a function of path geometry, exploiting hydrodynamic coupling between particles.
result: Counterintuitively, paths that are geometrically longer can require less total work when hydrodynamic interactions are harnessed, giving substantial reductions in the energetic cost of transport.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic interactions provide a generic control knob for minimizing dissipation in multiparticle microscopic transport, with implications for the design of low-dissipation protocols in driven soft-matter and stochastic systems.

title: Optomechanical Detection Of Individual Gas Collisions
authors: Yu-Han Tseng, Clarke A. Hardy, T. W. Penny, Cecily Lowe, Jacqueline Baeza-Rubio, Daniel Carney, And David C. Moore
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Han Tseng, Clarke A. Hardy, T. W. Penny, Cecily Lowe, Jacqueline Baeza-Rubio, Daniel Carney, and David C. Moore

An experiment resolves the tiny momentum transferred from an individual gas molecule to a levitated nanoparticle.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 173601] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: An experiment resolves the momentum kick delivered by a single gas molecule colliding with a levitated nanoparticle, reaching the single-collision regime.
motivation: Gas collisions are a dominant decoherence and heating channel for levitated mechanical sensors, so resolving individual collisions is needed to characterize and control the thermal environment of the oscillator.
method: A levitated nanoparticle optomechanically monitored in a high-vacuum trap is used to detect discrete momentum transfers from individual impinging gas molecules.
result: Individual collision events are resolved, giving a direct statistical handle on the momentum distribution and the resulting random-walk heating of the particle.
conclusion: The measurement establishes single-molecule collision resolution as a tool for understanding and mitigating environmental decoherence in levitated optomechanical systems.

title: Instability-enhanced Quantum Sensing With Tunable Multibody Interactions
authors: Bidhi Vijaywargia, Jorge Chávez-Carlos, Francisco Pérez-Bernal, And Lea F. Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Bidhi Vijaywargia, Jorge Chávez-Carlos, Francisco Pérez-Bernal, and Lea F. Santos

Dynamical instabilities can amplify small perturbations into measurable signals, offering a route to quantum-enhanced sensing. This mechanism was experimentally demonstrated in a collective spin system with quadratic interactions, described by a twist-and-turn Hamiltonian, where quantum evolution ne…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043052] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how dynamical instabilities in a collective spin model with tunable multibody (twist-and-turn-like) interactions can be exploited to amplify small perturbations for quantum-enhanced sensing.
motivation: Dynamical instabilities offer a practical route to quantum-enhanced metrology, as previously demonstrated in a collective spin system with quadratic interactions; the authors ask whether adding tunable multibody interactions can further enhance the sensitivity of such instability-based sensing protocols.
method: Using a collective spin model with quadratic and tunable multibody interactions, the authors analyze the dynamics of small perturbations under the resulting unstable evolution and characterize the achievable amplification and measurement sensitivity, likely also examining how chaos or integrability affects performance.
result: Tunable multibody interactions are shown to modify the instability-driven amplification, enabling enhanced sensing performance relative to the purely quadratic twist-and-turn case, with the sensitivity depending on the interaction parameters and dynamical regime.
conclusion: Instability-enhanced protocols with tunable multibody interactions provide a flexible platform for quantum sensing, and the interplay between interaction range and unstable dynamics offers a design knob for optimizing measurement precision.

title: Constructing Bulk Topological Orders Via Layered Gauging
authors: Shang Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Liu

Understanding quantum phases and phase transitions in the presence of symmetries is a central objective of quantum many-body physics. A powerful modern paradigm for investigating this problem is topological holography, which relates symmetries in [MATH] dimensions to “bulk” topological orders in $(k+1)…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245130] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a layered gauging construction to generate bulk topological orders from lower-dimensional symmetry data within topological holography.
motivation: Understanding quantum phases and phase transitions with symmetries is central to quantum many-body physics, and topological holography provides a framework relating lower-dimensional symmetries to higher-dimensional bulk topological orders.
method: The author uses a layered gauging procedure to construct bulk topological orders, connecting symmetry structures in d dimensions to topological orders in (d+1) dimensions.
result: The construction yields bulk topological orders and clarifies how symmetry data in lower dimensions maps to topological order in one higher dimension.
conclusion: This work advances the topological holography paradigm and provides a systematic route to constructing and classifying symmetry-related topological orders.

title: Mean-field Convective Phase Separation Under Thermal Gradients
authors: Meander van Den Brande, François Huveneers, And Kyosuke Adachi
abstract:
Author(s): Meander Van den Brande, François Huveneers, and Kyosuke Adachi

Nonequilibrium conditions fundamentally change how systems undergo phase separation. In lattice gases with attractive interactions under temperature gradients, particles have been shown to form periodic patterns and steady convective currents; however, a clear theoretical explanation of this convect…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042107] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: A mean-field theory explaining convective phase separation and periodic pattern formation in attractive lattice gases driven by a thermal gradient.
motivation: Temperature gradients in interacting lattice gases are known to produce periodic density patterns and steady convective currents, but a clear theoretical account of the underlying convective instability was lacking.
method: Mean-field treatment of an attractive lattice gas under a thermal gradient, deriving the conditions for the convective instability and the resulting steady-state periodic density profiles.
result: The analysis identifies the mechanism behind the instability and predicts the emergence of convective currents and periodic patterns, in agreement with earlier numerical observations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for nonequilibrium pattern formation and phase separation driven by thermal gradients in classical lattice gases.

title: Topological Flowscape Reveals State Transitions In Nonreciprocal Living Matter
authors: Hyunseok Lee, Eliseanne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, And Nikta Fakhri
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunseok Lee, EliseAnne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, and Nikta Fakhri

Characterizing living systems far from the thermodynamic limit can yield insight into the physics of nonreciprocity and biological self-organization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031061] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses a topological flowscape approach to identify state transitions in nonreciprocal living matter far from equilibrium.
motivation: Living systems operate far from thermodynamic equilibrium, and understanding nonreciprocity and self-organization can reveal general physical principles governing biological state transitions.
method: The authors analyze nonreciprocal dynamics in living matter through a topological flowscape framework, likely combining experimental data with topological/non-equilibrium modeling.
result: The analysis reveals state transitions in nonreciprocal living matter and highlights how topological features characterize non-equilibrium organization.
conclusion: Topological flowscape methods provide insight into nonreciprocity and self-organization in living systems, with broader implications for non-equilibrium matter.

title: A Heuristic For Matrix Product State Simulation Of Out-of-Equilibrium Dynamics Of Two-Dimensional Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, And Kostyantyn Kechedzhi
abstract:
Author(s): Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, and Kostyantyn Kechedzhi

A new heuristic approach accelerates the convergence of classical simulation of two-dimensional quantum dynamics, enabling the verification of quantum simulation experiments in previously inaccessible regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033048] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A heuristic is introduced to speed up convergence of matrix product state classical simulations of out-of-equilibrium dynamics in two-dimensional quantum spin systems, aimed at verifying quantum simulation experiments.
motivation: Verifying large-scale quantum simulation experiments requires classical simulation of 2D out-of-equilibrium quantum dynamics, which is severely limited by entanglement growth and computational cost in tensor-network methods.
method: The authors develop a heuristic (likely bond-dimension/truncation or gauging strategy) that accelerates convergence of MPS-based simulations of 2D spin dynamics, benchmarking against exact or high-accuracy references.
result: The heuristic enables classical simulation to reach dynamical regimes previously inaccessible, providing verification capability for quantum simulators in those regimes.
conclusion: The approach extends the practical reach of tensor-network classical simulation for 2D quantum dynamics, though it remains a numerical/algorithmic tool rather than an information-theoretic or thermodynamic result.

title: Quantum Architecture Generation Via Predictor-guided Diffusion Models
authors: Jiawen Dai, Jialiang Gu, Raymond Ho, Gary Man-Tat Man, Kwok Tai Chui, Kevin Hung, And Fanxu Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Jiawen Dai, Jialiang Gu, Raymond Ho, Gary Man-Tat Man, Kwok Tai Chui, Kevin Hung, and Fanxu Meng

The performance of variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) critically depends on the architecture of parametrized quantum circuits (PQCs), yet manually designing effective circuits remains challenging due to the exponentially large design space. Conventional quantum architecture search methods address…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042620] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a predictor-guided diffusion model to generate parametrized quantum circuit architectures for variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Designing effective PQC architectures by hand is difficult because the design space is exponentially large, and conventional quantum architecture search methods can be inefficient.
method: The authors use a diffusion-based generative model guided by a performance predictor to propose candidate quantum circuit architectures, aiming to reduce search cost and improve VQA performance.
result: The approach is presented as a way to automatically generate high-quality quantum architectures, though the abstract suggests an empirical architecture-search contribution rather than a new information-theoretic result.
conclusion: The work is primarily a machine-learning-driven quantum architecture search method with limited direct connection to the user's core interests in quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Flux-Floquet Instability In Fluctuating Superconductors
authors: Marios H. Michael, Duilio de Santis, Eugene A. Demler, And Patrick A. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Marios H. Michael, Duilio De Santis, Eugene A. Demler, and Patrick A. Lee

Intense terahertz light triggers a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, generating a giant magnetic response that reveals bound electron pairs survive well above the superconducting transition temperature.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031055] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: Intense THz light drives a flux-Floquet instability in high-Tc superconductors, producing a giant magnetic response that indicates bound electron pairs persist well above Tc.
motivation: Floquet driving of correlated superconductors is a route to non-equilibrium phases, but the collective magnetic response of fluctuating superconductors under strong periodic drive near and above Tc remains poorly understood.
method: A theoretical analysis of the Floquet response of superconducting order-parameter fluctuations under intense terahertz illumination, deriving an instability in the fluctuating flux sector and the resulting magnetic susceptibility.
result: The driven system exhibits a flux-Floquet instability generating a greatly enhanced magnetic response, interpreted as evidence for preformed electron pairs surviving above the transition temperature.
conclusion: The effect offers a driven, non-equilibrium probe of superconducting fluctuations and pair formation in the pseudogap regime of high-Tc materials.

title: Space-time Floquet Operator: Nonreciprocity And Fractional Topology Of Space-time Crystals
authors: Abhijeet Melkani And Jayson Paulose
abstract:
Author(s): Abhijeet Melkani and Jayson Paulose

A space-time Floquet operator is introduced that captures the long-time dynamics of systems with intertwined spatial and temporal periodicities. The resulting band framework uncovers fractional quantized charge pumping, connects topological windings to Floquet–Bloch oscillations, and predicts nonreciprocal amplification.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042009] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a space-time Floquet operator describing systems with intertwined spatial and temporal periodicity, yielding a band framework that predicts fractional quantized charge pumping, links topological windings to Floquet-Bloch oscillations, and implies nonreciprocal amplification.
motivation: Space-time crystals—systems modulated periodically in both space and time—host rich topological and nonreciprocal physics that is not captured by conventional Floquet or Bloch theory alone; a unified long-time dynamical operator is needed.
method: A space-time Floquet operator is constructed to capture the long-time dynamics of systems with commensurate spatial and temporal periods, and its band structure and topological invariants (winding numbers) are analyzed analytically.
result: The band framework reveals fractionally quantized charge pumping, connects topological windings to Floquet-Bloch oscillations, and predicts nonreciprocal amplification in such media.
conclusion: Space-time Floquet bands provide a general topological classification of space-time crystals with experimentally relevant consequences for pumping and nonreciprocal transport.

title: Quantum Phase Transitions Generated By Order From Quantum Disorder
authors: Fadi Sun, Jinwu Ye, And Wu-Ming Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Fadi Sun, Jinwu Ye, and Wu-Ming Liu

The order from quantum disorder (OFQD) effect was first discovered in frustrated quantum spin systems. Recently, OFQD was also found in Rashba spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) systems even on a square lattice. Here we study the role of OFQD in the experimentally realized weakly interacting bosonic quantum a…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235124] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies order-from-quantum-disorder effects in Rashba spin-orbit-coupled weakly interacting bosonic systems and their role in generating quantum phase transitions.
motivation: Order from quantum disorder was originally found in frustrated quantum magnets and has recently been identified in Rashba spin-orbit-coupled square-lattice systems; the authors aim to extend this mechanism to experimentally relevant weakly interacting bosonic platforms.
method: The authors analyze quantum phase transitions in weakly interacting bosonic systems with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, using order-from-quantum-disorder physics to identify ordered phases and transition mechanisms.
result: The study characterizes how quantum fluctuations and spin-orbit coupling can stabilize ordered phases and drive quantum phase transitions in bosonic systems.
conclusion: The work clarifies the role of order from quantum disorder in spin-orbit-coupled bosons and connects it to experimentally realizable condensed-matter settings.

title: Lee-Yang Zeros And Pseudocritical Drift In J-q Néel Antiferromagnet–valence-bond Solid Transitions
authors: Chunhao Guo, Zhe Wang, Danhe Wang, Zenan Liu, Haiyuan Zou, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Chunhao Guo, Zhe Wang, Danhe Wang, Zenan Liu, Haiyuan Zou, and Zheng Yan

Square-lattice J-Q models provide a sign-problem-free setting for probing the quantum phase transition between Néel antiferromagnets and columnar valence-bond solids. We analyze this transition through the scaling of Lee-Yang zeros, computed within stochastic series expansion quantum Monte Carlo by …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231112] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses Lee-Yang zero scaling in quantum Monte Carlo to characterize the Néel antiferromagnet–columnar valence-bond-solid transition in square-lattice J-Q models.
motivation: J-Q models offer a sign-problem-free platform for studying transitions between Néel order and valence-bond solids, and Lee-Yang zeros provide an alternative probe of critical behavior and pseudocritical drift.
method: The authors compute Lee-Yang zeros via stochastic series expansion quantum Monte Carlo and analyze their finite-size scaling to extract transition properties and pseudocritical behavior.
result: The scaling of Lee-Yang zeros reveals the critical behavior of the Néel–VBS transition and indicates pseudocritical drift in the J-Q model.
conclusion: Lee-Yang zero analysis provides a useful numerical diagnostic for quantum phase transitions in J-Q models, though the work is primarily a condensed-matter quantum-criticality study rather than an information-thermodynamics contribution.

title: Ramsey Atom Interferometry With Transverse Optical Modes
authors: Ryan Husband, Ryan J. Thomas, Yosri Ben-Aïcha, Rhys H. Eagle, Jessica Eastman, John E. Debs, Patrick J. Everitt, Michael Larsen, Eric Imhof, Charles A. Sackett, John D. Close, Simon A. Haine, And Samuel Legge
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Husband, Ryan J. Thomas, Yosri Ben-Aïcha, Rhys H. Eagle, Jessica Eastman, John E. Debs, Patrick J. Everitt, Michael Larsen, Eric Imhof, Charles A. Sackett, John D. Close, Simon A. Haine, and Samuel Legge

The authors demonstrate light-pulse atom interferometry based on the transverse helical phase of optical vortex modes, realizing a rotation sensor whose scale factor is governed by orbital angular momentum and interrogation time rather than an enclosed geometric area. Using cold rubidium atoms, they experimentally verify the linear scaling of the interferometer phase with rotation rate and interrogation time, and establish a predictive model for the thermal dephasing observed near the optical phase singularity.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043311] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate light-pulse Ramsey atom interferometry using the transverse helical phase of optical vortex beams, producing a rotation sensor whose scale factor depends on orbital angular momentum and interrogation time rather than enclosed area.
motivation: Conventional atom-interferometry rotation sensors (Sagnac gyroscopes) rely on large enclosed geometric areas, which limits compactness; using orbital angular momentum of optical vortex modes offers an alternative scaling mechanism.
method: Cold rubidium atoms are subjected to light-pulse interferometry with optical vortex modes carrying transverse helical phase; the rotation-dependent interferometer phase is measured as a function of rotation rate and interrogation time, and a model is developed for thermal dephasing near the optical phase singularity.
result: The experiment verifies linear scaling of the interferometric phase with rotation rate and with interrogation time, and reproduces the observed thermal dephasing near the vortex core with a predictive model.
conclusion: OAM-based atom interferometry provides a viable route to compact rotation sensing with scale factor set by orbital angular momentum and interrogation time, though technical noise from the phase singularity currently limits performance.

title: Energy Relaxation In Superconducting Single-crystal TiN Films Probed By Flux-flow Instability
authors: E. M. Baeva, N. A. Titova, M. A. Kirsanova, S. A. Evlashin, A. V. Semenov, D. Yu. Vodolazov, A. I. Kolbatova, And G. N. Goltsman
abstract:
Author(s): E. M. Baeva, N. A. Titova, M. A. Kirsanova, S. A. Evlashin, A. V. Semenov, D. Yu. Vodolazov, A. I. Kolbatova, and G. N. Goltsman

We employ the flux-flow instability (FFI) technique—a widely used method for determining the quasiparticle relaxation time ([MATH])—to investigate single-crystal superconducting titanium nitride (TiN) films characterized by weak vortex pinning and slow electron-phonon relaxation. By systematicall…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194513] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors use the flux-flow instability technique to extract the quasiparticle energy relaxation time in weakly pinned single-crystal TiN films with slow electron-phonon coupling.
motivation: Reliable knowledge of the quasiparticle relaxation time in superconducting nitride films is needed for device applications, and FFI offers an alternative to conventional pump-probe or microwave measurements, particularly in films with weak vortex pinning where other methods are difficult.
method: Current-voltage characteristics of single-crystal superconducting TiN films are measured and analyzed within the flux-flow instability framework, fitting the instability threshold to extract the quasiparticle relaxation time and its dependence on temperature, magnetic field, and film parameters.
result: The FFI-derived relaxation times are obtained across the studied parameter range and compared with expectations for slow electron-phonon relaxation in weakly pinned TiN, showing the technique's viability for this material class.
conclusion: FFI is demonstrated as a practical probe of quasiparticle relaxation dynamics in single-crystal TiN, providing material parameters of interest for superconducting device design but without direct qubit or quantum-information benchmarks.

title: Probing Antiferromagnetic Hysteresis On Programmable Quantum Annealers
authors: Elijah Pelofske, Pratik Sathe, Cristiano Nisoli, And Frank Barrows
abstract:
Author(s): Elijah Pelofske, Pratik Sathe, Cristiano Nisoli, and Frank Barrows

Using programmable analog quantum annealing processors, we implement a sampling-based magnetic hysteresis protocol to probe the counterintuitive notion of magnetic memory in antiferromagnetic models. A key component of this protocol responsible for the hysteresis is a transverse field, which enables…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214425] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors implement a sampling-based magnetic hysteresis protocol on programmable quantum annealers to demonstrate magnetic memory effects in antiferromagnetic spin models.
motivation: Antiferromagnets are conventionally expected to lack magnetic memory, so probing hysteresis in antiferromagnetic models is counterintuitive and of interest for understanding memory in frustrated spin systems.
method: A transverse field, applied within a sampling-based hysteresis protocol on D-Wave-style analog quantum annealing processors, drives the system through field cycles to reveal hysteretic behavior.
result: The annealer experiments show hysteresis loops in antiferromagnetic models, indicating that the transverse field is a key ingredient enabling the observed magnetic memory.
conclusion: Programmable quantum annealers can serve as platforms for exploring unconventional magnetic memory and hysteresis in antiferromagnetic systems.

title: Coherent Control Of Photon Pairs Via Quantum Interference Between Second- And Third-order Quantum Nonlinear Processes
authors: Alessia Stefano, Samuel E. Fontaine, J. E. Sipe, And Marco Liscidini
abstract:
Author(s): Alessia Stefano, Samuel E. Fontaine, J. E. Sipe, and Marco Liscidini

Genuine quantum interference between independent nonlinear processes of different order provides a route to coherent control that cannot be reduced to a classical field interference. Here we present an all-optical analog of coherent carrier injection by exploiting interference between second- and th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043527] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes an all-optical scheme for coherent control of photon pairs using quantum interference between second- and third-order nonlinear optical processes.
motivation: Genuine interference between independent nonlinear processes of different order could enable coherent control beyond classical field interference, with potential analogies to coherent carrier injection in semiconductors.
method: The authors develop a theoretical description of quantum interference between second-order and third-order nonlinear processes and apply it to photon-pair generation and control in an all-optical setting.
result: They show that interference between processes of different order can provide coherent control of photon-pair properties that cannot be reduced to classical optical interference.
conclusion: The work establishes a route to exploiting multi-order quantum nonlinear interference for controlling photon-pair generation, though its relevance to the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions is limited.

title: Penning Trap Single-photon Counter For Axion Detection
authors: Jack A. Devlin, Marko L. Wojtkowiak, Shreyak R. Banhatti, He Zhang, Jiacheng Shi, Toren S. Dofher, Jonathan M. H. Gosling, Michael R. Tarbutt, And Richard C. Thompson
abstract:
Author(s): Jack A. Devlin, Marko L. Wojtkowiak, Shreyak R. Banhatti, He Zhang, Jiacheng Shi, Toren S. Dofher, Jonathan M. H. Gosling, Michael R. Tarbutt, and Richard C. Thompson

Discovering the microscopic composition of dark matter is one of the most important open problems in physics today. Axions are a leading candidate to be dark matter; however, a search of the full range of all likely axion masses is hampered by the standard quantum noise limit. This makes haloscope s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043082] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a Penning-trap-based single-microwave-photon counter to circumvent the standard quantum limit that restricts axion haloscope searches over the full plausible mass range.
motivation: Discovering the microscopic nature of dark matter is a central open problem, and axion haloscopes are currently limited by quantum noise when scanning the wide range of candidate axion masses.
method: A single charged particle confined in a Penning trap is used as a sensitive detector of individual microwave photons, with the trapping and detection scheme characterized for quantum-noise-limited photon counting.
result: The scheme demonstrates single-photon sensitivity in the microwave regime relevant to axion conversion in a cavity haloscope, potentially enabling faster or broader mass scans.
conclusion: The Penning trap photon counter offers a route to surpass the standard quantum limit in axion dark matter searches, though the work is primarily an instrumental/metrology proposal rather than a quantum information result.

title: Searching For Ultralight Dark Matter With MOLeQuTE: A Massive Optically Levitated Quantum Tabletop Experiment
authors: Louis Hamaide, Hannah Banks, Peter Barker, And Andrew A. Geraci
abstract:
Author(s): Louis Hamaide, Hannah Banks, Peter Barker, and Andrew A. Geraci

Many well theoretically motivated models of ultralight dark matter are expected to give rise to feeble oscillatory forces on macroscopic objects. Optically trapped sensors have high force sensitivities but have remained relatively unexplored in this context. In this work, we propose a tunable, optic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043086] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: MOLeQuTE proposes a tunable optically levitated optomechanical sensor array to search for feeble oscillatory forces from ultralight dark matter.
motivation: Many well-motivated ultralight dark matter models predict weak oscillatory forces on macroscopic objects, and optically trapped sensors offer high force sensitivity but remain largely unexplored for this purpose.
method: The authors design a tabletop experiment using optically levitated dielectric particles with tunable trapping and readout to achieve high force sensitivity across a range of dark matter masses.
