result: The proposed scheme is projected to probe unconstrained regions of ultralight dark matter parameter space with enhanced force sensitivity compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: Optically levitated quantum sensors constitute a promising, tunable platform for tabletop dark matter searches.

title: Toward Complete Characterization Of Topological Insulators And Superconductors: A Systematic Construction Of Topological Invariants Based On Atiyah-Hirzebruch Spectral Sequence
authors: Seishiro Ono And Ken Shiozaki
abstract:
Author(s): Seishiro Ono and Ken Shiozaki

A framework based on the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space yields topological invariants that classify stable superconducting phases across 159 space groups.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041024] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The authors construct a systematic framework based on the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space to classify stable topological superconducting phases across all 159 space groups.
motivation: Topological insulators and superconductors require complete classification, but existing approaches struggle to produce explicit invariants for the full set of space groups, especially for superconductors.
method: They employ the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space, deriving topological invariants that capture stable superconducting phases for each of the 159 space groups.
result: The framework yields a complete set of topological invariants classifying stable superconducting phases across all 159 space groups, providing a systematic classification scheme.
conclusion: The spectral-sequence approach offers a unified route toward complete characterization of topological insulators and superconductors, though its relevance is confined to condensed-matter topology rather than quantum information.

title: One-Positron Quantum Cyclotron
authors: T. G. Myers, L. Soucy, B. A. D. Sukra, B. Sinha, And G. Gabrielse
abstract:
Author(s): T. G. Myers, L. Soucy, B. A. D. Sukra, B. Sinha, and G. Gabrielse

A device that stores a single positron and controls its quantum states could measure its magnetic moment with unprecedented precision, testing a symmetry principle central to quantum field theory.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 173001] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: A single positron stored in a Penning trap with its quantum cyclotron states controlled enables an ultra-precise measurement of the positron magnetic moment, providing a stringent test of CPT symmetry.
motivation: The electron/positron magnetic moment is one of the most precisely known quantities in physics and a sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model; comparing the two tests CPT invariance, a cornerstone of quantum field theory.
method: A one-particle quantum cyclotron apparatus traps an individual positron in a Penning trap, cools and manipulates its cyclotron and spin quantum states, and performs high-precision frequency measurements of the spin and cyclotron transitions.
result: The device demonstrates quantum-state control of a single trapped positron, enabling magnetic-moment measurements at unprecedented precision that can be compared against the electron's value.
conclusion: The work establishes single-positron quantum cyclotron techniques as a precision frontier for CPT tests and fundamental-constant metrology, rather than advancing quantum information processing.

title: Exact Generalized Langevin Dynamics Of Pair Coordinates In Elastic Networks
authors: Shunsuke Ando, Tomoya Urashita, Soya Shinkai, And Tomoshige Miyaguchi
abstract:
Author(s): Shunsuke Ando, Tomoya Urashita, Soya Shinkai, and Tomoshige Miyaguchi

Generalized Langevin equations (GLEs) provide a powerful framework for describing slow dynamics in soft-matter systems, but deriving an exact GLE for a reaction coordinate from an underlying many-body system remains generally difficult. Here, we analytically derive an exact coupled GLE for the overd…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042108] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The authors analytically derive an exact coupled generalized Langevin equation (GLE) for pair coordinates in overdamped elastic networks, providing a rigorous coarse-graining route from a many-body system to a reaction-coordinate description.
motivation: GLEs are a powerful framework for capturing slow, memory-dependent dynamics in soft matter, but obtaining an exact GLE for a chosen reaction coordinate from the underlying microscopic many-body dynamics is generally intractable.
method: Starting from an overdamped many-body elastic network model, they analytically eliminate the bath degrees of freedom to construct an exact coupled GLE for pair coordinates, with explicit memory kernels and fluctuating-force correlations.
result: The derivation yields an exact closed-form coupled GLE structure for pair coordinates, expressing the memory kernel and noise statistics in terms of the network's elastic properties and demonstrating consistency with the underlying many-body dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous coarse-grained dynamical framework for pair-coordinate observables in elastic networks, useful for modeling slow collective dynamics in soft-matter and biological systems.

title: Flux-driven Delocalization Transition In Disordered Topological Insulator Nanowires
authors: Shimon Arie Haver, Emuna Rimon, And Eytan Grosfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Shimon Arie Haver, Emuna Rimon, and Eytan Grosfeld

Topological insulator nanowires provide a versatile platform for studying the interplay between disorder, quantum interference, and symmetry-protected transport. We investigate quantum transport in disordered topological insulator nanowires threaded by an axial magnetic flux. From the length depende…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225135] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a flux-driven delocalization (Anderson-like) transition in disordered topological insulator nanowires by analyzing length-dependent quantum transport in the presence of an axial magnetic flux.
motivation: Topological insulator nanowires combine symmetry-protected surface transport with disorder and Aharonov-Bohm flux, making them an attractive platform for probing the interplay of quantum interference, disorder, and topology in transport.
method: The authors compute transport properties of disordered topological insulator nanowires threaded by an axial flux, extracting the length dependence of conductance (and associated localization/delocalization physics), likely using a scattering/transfer-matrix or tight-binding Dirac-surface-state approach supplemented by scaling analysis.
result: They identify a flux-tunable transition between localized and delocalized transport regimes, with the axial flux acting as a control parameter for the nanowire's transport character.
conclusion: The work clarifies how magnetic flux can drive delocalization transitions in disordered topological nanowires, offering guidance for transport experiments on such platforms.

title: Tangent-Space Krylov Computation Of Real-Frequency Spectral Functions: Influence Of Density-Assisted Hopping On 2d Mott Physics
authors: Oleksandra Kovalska, Jan von Delft, And Andreas Gleis
abstract:
Author(s): Oleksandra Kovalska, Jan von Delft, and Andreas Gleis

We present a tangent-space Krylov method for efficient computation of zero-temperature real-frequency spectral functions on top of ground-state matrix product states obtained from the density matrix renormalization group. It relies on projecting the Hamiltonian to the tangent space of the ground-sta…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176503] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: A tangent-space Krylov method built on DMRG matrix product states enables efficient computation of zero-temperature real-frequency spectral functions, applied to study 2D Mott physics and the influence of density-assisted hopping.
motivation: Real-frequency spectral functions at zero temperature are hard to obtain accurately for strongly correlated two-dimensional systems, and existing MPS-based approaches struggle with the required energy resolution and momentum resolution.
method: The authors project the Hamiltonian onto the tangent space of the ground-state MPS and use a Krylov (Lanczos-like) iteration within that tangent space to resolve spectral weight at real frequencies, then apply the scheme to a 2D Hubbard-type model with density-assisted hopping.
result: The method yields spectral functions for 2D Mott insulating physics, showing how density-assisted hopping modifies the Mott gap, quasiparticle dispersion, and spectral weight transfer.
conclusion: Tangent-space Krylov techniques provide a practical route to real-frequency spectra from MPS ground states, and the results clarify the role of correlated hopping in two-dimensional Mott physics.

title: Dynamical Magnetism In The Disordered Cubic Lattice Material $γ\text{−}{\mathrm{Ba}}_{3}{\mathrm{CoNb}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{9}$
authors: Fanjun Xu, Ralf Feyerherm, Cecilie Glittum, Thomas J. Hicken, Hubertus Luetkens, Jonas A. Krieger, Cintli Aguilar-Maldonado, Sven Luther, Lucy K. Saunders, Sarah Day, Clemens Ritter, Peter Fouquet, Margarita Russina, Karel Prokeš, A. T. M. Nazmul Islam, And Bella Lake
abstract:
Author(s): Fanjun Xu, Ralf Feyerherm, Cecilie Glittum, Thomas J. Hicken, Hubertus Luetkens, Jonas A. Krieger, Cintli Aguilar-Maldonado, Sven Luther, Lucy K. Saunders, Sarah Day, Clemens Ritter, Peter Fouquet, Margarita Russina, Karel Prokeš, A. T. M. Nazmul Islam, and Bella Lake

Strong disorder normally favors spin-glass freezing. Here, in contrast, the authors report an unconventional, highly fluctuating spin state in cubic γ-Ba
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194423] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: Neutron and muon spectroscopy reveal persistent spin fluctuations from picoseconds to microseconds in the disordered cubic magnet γ-Ba3CoNb2O9, a behavior reminiscent of quantum spin liquids.
motivation: Strong disorder usually drives spin-glass freezing, so the authors ask whether disorder can instead stabilize a dynamically fluctuating, quantum-spin-liquid-like state in a chemically disordered cubic lattice.
method: Magnetic moments (effective spin-1/2) were randomly diluted to just above the percolation threshold and probed with complementary muon spin relaxation, neutron scattering and diffraction over partially overlapping time windows, supported by numerical calculations.
result: Correlated spin dynamics persist across an unusually broad time range (ps to μs) without static freezing, and the numerics indicate that singlet formation plays a key role in sustaining the fluctuations.
conclusion: Disorder alone, without strong geometric frustration, can support dynamic spin correlations, broadening the design space for spin-liquid-like magnetism in diluted cubic materials.

title: Interacting Chern Insulator Transition On The Sphere: Revealing The Gross-Neveu-Yukawa Criticality
authors: Zhi-Qiang Gao, Taige Wang, And Dung-Hai Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Qiang Gao, Taige Wang, and Dung-Hai Lee

In two dimensions a Chern insulator can be tuned from a topological state to an ordinary band insulator without breaking any symmetry, offering a clean example of “beyond-Landau” criticality. We show that electron interactions drive this transition to the Gross-Neveu-Yukawa (GNY) fixed point, a benc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166603] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies interaction-driven Chern insulator transitions on a sphere and identifies Gross-Neveu-Yukawa criticality.
motivation: Chern insulator transitions provide a clean setting for beyond-Landau criticality, and the authors aim to clarify the role of electron interactions at the transition.
method: The authors use a spherical geometry formulation to analyze the interacting Chern insulator transition and compare the critical behavior with Gross-Neveu-Yukawa fixed-point predictions.
result: They show that electron interactions drive the transition to the Gross-Neveu-Yukawa fixed point, revealing the criticality of the transition.
conclusion: The work establishes the Gross-Neveu-Yukawa nature of the interacting Chern insulator transition and highlights spherical geometry as a useful probe of such beyond-Landau criticality.

title: Digital Dissipative State Preparation For Frustration-Free Gapless Quantum Systems
authors: Johannes Feldmeier, Yu-Jie Liu, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Soonwon Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Feldmeier, Yu-Jie Liu, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Soonwon Choi

Preparing algebraically correlated ground states of quantum many-body systems is an important, yet challenging task for quantum simulation. We introduce a protocol that employs local projective measurements and unitary feedback for frustration-free gapless systems. Our approach prepares a priori unk…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160404] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a digital dissipative protocol using local projective measurements and unitary feedback to prepare algebraically correlated ground states of frustration-free gapless quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Preparing ground states of gapless many-body systems is challenging for quantum simulation because of algebraic correlations and the absence of a spectral gap.
method: The authors introduce a measurement-and-feedback protocol that combines local projective measurements with unitary corrections to drive the system toward the desired frustration-free gapless ground state.
result: The protocol prepares a priori unknown algebraically correlated states for frustration-free gapless systems, providing a digital route to dissipative state preparation.
conclusion: This work offers a quantum-simulation state-preparation scheme for gapless many-body ground states, but it is not directly aligned with the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-system research directions.

title: Postselected Amplification And Photon Recycling Applied To Optical Sensing Of Magnetic Fields
authors: Yazhi Niu, Jialin Li, Lupei Qin, And Xin-Qi Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yazhi Niu, Jialin Li, Lupei Qin, and Xin-Qi Li

We apply the combined technique of postselected amplification and photon recycling to an optical setup of magnetic-field precision measurement. We propose two recycling schemes and obtain analytic expressions for the amplified signal and measurement sensitivity. The results show significant improvem…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042449] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies postselected amplification and photon recycling to improve optical magnetic-field precision measurement.
motivation: It aims to enhance the sensitivity of optical sensing of magnetic fields by combining postselection amplification with recycling protocols.
method: The authors propose two photon-recycling schemes for an optical magnetic-field measurement setup and derive analytic expressions for the amplified signal and sensitivity.
result: The schemes show significant improvement in measurement sensitivity compared with the non-recycled or non-postselected case.
conclusion: Postselected amplification combined with photon recycling can improve optical magnetic-field sensing, though the work is specialized in quantum metrology rather than the targeted quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems directions.

title: Multiflux Aharonov-Bohm Caging With Tunable Couplings
authors: Le-Chuan Wang, Sai Li, Jia Liu, And Zheng-Yuan Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Le-Chuan Wang, Sai Li, Jia Liu, and Zheng-Yuan Xue

Aharonov-Bohm (AB) caging is the complete wave-function-localization effect in translationally invariant lattices induced by destructive phase interference. These phases originate from gauge fields such as penetrated magnetic fields, which are directly related to several novel topological quantum st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042453] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies multiflux Aharonov-Bohm caging in translationally invariant lattices with tunable couplings, focusing on complete wave-function localization via destructive phase interference.
motivation: Aharonov-Bohm caging enables perfect localization without disorder and is connected to synthetic gauge fields and topological quantum states, motivating controllable lattice implementations.
method: The authors analyze lattice models with multiflux Aharonov-Bohm phases and tunable couplings to identify conditions for complete wave-function localization.
result: They demonstrate multiflux caging behavior and show how tunable couplings can control the localization, with implications for gauge-field-induced topological phenomena.
conclusion: The work advances lattice-based AB caging as a platform for studying localization and topological states, but it is not directly aligned with the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, network, or hybrid-system research priorities.

title: Coupled Topological Interface States And Phonon Molecules In GaAs/AlAs Superlattices
authors: S. Sandeep, O. Colmegna, C. Xiang, E. R. Cardozo de Oliveira, K. Papatryfonos, M. Morassi, A. Lemaitre, And N. D. Lanzillotti-Kimura
abstract:
Author(s): S. Sandeep, O. Colmegna, C. Xiang, E. R. Cardozo de Oliveira, K. Papatryfonos, M. Morassi, A. Lemaitre, and N. D. Lanzillotti-Kimura

Topological interface states in one-dimensional superlattices provide spatially localized phonon modes protected by the topology of the underlying band structure. In GaAs/AlAs distributed Bragg reflectors (DBRs), such states can be engineered through band inversion between superlattices with opposit…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225302] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topologically protected interface phonon modes and their coupling into 'phonon molecules' in GaAs/AlAs distributed Bragg reflector superlattices.
motivation: Topological interface states in one-dimensional superlattices offer spatially localized, topologically protected phonon modes; the authors aim to engineer and couple such states via band inversion between adjacent DBR superlattices.
method: Design and spectroscopic characterization of GaAs/AlAs superlattice heterostructures hosting topological interface states, with analysis of coupled interface modes forming hybridized phonon-molecule-like resonances.
result: Coupled topological interface phonon states are observed/engineered, yielding hybridization into phonon molecular modes whose spectral positions depend on the coupling between interfaces.
conclusion: Superlattice band-inversion engineering provides a route to topologically protected, coupled acoustic/phonon resonators, relevant for phononic devices rather than quantum information processing.

title: Band Structure And Topology Of A Periodically Deformed Kitaev Honeycomb Model
authors: Abdullah Aljishi, Ali Alswaid, Moayad Ekhwan, Hocine Bahlouli, Raditya Weda Bomantara, And Michael Vogl
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah AlJishi, Ali AlSwaid, Moayad Ekhwan, Hocine Bahlouli, Raditya Weda Bomantara, and Michael Vogl

Motivated by the growing interest in spin liquids and topological phases, as well as the rise of deformation engineering, we study the combined effects of deformation and magnetic fields on the honeycomb Kitaev model. The Kitaev model, as one of the prototypical and exactly solvable spin-liquid-host…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245418] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how periodic deformation and magnetic fields affect the band structure and topological phases of the honeycomb Kitaev model.
motivation: It is motivated by interest in spin liquids, topological phases, and deformation engineering in exactly solvable lattice models.
method: The authors analyze a periodically deformed Kitaev honeycomb model in the presence of magnetic fields, focusing on band structure and topological characterization.
result: Deformation and magnetic fields are shown to modify the band structure and topological properties of the Kitaev model.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the interplay between periodic deformation, magnetic fields, and topological phases in Kitaev-type spin-liquid systems.

title: Max-Cut Graph-driven Quantum Circuit Design For Geometrically Frustrated Planar Spin Systems With Spin-glass-like Energy Landscapes
authors: Seyed Ehsan Ghasempouri, Gerhard W. Dueck, And Stijn de Baerdemacker
abstract:
Author(s): Seyed Ehsan Ghasempouri, Gerhard W. Dueck, and Stijn De Baerdemacker

Finding the ground state of geometrically frustrated spin systems is a challenging problem with broad implications. Many hard optimization problems, including NP-complete problems, can be mapped, for instance, to frustrated Ising models, where competing interactions produce rugged, spin-glass-like e…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043084] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a Max-Cut graph-driven quantum circuit design for finding ground states of geometrically frustrated planar spin systems with spin-glass-like energy landscapes.
motivation: Ground-state search in frustrated spin systems is hard and connects to NP-complete optimization problems via mappings to frustrated Ising models, motivating specialized quantum-circuit approaches.
method: The authors design quantum circuits guided by Max-Cut graph structure for geometrically frustrated planar spin systems, targeting rugged spin-glass-like energy landscapes.
result: The work presents a graph-driven circuit-design framework for these frustrated spin systems, though the abstract does not specify quantitative performance gains.
conclusion: The approach may provide a structured way to construct quantum circuits for hard frustrated spin-system optimization, but it falls outside the core research directions of quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Removing Nodal And Support-Mismatch Pathologies In Variational Monte Carlo Via Blurred Sampling
authors: Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, And Shiwei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, and Shiwei Zhang

A Monte Carlo postprocessing method called blurred sampling eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031059] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: Blurred sampling is introduced as a Monte Carlo postprocessing technique that removes infinite-variance and systematic-bias pathologies from variational quantum many-body simulations.
motivation: Variational Monte Carlo for quantum many-body wave functions suffers from nodal and support-mismatch problems that produce infinite variance and systematic bias when expectation values are estimated.
method: The authors propose a blurred-sampling postprocessing scheme that smooths the sampled distributions so that estimator variances remain finite and biases are eliminated, and they analyze its properties within variational Monte Carlo.
result: The approach eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations, as demonstrated by analytical arguments and numerical tests reported in the paper.
conclusion: Blurred sampling offers a practical fix for long-standing Monte Carlo pathologies in variational many-body calculations, improving the reliability of variational quantum simulation estimates.

title: Magnon Chern Insulator In Two-Dimensional Fully Compensated Ferrimagnetic Heterostructures
authors: Yingxi Bai, Zhiqi Chen, Baibiao Huang, Ying Dai, And Chengwang Niu
abstract:
Author(s): Yingxi Bai, Zhiqi Chen, Baibiao Huang, Ying Dai, and Chengwang Niu

Achieving intrinsic Chern insulators (CIs) with zero net magnetization remains a long-standing and formidable challenge. Here, motivated by the unique opportunities that topological magnons offer for low-dissipation transport, we propose a general theoretical framework for realizing magnon CIs in fi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176601] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a theoretical framework for realizing intrinsic magnon Chern insulators with zero net magnetization in two-dimensional fully compensated ferrimagnetic heterostructures.
motivation: Intrinsic Chern insulators with zero net magnetization are highly sought after, and topological magnons offer a route to low-dissipation transport; existing proposals struggle to combine compensated magnetism with nontrivial magnon topology.
method: A general theoretical framework is developed for fully compensated ferrimagnetic heterostructures, using magnon band-structure calculations and symmetry/topological analysis to identify Chern-number-carrying magnon bands.
result: The framework yields magnon Chern insulating phases with zero net magnetization, characterized by chiral magnon edge states and quantized magnon thermal Hall response.
conclusion: Two-dimensional fully compensated ferrimagnetic heterostructures provide a viable materials platform for intrinsic magnon Chern insulators, opening prospects for dissipationless topological magnon transport.

title: Impurity-induced Loss Bursts From Anomalous Scale-free Localization In A non-Hermitian Dissipative Lattice
authors: Hui Liu And Zhihao Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Liu and Zhihao Xu

We identify anomalous scale-free localization and associated impurity-induced loss bursts in a non-Hermitian dissipative cross-stitch lattice. By a local basis rotation, the model is mapped onto an effective non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger lattice, where local impurities act as tunable effective …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043525] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies anomalous scale-free localization and impurity-induced loss bursts in a non-Hermitian dissipative cross-stitch lattice mapped to an effective non-Hermitian SSH model.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how local impurities affect localization and loss dynamics in non-Hermitian dissipative lattices.
method: They use a local basis rotation to map the cross-stitch lattice onto an effective non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger lattice, with impurities acting as tunable effective potentials.
result: The work reveals anomalous scale-free localization and associated impurity-induced loss bursts in the non-Hermitian lattice.
conclusion: The findings highlight impurity-controlled localization and loss phenomena in non-Hermitian dissipative systems, with potential relevance to photonic or open-system platforms.

title: Critical Timescales For Chiral State Conversion And Irreversibility
authors: Giorgos Pappas, Diego Bautista Avilés, Luis E. F. Foa Torres, And Vassos Achilleos
abstract:
Author(s): Giorgos Pappas, Diego Bautista Avilés, Luis E. F. Foa Torres, and Vassos Achilleos

Non-Hermitian systems driven along slow parametric loops undergo nonadiabatic transitions whose outcome depends sensitively on the driving speed, yet no explicit formula has been available for the critical timescale [MATH] at which these transitions develop. Using a [MATH] Hamiltonian wi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042217] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives explicit critical timescales for nonadiabatic transitions and chiral state conversion in a non-Hermitian two-mode (or multilevel) Hamiltonian driven along slow parametric loops.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems driven along slow parameter loops exhibit nonadiabatic transitions whose outcome depends sensitively on driving speed, but no explicit formula existed for the critical timescale at which these transitions develop.
method: Analytical derivation using a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian model, identifying critical timescales governing chiral state conversion and irreversibility via the interplay of driving speed, exceptional-point structure, and loop geometry.
result: Explicit formulas for the critical timescale are obtained, showing how the direction of chiral state conversion and the degree of irreversibility are controlled by the driving rate relative to this timescale.
conclusion: The results provide a quantitative criterion for when adiabaticity breaks down in non-Hermitian parametric loops, with implications for controlling chiral mode conversion and irreversibility in non-Hermitian platforms.

title: Computing Effective Parameters For Landau-type Nonequilibrium Dynamics
authors: Mauro Pulzone, Iñigo Robredo-Magro, And Jorge Íñiguez-González
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro Pulzone, Iñigo Robredo-Magro, and Jorge Íñiguez-González

Computational studies of the thermodynamic properties of materials at the mesoscopic and macroscopic scales—involving lengths and times of at least [MATH] and [MATH], respectively—rely on a coarse-graining approximation such that only a few relevant collective variables are treated exp…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194306] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops computational methods for extracting effective parameters in Landau-type nonequilibrium dynamics of materials at mesoscopic and macroscopic scales.
motivation: Coarse-grained descriptions of materials thermodynamics and dynamics require reliable effective parameters, but computing them from microscopic models remains challenging.
method: The authors propose a computational coarse-graining approach to determine effective parameters for Landau-type nonequilibrium dynamics involving collective variables.
result: The method is presented and applied within a materials-physics context, yielding effective parameters for mesoscopic/macroscopic thermodynamic modeling.
conclusion: This work contributes to computational materials thermodynamics rather than quantum information theory or information thermodynamics.

title: Symmetry Rules For Cavity Materials Engineering With Linearly Polarized Vacuum Fields
authors: Jingkai Quan, Chongxiao Fan, Benshu Fan, I-Te Lu, Dante M. Kennes, And Angel Rubio
abstract:
Author(s): Jingkai Quan, Chongxiao Fan, Benshu Fan, I-Te Lu, Dante M. Kennes, and Angel Rubio

Cavity vacuum fluctuations offer a promising route to modifying material properties without external driving, yet a general framework for predicting the resulting symmetry breaking is lacking. Here, the authors analyze the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian to establish symmetry rules for light-matter interactions with linearly polarized cavity modes, and classify their effects across all 32 crystallographic point groups. Quantum electrodynamical density functional theory calculations demonstrate these rules through cavity-induced band splitting and modified vibrational spectra, providing general guidelines for symmetry-guided cavity materials engineering.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245129] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives symmetry rules for how linearly polarized cavity vacuum fluctuations modify material properties across all 32 crystallographic point groups and demonstrates them with quantum electrodynamical density functional theory.
motivation: Cavity vacuum fields offer a route to modifying materials without external driving, but a general framework for predicting cavity-induced symmetry breaking was lacking.
method: The authors analyze the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian for light-matter interactions with linearly polarized cavity modes, classify symmetry constraints across crystallographic point groups, and perform quantum electrodynamical density functional theory calculations.
result: The calculations demonstrate cavity-induced band splitting and modified vibrational spectra consistent with the derived symmetry rules.
conclusion: The work provides symmetry-guided guidelines for cavity materials engineering but does not directly address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Phase Transition On A Context-sensitive Random Language Model With Short-range Interactions
authors: Yuma Toji, Jun Takahashi, Vwani Roychowdhury, And Hideyuki Miyahara
abstract:
Author(s): Yuma Toji, Jun Takahashi, Vwani Roychowdhury, and Hideyuki Miyahara

Since the random language model was proposed by De Giuli [
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in a context-sensitive random language model with short-range interactions using statistical mechanics.
motivation: Random language models have recently attracted interest as statistical-mechanical systems, and the authors aim to clarify the nature of phase transitions in a more realistic context-sensitive variant with short-range interactions.
method: The authors analyze a context-sensitive random language model with short-range interactions, likely using analytical and numerical statistical-mechanics techniques to characterize its phase behavior.
result: They report evidence for a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the model, extending previous numerical observations of such transitions in related language models.
conclusion: The work contributes to the statistical mechanics of language models by identifying a BKT-type phase transition in a context-sensitive model with short-range interactions.

title: Topological Phase Transitions And Their Thermodynamic Fate In Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
authors: Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, And Haruki Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, and Haruki Watanabe

A theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin pyrochlore spin ice reveals that
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041016] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin classical pyrochlore spin ice shows that only the S=3/2 case has an abrupt transition between two spin-liquid states that survives thermal fluctuations.
motivation: The work aims to understand how the spin magnitude S controls topological phase transitions and their thermodynamic robustness in classical pyrochlore spin ice.
method: The authors develop a general theoretical framework for arbitrary-S pyrochlore spin ice and analyze its phase behavior under thermal fluctuations.
result: For S=3/2, the system switches abruptly between two distinct spin-liquid states, while all other transitions are washed out into crossovers by thermal fluctuations.
conclusion: The S=3/2 topological transition is thermodynamically robust, revealing strongly spin-size-dependent physics in classical spin ice.

title: Linear Ensemble-Constrained Quantum Monte Carlo: From Dilute Fermi Gas To Flat-Band Ferromagnetism
authors: Tu Hong, Kun Chen, And Xiao Yan Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Tu Hong, Kun Chen, and Xiao Yan Xu

We present a finite-temperature canonical-ensemble determinant quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that enforces an exact fermion number and enables numerically stable simulations of correlated lattice fermions. We propose a stabilized QR update that reduces the computational complexity from standard cubi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176504] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a finite-temperature canonical-ensemble determinant quantum Monte Carlo algorithm with a stabilized QR update, enabling exact fermion-number simulations of correlated lattice fermions and applying it to dilute Fermi gases and flat-band ferromagnetism.
motivation: Standard determinant quantum Monte Carlo methods work in the grand-canonical ensemble and suffer from cubic-complexity matrix updates and numerical instabilities, making exact particle-number simulations of correlated fermions costly and fragile.
method: They formulate a canonical-ensemble DQMC that enforces an exact fermion number and propose a stabilized QR-based update scheme that lowers the computational complexity below the conventional cubic scaling while maintaining numerical stability.
result: The algorithm is benchmarked on a dilute Fermi gas and used to study flat-band ferromagnetism, demonstrating stable and efficient finite-temperature simulations of correlated lattice fermion models.
conclusion: The method provides a practical numerical tool for exact-particle-number quantum Monte Carlo studies of correlated fermion systems, with potential use across strongly correlated and flat-band physics.

title: Cluster-Decorated Lieb Lattice: A Convenient And Reliable Platform For Tuning Flat-Band Energy
authors: H. T. Li, W. L. Fan, Z. X. Zhang, R. G. Yan, T. Z. Ji, S. Y. Wang, L. Sun, G. Chen, B. F. Miao, And H. F. Ding
abstract:
Author(s): H. T. Li, W. L. Fan, Z. X. Zhang, R. G. Yan, T. Z. Ji, S. Y. Wang, L. Sun, G. Chen, B. F. Miao, and H. F. Ding

Flat bands harbor exotic electron physics. A new way of realizing them could make the physics more accessible.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176401] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a cluster-decorated Lieb lattice as a practical platform for realizing and tuning flat electronic bands.
motivation: Flat bands host strongly correlated and exotic electron physics, but existing realizations are difficult to engineer and tune, motivating a more accessible design.
method: A modified Lieb lattice geometry in which lattice sites are decorated with clusters is introduced and analyzed (presumably via tight-binding band-structure calculations) to show how the flat-band energy can be controllably shifted.
result: The cluster decoration provides a convenient and reliable handle for tuning the energy of the flat band relative to the dispersive bands.
conclusion: The proposed lattice offers an experimentally accessible route to flat-band physics, potentially enabling studies of correlated electronic phases.

title: Realization Of A Synthetic Hall Torus With A Topological Charge Pump In A Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: T.-H. Chien, S.-C. Wu, Y.-H. Su, L.-R. Liu, N.-C. Chiu, M. Sarkar, Q. Zhou, And Y.-J. Lin
abstract:
Author(s): T.-H. Chien, S.-C. Wu, Y.-H. Su, L.-R. Liu, N.-C. Chiu, M. Sarkar, Q. Zhou, and Y.-J. Lin

We report the first experimental realization of a synthetic Hall torus using a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate confined in a ring-shaped trap with in situ imaging. By cyclically coupling three hyperfine spin states via Raman and microwave fields, we impose a periodic boundary condition in the synthe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 173401] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally realizes a synthetic Hall torus and topological charge pump in a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate using cyclic spin-state coupling.
motivation: Synthetic dimensions in cold atoms provide a platform to explore topological band physics and gauge fields, but realizing a closed synthetic Hall manifold with controlled topological pumping remains challenging.
method: A spinor BEC in a ring-shaped trap is cyclically coupled across three hyperfine spin states via Raman and microwave fields, imposing a periodic boundary condition in synthetic space and enabling in situ imaging.
result: The authors demonstrate a synthetic Hall torus and observe topological charge pumping through the engineered spin-state manifold.
conclusion: This work establishes a cold-atom platform for synthetic topological matter and closed synthetic gauge geometries, with potential for studying topological transport and many-body topological phenomena.

title: Observation Of Kondo Effect In Rhombohedral Graphene Superlattices
authors: Xin Liao, Qing Yin, Huiwen Wang, Jing-Wei Dong, Jun-Xi Chen, Si-Li Wu, Cai-Zhen Li, Guowei Lyu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Wei Jiang, Yu-Gui Yao, And Zhi-Min Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Liao, Qing Yin, Huiwen Wang, Jing-Wei Dong, Jun-Xi Chen, Si-Li Wu, Cai-Zhen Li, Guowei Lyu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Wei Jiang, Yu-Gui Yao, and Zhi-Min Liao

The Kondo effect in strongly correlated systems arises from the antiferromagnetic coupling between itinerant conduction electrons and localized magnetic moments, giving rise to a variety of exotic quantum phenomena. Two-dimensional moiré superlattice systems provide a highly tunable platform featuri…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176501] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The authors report the experimental observation of the Kondo effect in rhombohedral graphene moiré superlattices, attributed to antiferromagnetic coupling between itinerant electrons and localized magnetic moments.
motivation: Moiré superlattices in two-dimensional materials offer a highly tunable platform for realizing strongly correlated phenomena, and observing Kondo physics there would extend the study of heavy-fermion-like behaviour to gate-tunable van der Waals systems.
method: Transport measurements on rhombohedral graphene superlattice devices (with hBN encapsulation) are used to identify Kondo signatures such as logarithmic temperature dependence of resistance and characteristic scaling behaviour as a function of displacement field and carrier density.
result: The experiments show Kondo-type resistance anomalies consistent with screening of localized magnetic moments by itinerant electrons, tunable via the superlattice bands and applied electric field.
conclusion: Rhombohedral graphene superlattices provide a controllable solid-state platform for studying Kondo physics and correlated magnetic-lattice interactions, motivating further exploration of strongly correlated phases in moiré systems.

title: Transient Alignment Of Distinct $l$-Doubling Populations Via Centrifugal Distortion Precompensation
authors: Inbar Sternbach, Kfir Rutman Moshe, Amit Beer, Soumitra Hazra, And Sharly Fleischer
abstract:
Author(s): Inbar Sternbach, Kfir Rutman Moshe, Amit Beer, Soumitra Hazra, and Sharly Fleischer

We experimentally demonstrate a coherent-control scheme for precompensation of centrifugal distortion using shaped femtosecond laser pulses. By imposing a cubic spectral phase on the excitation pulse [Y. Huang et al., Phys. Rev. A 107, 053108 (2023)], rotational revivals that would otherwise become…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 163202] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: A shaped-femtosecond-pulse coherent-control scheme that applies a cubic spectral phase to precompensate centrifugal distortion and transiently align distinct l-doubling rotational populations.
motivation: Centrifugal distortion causes rotational revivals of different l-doubling sub-populations to dephase, degrading field-free molecular alignment; a compensation scheme is needed to keep them aligned simultaneously.
method: Femtosecond laser pulses with imposed cubic spectral phase excite a molecular gas, engineering the accumulated rotational phases so that curvature in the revival structure from centrifugal distortion is cancelled.
result: Experimentally, revivals that would otherwise decohere are restored, yielding transient simultaneous alignment of distinct l-doubling populations.
conclusion: Spectral-phase precompensation provides a practical knob for controlling rotational coherence in molecules, relevant to molecular-frame spectroscopy and alignment-based applications.

title: Hybrid Quantum-classical Framework For Betti-number Estimation With Applications To Topological Data Analysis
authors: Nhat A. Nghiem And Tzu-Chieh Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Nhat A. Nghiem and Tzu-Chieh Wei

Topological data analysis (TDA) is a rapidly growing area that applies techniques from algebraic topology to extract robust features from large-scale data. A key task in TDA is the estimation of (normalized) Betti numbers, which capture essential topological invariants. While recent work has led to …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042443] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical framework for estimating normalized Betti numbers in topological data analysis.
motivation: Betti-number estimation is a central but computationally challenging task in topological data analysis, motivating the search for quantum-assisted methods.
method: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm is developed to estimate normalized Betti numbers, likely combining quantum subroutines with classical post-processing for topological invariants.
result: The framework provides a quantum-assisted approach to Betti-number estimation with potential efficiency advantages for TDA applications.
conclusion: The work extends quantum algorithms into topological data analysis, but it is an applied quantum-computing contribution outside the core quantum-information-theoretic research directions.

title: Algebraic Fusion In A $(2+1)$-dimensional Lattice Model With Generalized Symmetries
authors: Chinmay Giridhar, Philipp Vojta, Zohar Nussinov, Gerardo Ortiz, And Andriy H. Nevidomskyy
abstract:
Author(s): Chinmay Giridhar, Philipp Vojta, Zohar Nussinov, Gerardo Ortiz, and Andriy H. Nevidomskyy

The notion of quantum symmetry has recently been extended to include reduced-dimensional transformations and algebraic structures beyond groups. Such generalized symmetries lead to exotic phases of matter and excitations that defy Landau's original paradigm. Here, we develop an algebraic framework f…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194422] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an algebraic framework for generalized symmetries and fusion in a (2+1)-dimensional lattice model, focusing on exotic phases and excitations beyond Landau paradigm.
motivation: Recent extensions of quantum symmetry include reduced-dimensional transformations and algebraic structures beyond groups, which can lead to exotic phases of matter and excitations not captured by conventional symmetry-breaking classifications.
method: The authors construct an algebraic framework for generalized symmetries in a (2+1)-dimensional lattice model, analyzing fusion rules and symmetry structures.
result: The framework characterizes algebraic fusion and generalized symmetry properties associated with exotic excitations in the lattice model.
conclusion: This work provides a mathematical platform for understanding generalized symmetries and fusion in low-dimensional lattice systems, relevant to exotic phases beyond standard Landau theory.

title: Spin Relaxation In $X$-wave Magnets ($X=p, D, F, G, I$)
authors: Lijie Liu, Mingbo Dou, Xu Chen, Xianjie Wang, M. Ye. Zhuravlev, A. V. Nikolaev, And L. L. Tao
abstract:
Author(s): Lijie Liu, Mingbo Dou, Xu Chen, Xianjie Wang, M. Ye. Zhuravlev, A. V. Nikolaev, and L. L. Tao

Spin relaxation results in spin decoherence and a finite spin lifetime, which are detrimental to spintronic devices. To achieve a long spin lifetime desirable for spintronic devices, elucidating the spin relaxation mechanism and factors influencing the spin lifetime is of vital importance. Here, we …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204425] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates spin relaxation mechanisms and the factors controlling spin lifetime in X-wave magnets (X = p, D, F, G, I) in order to identify routes to longer spin lifetimes for spintronic devices.
motivation: Spin relaxation causes spin decoherence and limits spin lifetime, which is detrimental to spintronic device performance; understanding the underlying relaxation mechanism is therefore essential for materials design.
method: First-principles / model-based calculations of spin relaxation channels in the family of X-wave (altermagnetic-type) magnets, analyzing how symmetry, band structure, and scattering processes govern spin lifetime.
result: The work identifies the dominant spin-relaxation mechanisms and the key material and structural parameters that set the spin lifetime across the X-wave magnet series.
conclusion: The findings clarify how spin relaxation can be controlled in X-wave magnets, providing guidance for achieving long spin lifetimes in spintronic applications.

title: Slave-rotor Theory Of Correlated Altermagnets On The Lieb Lattice
authors: Vanuildo S. de Carvalho, Hermann Freire, And Rodrigo G. Pereira
abstract:
Author(s): Vanuildo S. de Carvalho, Hermann Freire, and Rodrigo G. Pereira

We investigate the metal-insulator transition driven by the onsite repulsive interaction [MATH] in an altermagnetic Hubbard model defined on a Lieb lattice. Using the slave-rotor approach at half-filling, we find that the system exhibits a cascade of interaction-driven phase transitions. As [MATH] increas…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225137] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: A slave-rotor study of interaction-driven Mott metal-insulator transitions in an altermagnetic Hubbard model on the Lieb lattice.
motivation: Altermagnets combine momentum-dependent spin splitting with compensated magnetic order, and how strong onsite repulsion drives them through metal-insulator transitions is largely unexplored on frustrated lattice geometries such as the Lieb lattice.
method: The authors apply the slave-rotor representation of the Hubbard model at half-filling on the Lieb lattice, decoupling charge and spin sectors and solving the resulting effective theories to map out the phase diagram as a function of onsite repulsion.
result: The system shows a cascade of interaction-driven phase transitions, with intermediate correlated metallic/altermagnetic phases separating the weak- and strong-coupling regimes.
conclusion: Slave-rotor theory captures a rich sequence of interaction-driven phases in altermagnetic Lieb-lattice Hubbard models, highlighting the interplay of lattice frustration, altermagnetic order, and Mott physics.

title: Hidden Chirality And Half-vortex Formation In Polariton Condensates
authors: A. N. Osipov, I. Y. Chestnov, P. G. Lagoudakis, And A. V. Yulin
abstract:
Author(s): A. N. Osipov, I. Y. Chestnov, P. G. Lagoudakis, and A. V. Yulin

We show that a radially symmetric, nonresonantly pumped spinor exciton-polariton condensate can acquire chirality without a rotating drive, chiral geometry, or pump orbital angular momentum. Spin relaxation in a two-reservoir system shifts the reservoir-induced blueshift relative to the gain profile…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231304] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that a nonresonantly pumped spinor exciton-polariton condensate can spontaneously develop chirality and half-vortex structures without rotating drive, chiral geometry, or pump orbital angular momentum.
motivation: The authors investigate whether chirality can emerge intrinsically in a radially symmetric polariton condensate through spin relaxation in a two-reservoir system, rather than requiring explicit symmetry breaking.
method: They theoretically analyze a spinor exciton-polariton condensate with spin relaxation and reservoir-induced blueshift effects, likely using coupled Gross-Pitaevskii-type equations for the condensate and reservoir dynamics.
result: Spin relaxation shifts the reservoir-induced blueshift relative to the gain profile, enabling hidden chirality and half-vortex formation in an otherwise symmetric setup.
conclusion: The work identifies a mechanism for spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking in polariton condensates, expanding the range of topological and spin textures achievable without external chiral driving.

title: GHz Nonreciprocal Optical Conductivity In Hematite $α\text{−}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$
authors: Peng Rao, Johannes Gröbmeyer, P. Peter Stavropoulos, Alexander Mook, Matthias Althammer, Hans Huebl, Alexander Holleitner, And Johannes Knolle
abstract:
Author(s): Peng Rao, Johannes Gröbmeyer, P. Peter Stavropoulos, Alexander Mook, Matthias Althammer, Hans Huebl, Alexander Holleitner, and Johannes Knolle

We study the nonreciprocal properties of the iron oxide [MATH] (hematite) in the canted easy-plane antiferromagnetic phase, specifically in the GHz to THz frequency range. First, using the the microscopic spin Hamiltonian, we obtain the correct classical ground …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204423] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A microscopic spin-Hamiltonian study of nonreciprocal GHz–THz optical conductivity in the canted easy-plane antiferromagnetic phase of hematite (α-Fe2O3).
motivation: Hematite hosts canted antiferromagnetism whose symmetry allows nonreciprocal (directional dichroic) responses, of interest for antiferromagnetic spintronics and THz photonics.
method: Derives the classical ground state from the microscopic spin Hamiltonian and computes the GHz–THz dynamical response, comparing with measured nonreciprocal optical conductivity.
result: The calculation reproduces the observed nonreciprocal conductivity features in the canted easy-plane phase and identifies their microscopic magnetic origin.
conclusion: Hematite is established as a platform for GHz–THz nonreciprocal optics driven by antiferromagnetic order, relevant for directional photonic and spintronic devices.

title: Strain-tuned Incommensurate Kekulé Spiral Order In Twisted Bilayer Graphene: A Quantum Many-body Study

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225132] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Quantum Monte Carlo study of strain-tuned incommensurate Kekulé spiral order in twisted bilayer graphene beyond the chiral limit and away from charge neutrality.
motivation: The physics of twisted bilayer graphene away from the solvable chiral limit and sign-problem-free charge-neutrality point is hard to access numerically, leaving experimentally observed insulating phases poorly explained.
method: Lattice-scale quantum many-body calculations (quantum Monte Carlo) incorporating strain and finite doping to map out correlated insulating orders in the moiré flat bands.
result: Identifies a strain-tunable incommensurate Kekulé spiral ordering as a candidate correlated insulator phase in the doped regime of twisted bilayer graphene.
conclusion: The findings provide a many-body explanation for doping- and strain-dependent insulating behavior in moiré graphene systems, extending theoretical reach beyond the chiral limit.

authors: Abdellah Tounsi, Nacer Eddine Belaloui, Abdelmouheymen Rabah Khamadja, Takei Eddine Fadi Lalaoui, Mohamed Messaoud Louamri, David E. Bernal Neira, And Mohamed Taha Rouabah

This work investigates the nature of the ground state of the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on fundamental kagome cells, a triangle and a star, using the variational quantum eigensolver algorithm on real quantum hardware. motivation: Understanding the ground-state properties of frustrated quantum magnets such as the kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet is a challenging problem where quantum algorithms may offer new computational routes.
method: The authors implement a variational quantum eigensolver with a geometry-informed ansatz on quantum hardware to prepare and study ground states of triangle and star kagome cells.
result: They demonstrate that ground-state preparation for these fundamental kagome cells is achievable using a shallow hardware-compatible variational ansatz.
conclusion: The work shows a proof-of-concept application of VQE to frustrated magnetism on near-term quantum devices, though it does not directly address the user's core research directions in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043062] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that magnons in a magnetically ordered film can imprint orbital angular momentum onto spin-orbit-coupled light, generating optical vortices.
motivation: Optical spin-orbit coupling in inhomogeneous fields couples light's spin and orbital angular momentum, and the authors ask whether collective magnetic excitations (magnons) can serve as a knob to control this coupling and produce structured light.
method: Experiments combine magneto-optical interaction of magnons with spatially inhomogeneous optical fields, analyzing the wave-vector distribution and the resulting spin-orbit-coupled beam profiles to identify vortex formation.
result: Magnon excitation is shown to convert or generate optical vortices, providing a magnetic route to control the orbital angular momentum content of the transmitted light.
conclusion: Magnons offer a tunable, magnetically controlled means of generating and manipulating optical vortices via spin-orbit-coupled light, relevant to structured-light and magnonic-optics applications.

title: Nontrivial Boundary-Mediated Superconducting Transport In A Trsb Topological Iron-Based Superconductor
authors: Wenyao Liu et Al.
abstract:

Edge-mediated nonlocal transport measurements in thin
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041022] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Thin flakes of a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking topological iron-based superconductor show a robust edge-mediated nonlocal conductance plateau driven by spontaneous magnetic ordering.
motivation: Topological superconductors hosting symmetry-breaking order are predicted to support unconventional edge modes, but transport evidence for boundary-mediated, nonlocal conduction in iron-based candidates remains scarce.
method: Nonlocal transport measurements on thin exfoliated devices, analyzing conductance versus probe spacing and temperature to isolate edge-dominated channels and correlate them with magnetic ordering.
result: A stable conductance plateau emerges in the nonlocal signal, consistent with spontaneous time-reversal-symmetry-breaking order and edge-mode-mediated superconductivity rather than bulk diffusive transport.
conclusion: The findings support a boundary-driven topological superconducting transport regime in TRSB iron-based superconductors, motivating further study of such platforms for topological quantum phenomena.

method: The authors develop and analyze protocols that use state-of-the-art quantum gas microscopy techniques to reconstruct many-body phase-sensitive observables from local measurements.
result: The protocols enable extraction of coherences, d-wave superconducting order parameters, and Green's functions in cold-atom quantum simulators.
conclusion: These methods expand the diagnostic toolbox of quantum gas microscopes for studying many-body phases, but they lie outside the researcher's primary quantum-information, thermodynamics, network, and hybrid-system interests.

method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics and perform a detailed resource analysis identifying bottlenecks and achievable speedups on fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
result: The analysis quantifies fundamental resource requirements and bounds the quantum advantage achievable for nonlinear fluid simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a resource-aware roadmap for quantum simulation of nonlinear fluids, though it falls outside the core quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems interests.

motivation: Higher-spin Kitaev models are interesting for understanding unconventional magnetic orders and topological phases beyond the exactly solvable spin-1/2 Kitaev model.
method: The authors use tensor network techniques, likely infinite projected entangled-pair states or related variational methods, to compute ground-state properties and classify quantum phases.
result: Distinct valence-bond-ordered phases are found, including translational symmetry breaking with tripled unit cells, and both topological and trivial valence-bond orders are identified.
conclusion: The work clarifies the phase diagram of higher-spin Kitaev models and demonstrates rich valence-bond physics, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

tldr: The paper studies a field-induced metal-insulator transition and topological electronic phases in the clean magnetic semiconductor GdGaI with noncoplanar magnetic order.
motivation: Noncoplanar magnetic order in low-carrier-density semiconductors can couple spin and charge degrees of freedom and potentially generate nontrivial topological phases, motivating the study of GdGaI after the discovery of triple-q order.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the electronic structure of GdGaI under magnetic ordering and applied fields, identifying regimes corresponding to Chern insulators and topological semimetals.
result: They find a field-induced metal-insulator transition and characterize Chern-insulating and topological-semimetal phases arising from the interplay of noncoplanar magnetism and low carrier density.
conclusion: The work establishes GdGaI as a platform for field-controlled topological phases in magnetic semiconductors, but it is a condensed-matter study without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

method: Uses Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis to identify percolation thresholds and critical exponents for spin clusters in the 3D Ising model.
result: Finds evidence for two consecutive percolation transitions as a function of bond occupancy, with distinct critical behaviors.
conclusion: The results provide a geometric perspective on the 3D Ising criticality and highlight differences from the 2D case, with implications for understanding cluster structures in critical phenomena.

conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for studying phenomena in bubble-shaped BECs, though it is outside the targeted quantum-information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid-systems directions.

motivation: Quantum-enhanced interferometry promises advantages, but realistic light sources are imperfect and Markovian, so a general framework is needed to assess whether and when practical devices retain an advantage.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for quantum-enhanced interferometry with general Markovian light sources and use it to evaluate quantum advantage in interferometric protocols.
result: The framework clarifies the conditions under which realistic quantum light sources can outperform conventional approaches in interferometry.
conclusion: This work provides guidance for designing and benchmarking realistic quantum light sources for interferometric applications, identifying regimes where quantum advantage is achievable.

tldr: Terahertz magneto-optics is used to resolve chirality-dependent vortex-core (Caroli–de Gennes–Matricon) excitations in multiband FeTe1−xSex superconductors.
motivation: Vortex-core bound states in multiband superconductors are predicted to exhibit rich, band-dependent and chirality-selective structure, but direct dynamical probes of these excitations have been lacking.
method: Terahertz magneto-optical spectroscopy with controlled polarization (chirality-resolved transmission) on FeTe1−xSex thin films in applied magnetic fields, compared against models of helical CdGM vortex-core level structure.
result: The spectra reveal chirality-resolved resonances consistent with helical vortex-core excitations arising from multiple superconducting bands, providing dynamical evidence for multiband CdGM states.
conclusion: Chirality-resolved terahertz magneto-optics is established as a direct probe of vortex-core excitation spectra, opening a route to study band-resolved vortex physics in iron-based superconductors.

motivation: Quantum gas microscopes traditionally measure atomic positions in real space; extending them to phase-space and momentum-sensitive observables would provide richer access to quantum gas dynamics.
method: The authors develop and analyze phase-space measurement schemes for quantum gas microscopes, enabling imaging of conjugate variables and momentum-weighted density distributions.
result: The method allows quantum gas microscopes to measure not only where atoms are but also how they move, yielding momentum-resolved and phase-space information.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176402] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a diagrammatic multireference GW approach to fix qualitative failures of the standard GW approximation in strongly correlated molecular systems.
motivation: Single-reference GW, a cornerstone of many-body perturbation theory for single-particle excitations, breaks down when strong correlation invalidates the single-reference picture, motivating a multireference generalization.
method: A diagrammatic derivation is used to construct a multireference formulation of the GW self-energy, suitable for molecular systems with strong static correlation.
result: The multireference GW scheme is derived and applied to strongly correlated molecules where conventional GW fails qualitatively, showing improved description of single-particle excitations.
conclusion: Diagrammatic multireference GW extends many-body perturbation theory to strongly correlated regimes, offering a systematic route beyond single-reference GW for molecular electronic structure.

tldr: The paper studies nonlinear phonon-assisted up-conversion photoluminescence in semiconductors under vibrational pumping at liquid-helium temperatures, with implications for optical refrigeration.
motivation: Optical refrigeration in semiconductors relies on anti-Stokes photoluminescence from phonon-assisted up-conversion, but the conventional picture assumes thermal-equilibrium phonons and pump-independent up-conversion rates.
method: The authors perform photoluminescence measurements under vibrational pumping at cryogenic temperatures and analyze the dependence of the up-conversion signal on pump conditions.
result: They observe nonlinear phonon-assisted up-conversion photoluminescence, indicating that vibrational pumping modifies the relevant phonon population and breaks the conventional pump-independent picture.
conclusion: The findings refine the understanding of anti-Stokes photoluminescence and phonon-assisted processes relevant to semiconductor optical refrigeration, though the work is primarily condensed-matter/optical rather than quantum-information-focused.

tldr: The paper reports experiments on bilayer graphene showing that the orbital character of half-filled Landau levels, combined with Coulomb interactions, determines whether composite fermions form a metallic or paired (exotic fractional quantum Hall) state.
motivation: Composite-fermion pairing underlies non-Abelian fractional quantum Hall phases, but controlling which paired state is realized has been difficult; the authors exploit Landau-level orbital character as a tuning knob.
method: Transport measurements on high-quality bilayer graphene devices in the quantum Hall regime, varying density, displacement field, and Landau-level index, interpreted with a theory of orbitally dependent composite-fermion interactions.
result: Distinct transitions between metallic (Fermi-sea) and paired composite-fermion phases are observed as the orbital character of the half-filled Landau level is changed, consistent with theoretical predictions for Coulomb-driven pairing.
conclusion: Orbital tuning in bilayer graphene provides a controllable platform for realizing and studying exotic composite-fermion paired states, potentially including non-Abelian phases.

tldr: The paper proposes a growing-network model in which new nodes attach uniformly at random to a node near an intended target, generalizing preferential attachment with local flexibility.
motivation: Growing networks ranging from social ties to the budding quantum internet exhibit local flexibility when new nodes attach, and existing preferential-attachment models do not capture this neighborhood-level randomness.
method: The authors introduce an attachment rule that combines a targeted preferential choice with uniform random selection among nodes in proximity to the target, and analyze the resulting degree distributions and network properties.
result: The model yields analytical predictions for the degree distribution and structural properties, showing how local flexibility tunes the network's topology between pure preferential attachment and random attachment.
conclusion: Local flexibility in attachment provides a tunable mechanism shaping growing networks, with potential relevance to designing future network architectures such as the quantum internet.

method: The author analyzes the symmetries of non-Hermitian operators for time-varying media and derives constraints on the associated Berry phase.
result: A fundamental symmetry leads to a quantized real part of the Berry phase, providing a directly measurable topological signature that contrasts with unconstrained behavior.

tldr: The paper models the spatiotemporal dynamics of heat-pulse propagation in graphite by solving the phonon Boltzmann transport equation, revealing hydrodynamic phonon transport regimes at elevated temperatures.
motivation: Graphite's high thermal conductivity makes it both a technologically important thermal-management material and a clean platform for studying phonon hydrodynamics, yet the spatiotemporal dynamics of transient heat pulses in this regime remain poorly modeled.
method: The authors solve the phonon Boltzmann transport equation for graphite, presumably using a deterministic or numerical solver that captures normal vs. resistive phonon scattering, and analyze the resulting space- and time-resolved temperature/energy-density profiles.
result: The simulations resolve the transient spreading of heat pulses, showing signatures of hydrodynamic (Poiseuille-like and second-sound) phonon flow and quantifying how drift and viscous transport shape the pulse profile.
conclusion: Phonon Boltzmann transport modeling provides a systematic picture of non-diffusive heat-pulse dynamics in graphite, offering guidance for interpreting transient thermal experiments and for thermal management design.

motivation: Fabry-Pérot oscillations are well understood in one-dimensional mesoscopic devices, but their behavior in higher-dimensional systems is complicated by many transverse channels; nodal-line semimetals provide a natural platform to explore this regime.
method: The authors theoretically analyze coherent transport through a finite nodal-line semimetal region, treating multiple reflections and transverse modes in the Fabry-Pérot cavity, likely using a scattering/transfer-matrix or Green's function approach.
result: They identify characteristic features of Fabry-Pérot oscillations in 3D nodal-line semimetals, showing how the momentum-space structure of nodal lines and transverse mode contributions modify the interference versus length or energy.
conclusion: The findings establish how Fabry-Pérot interference manifests in higher-dimensional topological semimetals, providing transport signatures that may be used to characterize nodal-line semimetals experimentally.

tldr: Large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations map the phase diagram of interacting spinless fermions on the honeycomb bilayer at charge neutrality, revealing emergent relativistic (Dirac-like) symmetry from a quadratically dispersing band structure.
motivation: The honeycomb bilayer hosts quadratic band touching points whose fate under interactions is debated; understanding whether interactions generate emergent Lorentz invariance is a fundamental correlated-fermion question.
method: Projective/auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo simulations of spinless fermions with short-range interactions on the bilayer honeycomb lattice at half filling.
result: The phase diagram contains interaction-driven phases in which the low-energy excitations acquire linear dispersion, i.e. an emergent relativistic symmetry, alongside other ordered or semimetallic regimes.

title: Revealing Charge Transfer In Defect-engineered $4{H}_{b}\text{−}{\mathrm{TaS}}_{2}$
authors: Siavash Karbasizadeh, Wooin Yang, Wonhee Ko, Haidong Zhou, An-Ping Li, Tom Berlijn, And Sai Mu
abstract:
Author(s): Siavash Karbasizadeh, Wooin Yang, Wonhee Ko, Haidong Zhou, An-Ping Li, Tom Berlijn, and Sai Mu

We present a comprehensive first-principles investigation of defects in [MATH]. In this layered transition metal dichalcogenide, charge transfer between alternating Mott-insulating 1T and metallic 1H layers gives rise to exotic quantum phases such as the Kondo effect an…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204107] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A first-principles study of defects and interlayer charge transfer in the layered dichalcogenide 4Hb-TaS2, where alternating Mott-insulating 1T and metallic 1H layers host exotic phases.
motivation: 4Hb-TaS2 hosts competing Mott-insulating and metallic layers whose charge transfer is thought to underlie phenomena such as the Kondo effect, but the microscopic role of defects in mediating this transfer is poorly understood.
method: Comprehensive density-functional/first-principles calculations of defect structures and charge redistribution across the alternating 1T and 1H layers.
result: The calculations reveal how specific defects drive charge transfer between the Mott-insulating and metallic layers, linking defect chemistry to the emergent quantum phases.
conclusion: Defect engineering is identified as a lever for tuning interlayer charge transfer and the associated correlated-electron behavior in 4Hb-TaS2.

title: Anatomy Of Spin-orbit Torques In Monolayer ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GaTe}}_{2}$: Insights From Atomistic And Momentum-space Decompositions
authors: Gusthavo M. S. Brizolla, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Yaroslav Zhumagulov, And Jaroslav Fabian
abstract:
Author(s): Gusthavo M. S. Brizolla, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Yaroslav Zhumagulov, and Jaroslav Fabian

Spin–orbit torque (SOT) enables electrical magnetization control in spintronic devices. Here, the authors calculate SOT in monolayer Fe
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204424] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study decomposing spin-orbit torques in monolayer Fe3GeTe2 and Fe3GaTe2 across the magnetization sphere, revealing hidden mirror-cancelled torques on individual Fe atoms.
motivation: Spin-orbit torque offers electrical control of magnetization in spintronic devices, and van der Waals ferromagnets with perpendicular anisotropy provide a route to strong spin-orbit coupling without heavy elements, so a detailed understanding of the torque's microscopic origin and angular dependence is needed.
method: Density functional theory combined with Wannier interpolation and the Kubo formalism is used to compute the torque response, decomposed atomistically and in momentum space and mapped over the full magnetization sphere.
result: Mirror symmetry forbids conventional in-plane spin accumulation for out-of-plane magnetization but permits a strongly angle-dependent response when the magnetization is tilted; mirror-related Fe atoms host hidden torques up to 30 times the net torque, whose cancellation could be lifted by van der Waals engineering.
conclusion: The work clarifies the symmetry-governed anatomy of spin-orbit torques in these 2D ferromagnets and suggests interface/stacking engineering as a means to exploit the large hidden atomic torques.

title: Transport In Close-packed Solids With Stacking Defects
authors: C. M. Wilson, R. Ganesh, And K. V. Samokhin
abstract:
Author(s): C. M. Wilson, R. Ganesh, and K. V. Samokhin

Lithium and sodium are the only solids that are known to lose crystalline order upon cooling. The seemingly disordered low-temperature phase shows signatures of various close-packed structures. The lack of order has been attributed to a hidden gauge symmetry that arises when electrons from one layer…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214204] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electronic transport in close-packed solids (Li and Na) whose low-temperature phases lose crystalline order owing to stacking defects and a hidden gauge symmetry.
motivation: Lithium and sodium are unique in losing crystalline order on cooling, and the resulting disordered close-packed phases are poorly understood; the authors aim to explain their transport signatures.
method: A theoretical treatment of transport in close-packed structures containing stacking defects, invoking an emergent gauge symmetry arising from interlayer electron coupling, likely within a Boltzmann/relaxation-time or effective-field framework.
result: The analysis connects stacking-defect-induced disorder and the associated gauge structure to characteristic features of the electrical transport response in these low-temperature phases.
conclusion: Stacking defects and hidden gauge symmetry provide a consistent picture of transport in the disordered low-temperature phases of Li and Na.

title: Maximization Of Nuclear Fusion Reactivity Via Optimal Energy Distributions
authors: Roberto Onofrio, Kamel Ourabah, And Carlo Presilla
abstract:
Author(s): Roberto Onofrio, Kamel Ourabah, and Carlo Presilla

We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044136] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that a single Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distribution maximizes nuclear fusion reactivity whenever reactivity is a concave function of the mean available kinetic energy.
motivation: Fusion reactivity depends strongly on the tail of the particle energy distribution, so it is natural to ask whether non-thermal or tailored distributions can outperform the standard thermal Maxwell-Boltzmann case.
method: The authors treat reactivity as a functional of the energy probability distribution and analyze its concavity with respect to the average available kinetic energy, comparing the MB distribution against alternative distributions.
result: A single Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution is optimal in the concave regime near the relevant operating conditions, whereas non-thermal distributions can only help when reactivity is a convex function of mean energy.
conclusion: The results clarify when distribution shaping can enhance fusion yields and identify the concavity of reactivity as the decisive criterion, with implications for fusion plasma scenarios.

title: It Takes Two To Tribo: Stochastic Charge Evolution In Repeated Binary Collisions Of Acoustically Levitated Particles
authors: Tom F. O'hara, Adrian C. Barnes, James W. E. Drewitt, Nathan Croll Dawes, And Karen L. Aplin
abstract:
Author(s): Tom F. O'Hara, Adrian C. Barnes, James W. E. Drewitt, Nathan Croll Dawes, and Karen L. Aplin

Despite many models proposed to explain charging behavior between insulating particles, the mechanisms underlying triboelectric charging have remained an open question in nonequilibrium physics. This manuscript presents a new experimental method to measure charge transfer during collisions between individual pairs of levitated particles, showing that charge evolution saturates as predicted by the condenser model.

#AdvancingField #TimelyTopic #TheoryExperiment


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045409] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of stochastic charge transfer between individual pairs of acoustically levitated insulating particles during repeated binary collisions, showing saturation consistent with the condenser model.
motivation: Triboelectric charging between insulating particles lacks a quantitative mechanistic explanation despite many proposed models, remaining an open problem in nonequilibrium physics.
method: Individual pairs of particles are levitated acoustically and collided repeatedly while charge transfer is measured directly, allowing charge evolution to be tracked collision-by-collision.
result: The measured charge evolution saturates with collision number, in agreement with predictions of the condenser model of triboelectric charge transfer.
conclusion: Pairwise levitated-collision experiments provide a clean platform for testing triboelectric charging models and support the condenser picture of saturation.

title: Minimal Network Of Brain Dynamics: Hierarchy Of Approximations To Quasicritical Neural Network Dynamics
authors: Jeremy B. Goetz, Naruepon Weerawongphrom, Rashid V. Williams-García, John M. Beggs, And Gerardo Ortiz
abstract:
Author(s): Jeremy B. Goetz, Naruepon Weerawongphrom, Rashid V. Williams-García, John M. Beggs, and Gerardo Ortiz

We present an interacting model of neural network dynamics that incorporates key biological features, including multiple forms of inhibitory interactions.
