We develop a hierarchy of analytical mean-field approximations to characterize nonequilibrium phase transitions between ordered, disordered, and …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044321] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A mean-field hierarchy is developed to describe nonequilibrium phase transitions between ordered, disordered, and critical regimes in a model of neural network dynamics with multiple inhibitory interaction types.
motivation: Real biological neural circuits show quasicritical dynamics with several forms of inhibition, and a tractable interacting model with analytical approximations is needed to characterize their collective phases.
method: The authors construct an interacting neural network model incorporating multiple inhibitory mechanisms and analyze it via a hierarchy of mean-field approximations to map out nonequilibrium phase transitions.
result: The hierarchy of approximations reveals transitions among ordered, disordered, and quasicritical regimes, with the level of approximation systematically refining the predicted phase boundaries and critical behavior.
conclusion: Mean-field hierarchies offer a practical analytical route to quasicritical neural dynamics, though the framework is purely classical and concerns biological networks rather than quantum systems.

title: Absorbing Phase Transition In A Queueing Model Of Coupled Adaptive Agents
authors: Alexei Vazquez
abstract:
Author(s): Alexei Vazquez

What decides whether people do things together or separately? Many activities cannot be carried out alone, and an individual must rank them against the private tasks competing for the same time. We address this within the priority-queue description of human activity by letting each agent choose the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044322] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A priority-queue model in which adaptive agents choose which collective activities to join exhibits an absorbing phase transition separating coordinated collective behavior from fragmented individual activity.
motivation: Many human activities require coordination with others while competing for limited individual time, so understanding what determines whether people act together or separately is a basic question about collective social dynamics.
method: Each agent in a priority-queue description of human activity is allowed to choose its tasks, and the resulting stochastic dynamics is analyzed for phase-transition behavior, presumably via mean-field or numerical simulation approaches.
result: The model displays an absorbing phase transition between a regime where collective activities are sustained by a finite fraction of agents and a regime where collective activity dies out.
conclusion: Coordination of human activity can be understood as a nonequilibrium critical phenomenon, with adaptive task selection alone sufficient to generate a sharp transition in collective behavior.

title: Reentrance And Temperature Chaos In The $p$-spin Ising Spin Glass
authors: Hidetoshi Nishimori
abstract:
Author(s): Hidetoshi Nishimori

Reentrant transitions and temperature chaos are two unusual properties of spin glasses. We recently established a general logical relation between these two phenomena [
tldr: The paper presents an explicit p-spin Ising spin-glass example illustrating a logical relation between reentrant transitions and temperature chaos.
motivation: Reentrant transitions and temperature chaos are unusual spin-glass phenomena, and the author seeks to clarify their general logical connection through a concrete model.
method: The analysis uses the fully connected p-spin Ising spin glass as an explicit example to demonstrate the previously established logical relation between the two phenomena.
result: The paper provides a concrete realization of the logical link between reentrance and temperature chaos in the p-spin Ising spin-glass model.
conclusion: The example supports the general relation between reentrant transitions and temperature chaos, but the work is a classical statistical-mechanics study rather than a quantum-information or information-thermodynamics contribution.

title: Long-range States In Collisions Of Ultracold Molecules
authors: James F. E. Croft, Brian K. Kendrick, And Jeremy M. Hutson
abstract:
Author(s): James F. E. Croft, Brian K. Kendrick, and Jeremy M. Hutson

We use coupled-channel calculations to explore the nature of near-threshold bound states in a simplified model of [MATH]. This is a prototype for systems with very strong coupling at short range and chaotic behavior for the short-range states. We find that there are states with s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043087] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: Coupled-channel calculations are used to characterize near-threshold long-range bound states in a simplified model of ultracold molecule collisions with strong short-range coupling.
motivation: Ultracold molecular collisions exhibit chaotic short-range spectra and strong coupling, making the nature of near-threshold bound states and their role in scattering and loss processes important to understand.
method: Quantum coupled-channel scattering calculations on a model molecular system, extracting near-threshold bound-state structure and comparing long-range states against the chaotic short-range spectrum.
result: The authors identify long-range states with atypical character distinct from the chaotic short-range level structure, and characterize how they emerge near threshold in the strongly coupled model.
conclusion: Long-range states in ultracold molecule collisions form a distinguishable class of near-threshold levels whose properties are governed by the long-range potential rather than short-range chaos, with implications for modeling cold collision dynamics.

title: Origin Of The Magnetic Ground State Of ${\mathrm{Tb}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ir}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$
authors: Y. Alexanian, E. Lhotel, J. Robert, S. Petit, E. Lefrançois, P. Lejay, A. Hadj-Azzem, F. Damay, J. Ollivier, B. Fåk, S. de Brion, R. Ballou, And V. Simonet
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Alexanian, E. Lhotel, J. Robert, S. Petit, E. Lefrançois, P. Lejay, A. Hadj-Azzem, F. Damay, J. Ollivier, B. Fåk, S. De Brion, R. Ballou, and V. Simonet

Rare-earth pyrochlore iridates offer a fertile ground for unconventional magnetic phenomena. In Tb+ ions, subject to rare-earth interactions and to the Ir magnetic field, plays a key role in shaping the magnetic order.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043060] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering, specific heat, and numerical simulations are combined to explain the unusual low-temperature magnetic ground state of the pyrochlore iridate Tb2Ir2O7, where an unexpected extra ordering component arises from the quantum nature of Tb3+ ions coupled to the Ir magnetic field.
motivation: Rare-earth pyrochlore iridates host unconventional magnetism, and Tb2Ir2O7 shows an anomalous ordered moment component orthogonal to the direction favored by the dominant interactions, whose origin was unexplained.
method: The authors combine numerical simulations with neutron scattering experiments and specific heat measurements extending down to dilution-refrigerator temperatures.
result: The quantum character of the Tb3+ ions, acting under rare-earth interactions and the internal magnetic field from Ir, is shown to be essential in producing the observed magnetic order with its additional orthogonal component.
conclusion: The magnetic ground state of Tb2Ir2O7 is governed by the interplay of quantum crystal-field physics of Tb3+ and Ir-derived fields, clarifying the origin of its anomalous ordering.

title: Quasicrystal Topological Hydrodynamics
authors: Jun-Liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-Jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, And Jin-Hui Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, and Jin-hui Chen

Quasicrystalline water waves allow exquisite insight into topological physics and provides a unique platform for manipulating particle for a wide range of applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031078] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates quasicrystalline water-wave platforms for realizing and probing topological physics and particle manipulation.
motivation: Quasicrystals offer aperiodic long-range order that can host exotic topological phenomena, and classical water waves provide a versatile, observable testbed for such physics.
method: The authors use quasicrystalline arrangements of water-wave scatterers/structures to engineer topological band structure and hydrodynamic transport, characterizing the resulting wave dynamics experimentally and theoretically.
result: Topological features and robust transport/manipulation capabilities are observed in the quasicrystalline water-wave system, enabling controlled particle motion.
conclusion: Quasicrystalline hydrodynamic platforms constitute a practical route to exploring topological physics and to applications in wave-based particle manipulation.

title: Genuine And Spurious (Non-)Ergodicity In Single Particle Tracking
authors: Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, And Aleksei Chechkin
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, and Aleksei Chechkin

The mean-squared increment is introduced as a new statistic to characterize single-particle positional time series data, providing a more precise and unambiguous method than previous approaches to evaluating ergodicity and helping to discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031071] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the mean-squared increment as a statistic for analyzing single-particle tracking data and distinguishing ergodic from non-ergodic stochastic processes.
motivation: Single-particle tracking often requires robust methods to assess ergodicity and classify stochastic processes, and previous approaches can be ambiguous.
method: The authors define and analyze the mean-squared increment of positional time series and use it to characterize ergodicity and discriminate between classes of stochastic processes.
result: The mean-squared increment provides a more precise and unambiguous ergodicity diagnostic than earlier statistics and helps distinguish genuine from spurious non-ergodicity.
conclusion: The proposed statistic improves the interpretation of single-particle tracking data and offers a practical tool for ergodicity analysis in stochastic processes.

title: Role Of Anisotropic Electronic Friction In Laser-Driven Hydrogen Recombination On Copper
authors: Alexander Spears, Wojciech G. Stark, And Reinhard J. Maurer
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Spears, Wojciech G. Stark, and Reinhard J. Maurer

Ultrafast light-driven chemical dynamics at surfaces are governed by energy transfer from excited electrons to vibrational degrees of freedom. When this nonadiabatic energy transfer is anisotropic, it can lead to dynamical steering effects that affect reaction probabilities or nonthermal final energ…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 178001] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how anisotropic electronic friction affects laser-driven hydrogen recombination dynamics on a copper surface.
motivation: Ultrafast light-driven chemistry at surfaces depends on nonadiabatic energy transfer from excited electrons to molecular vibrations, and anisotropic friction may produce dynamical steering that changes reaction outcomes.
method: The authors model laser-induced hydrogen recombination on copper using nonadiabatic surface dynamics with anisotropic electronic friction to quantify energy transfer and reaction probability changes.
result: Anisotropic electronic friction is found to induce dynamical steering effects that alter reaction probabilities and nonthermal final energy distributions.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of laser-driven surface reactions requires accounting for the directional dependence of electronic friction rather than treating it isotropically.

title: Bulk-Mediated Reflection Of Chirality-Protected Surface Spin Waves
authors: Vitaliy I. Vasyuchka, Florin Ciubotaru, Andrii V. Chumak, Burkard Hillebrands, And Alexander A. Serga
abstract:
Author(s): Vitaliy I. Vasyuchka, Florin Ciubotaru, Andrii V. Chumak, Burkard Hillebrands, and Alexander A. Serga

Surface spin waves of the Damon-Eshbach type exhibit intrinsically nonreciprocal transport properties with a chiral dynamical field structure that localizes counterpropagating waves at opposite film surfaces. Such chirality has been predicted to suppress direct backscattering in thin films within fr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176701] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how chiral, nonreciprocal Damon-Eshbach surface spin waves in magnetic films are reflected via bulk spin-wave modes, clarifying the limits of chirality-protected backscattering suppression.
motivation: Chirality of surface spin waves was predicted to suppress direct backscattering in thin films, which is attractive for magnonic transport, but the actual loss channels and reflection mechanisms remained unclear.
method: Microwave-excited spin-wave propagation experiments combined with mode analysis of surface and bulk spin-wave branches in a magnetic film, mapping how surface modes convert into bulk modes and back.
result: Chirality protection suppresses direct surface-to-surface backscattering, but reflection still occurs via intermediate bulk spin-wave states, imposing a residual loss channel on nonreciprocal surface transport.
conclusion: The findings delimit the practical effectiveness of chirality-protected spin-wave transport and identify bulk-mediated conversion as the dominant relaxation pathway for Damon-Eshbach modes.

title: Field-angle Dependent Spin Dynamics And Mode Evolution In Monoclinic Few-layer ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}$
authors: Manar Haouili, Hua Xu, And Yan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Manar Haouili, Hua Xu, and Yan Liu

Few-layer [MATH] exhibits thickness-dependent interlayer antiferromagnetic coupling and magnetic-field-induced spin-flip transitions. Although bilayer [MATH] has been extensively studied, the spin dynamics of thicker multilayer structures remain less well understood. In t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194424] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically/experimentally studies field-angle-dependent spin dynamics and magnon mode evolution in monoclinic few-layer CrI3, a layered antiferromagnet.
motivation: Few-layer CrI3 shows thickness-dependent interlayer antiferromagnetic coupling and field-induced spin-flip transitions, but spin dynamics in thicker multilayers is poorly understood.
method: Spin-wave/magnon analysis of multilayer CrI3 as a function of applied magnetic field angle, tracking mode evolution across spin-flip transitions.
result: Identifies angle-dependent spin dynamics and the evolution of magnon modes with layer number and field orientation in monoclinic few-layer CrI3.
conclusion: The work clarifies magnetic excitation structure in multilayer CrI3, relevant to layered antiferromagnet spintronics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nonrelativistic Anisotropic Magnetoresistance With Collinear And Noncollinear Magnetic Order
authors: P. Ritzinger, O. Sedláček, J. Železný, And K. Výborný
abstract:
Author(s): P. Ritzinger, O. Sedláček, J. Železný, and K. Výborný

Anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) arises from symmetry lowering of the conductivity tensor induced by magnetic order. In simple ferromagnets, AMR is a relativistic effect, relying on spin-orbit interaction (SOC). Here, we demonstrate that a comparable symmetry lowering can also occur in a nonrelat…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204427] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theory of anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) in nonrelativistic settings, showing that symmetry lowering of the conductivity tensor can arise from collinear and noncollinear magnetic order even without spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: AMR is conventionally understood as a relativistic effect mediated by spin-orbit interaction in simple ferromagnets, so the authors ask whether comparable symmetry lowering of transport can occur in nonrelativistic magnetic systems.
method: Symmetry-based analysis of the conductivity tensor combined with microscopic/tight-binding style transport calculations for collinear and noncollinear magnetic orders, decomposing effects by magnetic symmetry rather than SOC.
result: A symmetry-lowering contribution to the conductivity tensor comparable in magnitude to conventional AMR is identified in nonrelativistic magnets, with distinct signatures for collinear versus noncollinear order.
conclusion: AMR-like transport anisotropies are not exclusively relativistic phenomena, which broadens the classification of magnetotransport effects and suggests new routes to designing spintronic responses in complex magnets.

title: Structure And Equation Of State Of Warm Expanded Carbon: Insights From Molecular Dynamics With Machine-learned Potentials
authors: J. X. D'souza, E. B. Bauer, S. Jiang, L. X. Benedict, N. Goldman, R. A. London, M. P. Hill, Y. Ping, A. Lazicki, M. Foord, And S. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): J. X. D'Souza, E. B. Bauer, S. Jiang, L. X. Benedict, N. Goldman, R. A. London, M. P. Hill, Y. Ping, A. Lazicki, M. Foord, and S. Zhang

Experimental validation of equation-of-state (EOS) models for high-energy-density applications typically involves measuring the shock Hugoniot, which helps constrain the high-pressure, high-density EOS. However, EOS measurements at below ambient density in the expanded regime are less common. Recent…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214110] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: Machine-learned molecular dynamics simulations are used to compute the structure and equation of state of warm expanded carbon at below-ambient densities, benchmarking against recent experiments.
motivation: Equation-of-state models at high energy density are usually constrained by shock Hugoniot measurements, but data in the low-density expanded regime are scarce, leaving EOS models poorly validated there.
method: The authors perform molecular dynamics simulations driven by machine-learned interatomic potentials to obtain structural and thermodynamic properties of warm expanded carbon, and compare the resulting EOS with experimental data.
result: The simulations reproduce the measured structure and EOS of expanded carbon and clarify how bonding and ionization change in the warm expanded regime.
conclusion: Machine-learned potentials provide a practical route to validated EOS models for high-energy-density applications where direct measurement is difficult.

title: Coupled Dynamical Boltzmann Transport Equations With Long-range Electron-phonon And Electron-electron Interactions In Two-dimensional Materials
authors: Francesco Macheda And Thibault Sohier
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Macheda and Thibault Sohier

The intrinsic resistivity of materials depends on the interplay of current-carrying electrons with vibrational and electronic excitations. Here, the authors develop a numerical solution to the coupled dynamics of electrons and electrodynamic modes, for 2D monolayers and heterostructures, which includes both types of excitations. They show that while resistivity is ultimately driven by phonons, electronic excitations can play a significant role via direct electron-electron scattering and dynamical screening of the phonons.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245419] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a numerical framework for solving coupled dynamical Boltzmann transport equations in two-dimensional monolayers and heterostructures that includes both electron-phonon and electron-electron interactions.
motivation: Intrinsic resistivity in materials arises from the interplay of electrons with vibrational and electronic excitations, but existing transport treatments typically treat phonon and electron-electron scattering separately.
method: A coupled system of dynamical Boltzmann transport equations for electrons and electrodynamic modes is derived and solved numerically for 2D materials, incorporating long-range electron-phonon and electron-electron interactions and dynamical screening.
result: Resistivity is found to be ultimately phonon-driven, while electronic excitations contribute significantly through direct electron-electron scattering and through dynamical screening of the phonons.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of 2D transport requires treating phonon and electronic excitations on equal footing; the presented coupled Boltzmann approach provides a practical tool for such calculations.

title: Noise-induced Bistability Of Information-driven Active Agents In Turbulence
authors: Chenfeng Ma And Yan Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Chenfeng Ma and Yan Cui

Information-driven active matter relies on continuous feedback loops subject to intrinsic processing latency. We investigate how this temporal nonlocality interacts with the spatial fluctuations of homogeneous isotropic turbulence for agents operating in the dilute, noncommunicating limit. This inte…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045403] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies noise-induced bistability in information-driven active agents moving through homogeneous isotropic turbulence with feedback latency.
motivation: Active matter agents that rely on delayed information feedback may exhibit nontrivial collective or dynamical behavior when coupled to turbulent fluctuations, but this interaction is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze dilute, noncommunicating information-driven agents subject to intrinsic processing latency in homogeneous isotropic turbulence, likely using stochastic modeling and/or numerical simulations.
result: They find that the interplay between temporal nonlocality from feedback delay and spatial turbulence fluctuations can produce noise-induced bistability in the agents' behavior.
conclusion: The work highlights how delayed information processing and environmental noise can generate bistable dynamics in classical active matter, with implications for information-driven agents in turbulent flows.

title: Field-induced Magnetic Phase Transition Driven By A Ground-state Level Crossing In ${\mathrm{CsErSe}}_{2}$
authors: Hope Whitelock, Allen O. Scheie, Marissa Mcmaster, Ian A. Leahy, Li Xiang, Mykhaylo Ozerov, Dmitry Smirnov, Eun Sang Choi, C. Dela Cruz, M. O. Ajeesh, Eliana S. Krakovsky, Daniel A. Rehn, Jie Xing, Athena S. Sefat, And Minhyea Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hope Whitelock, Allen O. Scheie, Marissa McMaster, Ian A. Leahy, Li Xiang, Mykhaylo Ozerov, Dmitry Smirnov, Eun Sang Choi, C. dela Cruz, M. O. Ajeesh, Eliana S. Krakovsky, Daniel A. Rehn, Jie Xing, Athena S. Sefat, and Minhyea Lee

We report a comprehensive study of the low-temperature magnetic properties of the insulating rare-earth triangular magnet [MATH]. We uncover a field-induced level crossing at the crystal electric field ground state, which gives rise to a first-order phase transition as well as to di…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043072] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive experimental and theoretical study of the low-temperature magnetic properties of the insulating rare-earth triangular magnet CsErSe2, revealing a field-induced crystal-electric-field ground-state level crossing that drives a first-order phase transition.
motivation: Rare-earth triangular magnets hosting crystal-electric-field-split doublets are candidate platforms for exotic magnetic phases, and understanding how field-induced level crossings reshape their phase diagrams is of intrinsic interest to frustrated magnetism.
method: The authors combine magnetization, heat capacity, and high-field spectroscopy (including terahertz/infrared and pulsed-field measurements) with crystal-field modeling to map the low-temperature H–T phase diagram of CsErSe2.
result: They identify a level crossing within the crystal-electric-field ground-state doublet that produces a first-order magnetic phase transition and accompanying anomalies in the thermodynamic response under applied field.
conclusion: The work establishes ground-state level crossings as a control knob for field-driven phase transitions in rare-earth triangular magnets, though the results remain within condensed-matter magnetism with no quantum-information or information-thermodynamic analysis.

title: Formation Of Cavity Polaritons Via High-order Van Hove Singularities
authors: Igor Gianardi, Michele Pini, And Francesco Piazza
abstract:
Author(s): Igor Gianardi, Michele Pini, and Francesco Piazza

We consider polaritons formed by hybridizing a continuum of interband particle-hole excitations of an insulating phase with a cavity photon at subgap frequencies, where absorption is suppressed. The strength of the hybridization is driven by the Van Hove singularity (VHS) in the joint density of sta…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043074] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies cavity polaritons formed by hybridizing cavity photons with interband particle-hole excitations near high-order Van Hove singularities in an insulating material.
motivation: Subgap-frequency polaritons are attractive because absorption is suppressed, but strong light-matter hybridization typically requires resonant matter excitations or large joint density of states.
method: The authors analyze polariton formation by coupling a cavity photon mode to a continuum of interband particle-hole excitations, focusing on enhancement driven by high-order Van Hove singularities in the joint density of states.
result: They show that high-order Van Hove singularities can strongly enhance the hybridization strength and enable cavity polariton formation at subgap frequencies.
conclusion: The work identifies high-order Van Hove singularities as a route to engineer strong light-matter coupling in cavity polariton systems, with relevance to condensed-matter polaritonics rather than quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Disordered Ground State And Relative Proximity To An Exactly Solvable Model In The Frustrated Magnet ${\mathrm{CeMgAl}}_{11}{\mathrm{O}}_{19}$
authors: G. Bastien, A. Eliáš, V. Anderle, A. Kancko, C. A. Corrêa, S. Kumar, P. Proschek, J. Prokleška, L. Nádherný, D. Sedmidubský, T. Treu, P. Gegenwart, M. Kratochvílová, M. Žonda, And R. H. Colman
abstract:
Author(s): G. Bastien, A. Eliáš, V. Anderle, A. Kancko, C. A. Corrêa, S. Kumar, P. Proschek, J. Prokleška, L. Nádherný, D. Sedmidubský, T. Treu, P. Gegenwart, M. Kratochvílová, M. Žonda, and R. H. Colman

Single-crystal measurements and numerical calculations reveal a quantum-disordered magnetic ground state in the triangular-lattice magnet CeMgAl
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042007] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: Single-crystal measurements and numerical modeling show that the triangular-lattice magnet CeMgAl11O19 hosts a quantum-disordered magnetic ground state with no order down to 30 mK.
motivation: The authors aim to test whether this frustrated magnet realizes a quantum-disordered state near an exactly solvable spin-1/2 quantum critical point and to assess the role of structural disorder.
method: They perform thermodynamic and magnetic measurements on single crystals and compare the data quantitatively with an anisotropic spin-1/2 model and numerical calculations.
result: No magnetic ordering is observed down to 30 mK, and the material is found to lie farther from the exactly solvable quantum critical point than previously estimated, with structural disorder likely suppressing magnetic order.
conclusion: CeMgAl11O19 is a candidate quantum-disordered frustrated magnet, but its proximity to the idealized solvable model is weaker than earlier thought and disorder effects are important.

title: Imaging Orbital Rashba Induced Charge Transport Anisotropy
authors: Eylon Persky, Xi Wang, Giacomo Sala, Thierry C. van Thiel, Edouard Lesne, Alexander Lau, Mario Cuoco, Marc Gabay, Carmine Ortix, Andrea D. Caviglia, And Beena Kalisky
abstract:
Author(s): Eylon Persky, Xi Wang, Giacomo Sala, Thierry C. van Thiel, Edouard Lesne, Alexander Lau, Mario Cuoco, Marc Gabay, Carmine Ortix, Andrea D. Caviglia, and Beena Kalisky

Scanning SQUID current imaging reveals domain-dependent charge transport anisotropy at the (111) LaAlO
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042008] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: Scanning SQUID imaging of the (111) LaAlO3/SrTiO3 interface reveals domain-dependent charge transport anisotropy linked to orbital Rashba coupling and nonlinear Hall response.
motivation: Broken symmetries at oxide interfaces can generate orbital Rashba spin-orbit coupling, but a local, electrical probe of the resulting orbital textures and their impact on transport has been lacking.
method: The authors use scanning SQUID current imaging to map local current flow and anisotropy across domains, combined with global transport measurements of the nonlinear Hall response.
result: Domain-dependent anisotropic charge transport is observed and connected to anisotropic orbital Rashba coupling, enabling an electrical readout of orbital textures.
conclusion: The work establishes local current imaging plus nonlinear Hall measurements as a route to probe orbital textures in oxide interfaces, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Moving Heterointerface With Robustly High Thermal Conductance
authors: Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, And Bai Song
abstract:
Author(s): Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, and Bai Song

Structural superlubricity between gold micromesas and graphite enables high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that remains insensitive to sliding and rotation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041005] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports robustly high interfacial thermal conductance at moving gold-graphite heterointerfaces enabled by structural superlubricity.
motivation: The authors aim to achieve high, wear-free thermal conductance across sliding interfaces, which is challenging because motion usually degrades contact quality and heat transfer.
method: They study gold micromesas on graphite in a structural superlubricity regime and measure interfacial thermal conductance under sliding and rotation.
result: The heterointerface exhibits high thermal conductance that remains nearly insensitive to sliding and rotation while avoiding wear.
conclusion: Structural superlubricity can provide stable, high thermal transport across moving interfaces, with implications for thermal management in movable contacts.

title: Pomeranchuk Instability Induced By An Emergent Higher-Order Van Hove Singularity On The Distorted Kagome Surface Of ${\mathrm{Co}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$
authors: Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, And Haim Beidenkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Pranab Kumar Nag, Rajib Batabyal, Julian Ingham, Noam Morali, Hengxin Tan, Jahyun Koo, Jean Souza, Moshe Haim, Armando Consiglio, Enke Liu, Raquel Queiroz, Ronny Thomale, Binghai Yan, Claudia Felser, Nurit Avraham, and Haim Beidenkopf

Surface deformation of the kagome lattice in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031069] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: A scanning tunneling microscopy and theory study showing that surface distortion of the kagome lattice in Co3Sn2S2 flattens saddle points into a higher-order Van Hove singularity, driving a Pomeranchuk instability and nematic order.
motivation: The kagome lattice hosts Dirac and flat bands whose saddle points can produce Van Hove singularities, and it has been proposed that deforming the lattice could realize higher-order Van Vleck singularities with divergent density of states. The authors ask whether such a deformation occurs on the surface of Co3Sn2S2 and whether it destabilizes the electronic system.
method: The authors combine spectroscopic-imaging STM/STS measurements of the kagome surface with tight-binding and effective-model calculations to map the band structure and locate the saddle points, then analyze the resulting Fermi-surface instabilities within a mean-field Pomeranchuk/nematic framework.
result: The surface kagome layer is shown to be structurally distorted in a way that flattens the saddle points into a higher-order Van Hove singularity, and the measured quasiparticle interference and spectra indicate a Pomeranchuk instability that produces a nematic electronic state.
conclusion: Surface lattice deformation provides a tunable route to higher-order Van Hove singularities and correlation-driven nematic order in kagome metals, establishing Co3Sn2S2 as a platform for studying higher-order Van Hove physics.

title: Effective Ionic Valence And Local Magnetic Moment In Kagome Superconductors
authors: Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, And Wei Ku
abstract:
Author(s): Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, and Wei Ku

Revealing concealed ionic local moments in kagome superconductors reflects strong local correlations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031064] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports evidence for concealed ionic local moments and effective ionic valence in kagome superconductors, indicating strong local electronic correlations.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between superconductivity and correlated local moments in kagome metals is important for clarifying their unconventional electronic phases.
method: The authors combine experimental probes and theoretical analysis to infer effective ionic valence and local magnetic moments in kagome superconductors.
result: They find signatures of local magnetic moments that are not captured by simple band-structure pictures, pointing to strong local correlations in these materials.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of local correlation effects in kagome superconductors and their role in shaping the observed physical properties.

title: Directional Transport By Topological Pump Of Localized Moiré Bulk States
authors: Dan Yao, Zhonghao Fu, Hailong He, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Liping Ye, Manzhu Ke, And Zhengyou Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Dan Yao, Zhonghao Fu, Hailong He, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Liping Ye, Manzhu Ke, and Zhengyou Liu

The discovery of directional and robust wave manipulation has become a crucial goal in the field of science and technology. Topological pump, as an efficient form of directed energy transport protected by nontrivial topology, has been intensively studied in condensed matter and materials physics. Co…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176301] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates directional, topologically protected transport of localized moiré bulk states via a topological pump in a classical wave (acoustic/phononic) platform.
motivation: Robust directional wave manipulation is highly desirable, and topological pumping provides a mechanism for directed energy transport protected by nontrivial band topology; the authors aim to extend this to localized moiré bulk states.
method: A topological pump is designed and implemented (likely in an acoustic metamaterial) to adiabatically cycle parameters so that localized moiré bulk states are transported in a controlled direction, with topological invariants underpinning the protection.
result: The experiment/analysis shows that the pumped moiré bulk states exhibit directional, robust transport immune to moderate disorder, confirming the topological character of the pumping process.
conclusion: Topological pumping of moiré bulk states offers a viable route to robust directional wave guiding, with potential applications in classical wave manipulation and topological metamaterials.

title: Electronic Transport In Hexagonal-Boron-Nitride-Encapsulated Graphene Limited By Remote Phonon Scattering
authors: K. Dinar, F. Macheda, A. Guandalini, M. Paillet, C. Consejo, F. Teppe, B. Jouault, T. Sohier, And S. Nanot
abstract:
Author(s): K. Dinar, F. Macheda, A. Guandalini, M. Paillet, C. Consejo, F. Teppe, B. Jouault, T. Sohier, and S. Nanot

We study the impact of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) phonons on the electrical resistivity of hBN-encapsulated graphene. While encapsulation yields high-mobility devices, the surrounding hBN itself introduces remote scattering from polar optical phonons, whose role in standard resistivity measuremen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176302] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper quantifies how remote polar-optical phonons in the hexagonal boron nitride encapsulating layers limit the electrical resistivity and mobility of graphene transistors.
motivation: hBN encapsulation is widely used to obtain high-mobility graphene devices, but the encapsulant itself introduces remote phonon scattering whose contribution to standard resistivity measurements is poorly characterized.
method: The authors combine transport measurements on hBN-encapsulated graphene with first-principles modeling of hBN phonon modes and scattering rates to extract the remote-phonon contribution to resistivity versus temperature and carrier density.
result: Remote polar optical phonon scattering from hBN is shown to set a significant, previously underestimated contribution to the resistivity of encapsulated graphene, with a characteristic temperature dependence distinguishable from other scattering channels.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of hBN remote phonons is needed to interpret mobility data in encapsulated graphene and to assess the ultimate limits of such devices.

title: Altermagnetism In Folded Iron Chain Systems
authors: Ling-Fang Lin, Yang Zhang, Satoshi Okamoto, Adriana Moreo, Lun-Hui Hu, And Elbio Dagotto
abstract:
Author(s): Ling-Fang Lin, Yang Zhang, Satoshi Okamoto, Adriana Moreo, Lun-Hui Hu, and Elbio Dagotto

Altermagnetism—moment-compensated magnetism with momentum-dependent spin splitting—has so far been realized primarily in Néel-type antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate altermagnetism in folded iron chain systems with block-type magnetic order (e.g.,[MATH]). In the strictly one-dimensional (1D) cas…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176702] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate that altermagnetism—moment-compensated magnetism with momentum-dependent spin splitting—can arise in folded iron chain systems with block-type magnetic order, extending altermagnetism beyond the Néel-type antiferromagnets where it was previously found.
motivation: Altermagnetism had been realized mainly in Néel-type antiferromagnets, so the community lacks examples in other magnetic-order geometries; the authors ask whether block-type magnetic order in folded iron chains can host the same momentum-dependent spin splitting.
method: They analyze the magnetic symmetry and electronic structure of folded iron chain systems with block-type magnetic order, treating the strictly one-dimensional case and its extensions using model and first-principles band-structure techniques.
result: They find that folded iron chain geometries with block-type magnetic order exhibit altermagnetic spin splitting, establishing a new class of altermagnetic materials beyond the Néel-type framework.
conclusion: The work broadens the material and symmetry space of altermagnetism to chain-based block-type magnets, suggesting new platforms for spin-split compensated magnetism.

title: Contamination-Free Resolution Of Cantor Spectra And Magic-Angle Localization In Moiré Quasicrystals And Aperiodic Media
authors: James Chok, Matthew J. Colbrook, Mark Embree, And Jake Fillman
abstract:
Author(s): James Chok, Matthew J. Colbrook, Mark Embree, and Jake Fillman

Quasicrystalline Hamiltonians host Cantor-like spectra, gaps, and critical states, yet conventional finite-patch diagonalization is often compromised by spectral pollution: spurious eigenvalues absent from the infinite system. We introduce a certified spectral-computation framework for aperiodic med…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176403] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a certified spectral-computation framework to resolve Cantor spectra and magic-angle localization in moiré quasicrystals and aperiodic media without spectral pollution.
motivation: Finite-patch diagonalization of quasicrystalline Hamiltonians suffers from spectral pollution, producing spurious eigenvalues absent from the infinite system, which obscures genuine Cantor-like spectra and localization phenomena.
method: The authors develop a certified spectral-computation approach for aperiodic media, likely combining rigorous spectral theory, operator techniques, and numerical algorithms to distinguish true spectrum from pollution.
result: The framework resolves Cantor spectra and magic-angle localization in moiré quasicrystals and aperiodic media, providing contamination-free spectral information.
conclusion: This work advances mathematical and computational spectral theory for aperiodic quantum systems but is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Selective Strain Tuning Of Nonequilibrium Multiferroic Dynamics In ${\mathrm{BiFeO}}_{3}$
authors: Chenhang Xu, Patrick Liu, Bo Zhang, Minyong Han, Henry G. Bell, Cameron J. R. Duncan, Yusong Liu, Patrick L. Kramer, Randy Lemons, Jake D. Koralek, Alexander H. Reid, Dong Qian, Harold Y. Hwang, And Alfred Zong
abstract:
Author(s): Chenhang Xu, Patrick Liu, Bo Zhang, Minyong Han, Henry G. Bell, Cameron J. R. Duncan, Yusong Liu, Patrick L. Kramer, Randy Lemons, Jake D. Koralek, Alexander H. Reid, Dong Qian, Harold Y. Hwang, and Alfred Zong

Quantum materials are characterized by intertwined orders, and a fundamental goal in condensed matter physics is to achieve their selective control in such a way that one order parameter can be tuned while leaving others largely unaffected. Although significant progress has been made in thermal equi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176901] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: This work demonstrates selective strain control of nonequilibrium multiferroic order dynamics in BiFeO3 using ultrafast optical excitation.
motivation: Quantum materials host intertwined orders, and controlling one order parameter without disturbing others is a central goal in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use strain tuning combined with time-resolved ultrafast measurements to probe nonequilibrium multiferroic dynamics in BiFeO3.
result: Selective strain tuning enables distinct control over coupled multiferroic order parameters in the nonequilibrium regime.
conclusion: The findings establish strain as a selective knob for manipulating intertwined orders in multiferroic quantum materials, with implications for ultrafast control of functional properties.

title: Spectral Contraction From Gaussian Beams To Helmholtz Waves
authors: A. Domínguez-Cruz And B. M. Rodríguez-Lara
abstract:
Author(s): A. Domínguez-Cruz and B. M. Rodríguez-Lara

We introduce the ratio between the transverse Helmholtz length and the paraxial Gaussian-beam width as the physical parameter governing the contraction from separable Gaussian beams to transverse Helmholtz waves. For a fixed transverse Helmholtz shell within the paraxial angular spectrum, the large-…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043526] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a parameter comparing transverse Helmholtz length to paraxial Gaussian-beam width to characterize the transition from separable Gaussian beams to transverse Helmholtz waves.
motivation: The authors aim to quantify how paraxial Gaussian beam descriptions contract toward nonparaxial Helmholtz wave behavior within a fixed transverse angular spectrum shell.
method: They define the ratio of transverse Helmholtz length to Gaussian-beam width and analyze its role in governing the spectral contraction between the two wave descriptions.
result: The ratio is identified as the physical parameter controlling the contraction from separable Gaussian beams to transverse Helmholtz waves.
conclusion: This provides a simple physical criterion for understanding the paraxial-to-Helmholtz transition in beam optics.

title: Numerical Evaluation Of Casimir Forces Using The Discontinuous Galerkin Time-domain Method
authors: Carles Martí Farràs, Bettina Beverungen, Philip Trøst Kristensen, Francesco Intravaia, And Kurt Busch
abstract:
Author(s): Carles Martí Farràs, Bettina Beverungen, Philip Trøst Kristensen, Francesco Intravaia, and Kurt Busch

Casimir forces dominate the interaction between electrically neutral macroscopic objects at nanoscale separations, making their quantitative description highly relevant to modern technology and fundamental physics. In this work, we present a time-domain scheme for computing Casimir forces between va…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042817] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a time-domain discontinuous Galerkin method for numerically computing Casimir forces between macroscopic objects.
motivation: Casimir forces dominate neutral macroscopic interactions at nanoscale separations and require accurate quantitative modeling for fundamental and technological applications.
method: The authors develop a discontinuous Galerkin time-domain scheme to evaluate Casimir forces between objects, likely using electromagnetic field simulations.
result: The method enables numerical computation of Casimir forces in complex geometries within a time-domain framework.
conclusion: This work provides a computational tool for Casimir force calculations, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Intense-laser Nondipole-induced Symmetry Breaking In Solids
authors: Asger Weeth And Lars Bojer Madsen
abstract:
Author(s): Asger Weeth and Lars Bojer Madsen

High-harmonic spectroscopy in solids gives insight into the inner workings of solids, such as reconstructing band structures or probing the topological phase of materials. High-harmonic generation (HHG) is a highly nonlinear phenomena and simulations guide interpretations of experimental results. Th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043116] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates how nondipole effects in intense-laser-driven solids break symmetry and thereby modify high-harmonic generation spectra, providing guidance for interpreting high-harmonic spectroscopy experiments.
motivation: High-harmonic spectroscopy in solids is used to reconstruct band structures and probe topological phases, but accurate interpretation requires simulations that account for the spatial variation of the laser field across the solid, i.e., nondipole (magnetic-field) contributions that can break symmetries.
method: Numerical simulations of intense-laser-driven solids within a nondipole formulation of the light-matter interaction, analyzing how the resulting symmetry breaking manifests in the emitted harmonic spectrum.
result: Nondipole-induced symmetry breaking produces characteristic, selection-rule-violating features in the high-harmonic spectrum of solids.
conclusion: Nondipole effects must be included when using high-harmonic spectroscopy to infer band structure or topological properties of solids.

title: Electron Correlation Effects Via Triple Excitations On Energies And Hyperfine Structure Constants Of $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$
authors: Vaibhav Katyal And B. K. Sahoo
abstract:
Author(s): Vaibhav Katyal and B. K. Sahoo

Accurate determination of hyperfine structure constants in atomic systems provides important insight into the interplay of electron correlation and relativistic effects in the nuclear region. Although sodium (Na) is a relatively light atom, previous all-order relativistic many-body calculations of t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042813] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: Relativistic many-body calculations including triple excitations are used to compute energies and hyperfine structure constants of atomic sodium-23.
motivation: Accurate hyperfine structure constants probe the interplay of electron correlation and relativistic effects near the nucleus, and previous all-order calculations for sodium showed discrepancies that motivate more complete correlation treatments.
method: All-order relativistic many-body perturbation theory is extended to include triple excitations to improve the treatment of electron correlation in the valence and core-polarization sectors.
result: The inclusion of triple excitations modifies the computed energies and hyperfine constants, bringing theoretical values into closer agreement with precision measurements for 23Na.
conclusion: Higher-order correlation effects are important for accurate hyperfine structure predictions in light alkali atoms, and the approach can be extended to other systems.

title: Photodetachment Energy Of Negative Hydrogen Ions
authors: Maen Salman And Jean-Philippe Karr
abstract:
Author(s): Maen Salman and Jean-Philippe Karr

We report a high-precision calculation of the photodetachment energy of the hydrogen anion [MATH], also known as the electron affinity of the hydrogen atom. The nonrelativistic bound-state energy is obtained using an exact three-body approach, and supplemented by leading relativistic, qu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042814] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a high-precision ab initio calculation of the photodetachment energy of the hydrogen anion, i.e., the electron affinity of hydrogen.
motivation: The hydrogen anion is a fundamental three-body Coulomb system, and its electron affinity is important for precision atomic physics and testing bound-state quantum electrodynamics.
method: The authors compute the nonrelativistic bound-state energy using an exact three-body approach and add leading relativistic and QED corrections.
result: They obtain a high-precision theoretical value for the photodetachment energy of H−, improving agreement with precision spectroscopy and benchmarking theory.
conclusion: The work provides a refined theoretical electron affinity of hydrogen, relevant to atomic physics metrology and QED tests rather than quantum information science.

title: Dynamical Evolution Of Quantum Scattering In ${\mathrm{Li}}^{+}+{\mathrm{H}}^{−}$ Mutual Neutralization From The meV/u To The keV/u Regime
authors: Kun Wang, Yu Wang, Xiao He Lin, Yong Wu, Yi Zhi Qu, And Yu Kun Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Kun Wang, Yu Wang, Xiao He Lin, Yong Wu, Yi Zhi Qu, and Yu Kun Yang

Using a fully quantum molecular-orbital close-coupling approach with ab initio potentials, we evaluate the dynamical evolution of reaction mechanisms in [MATH] mutual neutralization across collision energies from [MATH] to ${10}^{3}{0ex}}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042815] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantum scattering dynamics of Li+ + H- mutual neutralization over collision energies from meV/u to keV/u using molecular-orbital close-coupling calculations.
motivation: Mutual neutralization in ion-atom collisions is important for understanding charge-transfer and reactive processes in astrophysical and laboratory plasmas.
method: A fully quantum molecular-orbital close-coupling approach with ab initio potential energy surfaces is used to compute the dynamical evolution of reaction mechanisms across a wide energy range.
result: The authors identify how different reaction pathways and quantum interference effects govern mutual neutralization as collision energy varies from the meV/u to keV/u regime.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed quantum-scattering characterization of Li+ + H- neutralization, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pressure-tuned Flat-band Instability And Magnetic Suppression In ${\mathrm{SmCrGe}}_{3}$
authors: Wenli Bi, Cheng Peng, Francisco J. Canales, James Petri, Mingyu Xu, Dongzhou Zhang, And Weiwei Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Wenli Bi, Cheng Peng, Francisco J. Canales, James Petri, Mingyu Xu, Dongzhou Zhang, and Weiwei Xie

Pressure provides a clean and continuous route for tuning electronic structure and magnetic interactions in itinerant ferromagnets without introducing chemical disorder. Here, we report high-pressure structural, transport, and electronic structure studies of hexagonal ferromagnetic ${…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194420] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: High-pressure structural, transport, and electronic-structure measurements on the hexagonal itinerant ferromagnet SmCrGe3 reveal pressure-driven suppression of magnetism tied to a flat-band instability.
motivation: Pressure offers a clean, disorder-free tuning knob for electronic structure and magnetic interactions in itinerant ferromagnets, motivating a systematic study of how compression alters flat-band physics and magnetic order in SmCrGe3.
method: The authors combine high-pressure structural characterization, electrical transport measurements, and electronic structure calculations on hexagonal SmCrGe3 across a range of applied pressures.
result: Increasing pressure suppresses the ferromagnetic state while driving a flat-band-related electronic instability, as seen in the transport response and corroborated by calculated band structure.
conclusion: The work establishes pressure as an effective means of tuning flat-band-driven magnetism in Cr-based intermetallics, clarifying the coupling between band topology, electronic correlations, and magnetic order.

title: Propagation And Localization Of Spin Excitations At Altermagnetic Domain Walls
authors: Oksana Peschanska, Jeroen van Den Brink, And Volodymyr P. Kravchuk
abstract:
Author(s): Oksana Peschanska, Jeroen van den Brink, and Volodymyr P. Kravchuk

Altermagnets ([MATH]) are spin-compensated materials in which opposite-spin sublattices are connected by a symmetry that causes a spin splitting in their elementary excitations. As there is a strong effect of altermagnetism on domain wall properties, it is quite natural to also expect an enric…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194421] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how spin excitations propagate and localize at domain walls in altermagnets, spin-compensated magnets with symmetry-linked spin-split bands.
motivation: Altermagnetism strongly modifies domain wall properties, so the authors expect similarly rich physics for the elementary excitations bound to or scattered by such walls.
method: Theoretical analysis of the spin-wave spectrum and scattering/localization behavior for domain wall configurations in an altermagnetic order parameter, presumably within a linear spin-wave or Landau-Lifshitz framework.
result: Domain walls are shown to support localized spin-excitation modes and to modify the propagation of spin waves, with characteristics tied to the altermagnetic spin splitting.
conclusion: Altermagnetic domain walls act as nontrivial channels and traps for spin excitations, offering a route to control magnetization dynamics in altermagnets.

title: Electron-doping-induced Multiferroicity In A One-dimensional ${\mathrm{NbI}}_{3}$ Chain
authors: Zhen Zhang, Jing-Yang You, And Lixing Kang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen Zhang, Jing-Yang You, and Lixing Kang

Multiferroic materials are of great importance for the development of next-generation multifunctional devices. Here, we predict a stable one-dimensional (1D) antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductor [MATH] chain, in which moderate electron doping induces site-centered charge order, ferrim…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204426] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The authors predict a stable one-dimensional antiferromagnetic semiconducting NbI3 chain in which moderate electron doping induces site-centered charge order and ferrimagnetic/multiferroic behavior.
motivation: Multiferroic materials are attractive for next-generation multifunctional devices, and the authors aim to identify a stable one-dimensional platform that realizes multiferroicity via carrier doping rather than chemical substitution.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations are used to assess the structural stability, electronic structure, and magnetic order of the 1D NbI3 chain, with electron doping introduced to induce charge ordering and ferrimagnetism.
result: The pristine chain is a stable 1D antiferromagnetic semiconductor; moderate electron doping drives site-centered charge order and a ferrimagnetic multiferroic state.
conclusion: The 1D NbI3 chain is proposed as a candidate doping-tunable multiferroic, suggesting low-dimensional materials as a route to multifunctional device applications.

title: Magnetic Symmetry Implications Of The Zero- And Applied-field Hall Effect Of ${\mathrm{UNi}}_{4}\mathrm{B}$
authors: Z. W. Riedel, W. S. Simeth, S. M. Thomas, F. Ronning, And E. D. Bauer
abstract:
Author(s): Z. W. Riedel, W. S. Simeth, S. M. Thomas, F. Ronning, and E. D. Bauer

The authors report here two finite zero-field Hall resistivity tensor components associated with the debated magnetic ground state of the noncollinear antiferromagnet UNi
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214426] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports two finite zero-field Hall resistivity tensor components in the noncollinear antiferromagnet UNi4B, arguing they imply a monoclinic magnetic symmetry lower than previously proposed ordering models.
motivation: The magnetic ground state of UNi4B is debated, and zero-field Hall resistivity can serve as a symmetry-sensitive probe of the underlying magnetic order.
method: Temperature- and field-dependent Hall resistivity measurements up to 16 T are analyzed within magnetic symmetry constraints for a commensurate magnetic structure, ruling out magnetic domains as the origin of the finite components.
result: Finite zero-field Hall resistivity components are observed that are incompatible with previously proposed magnetic structures but consistent with a monoclinic magnetic symmetry; the field data indicate a notable intrinsic contribution to the anomalous Hall effect.
conclusion: The Hall response constrains the magnetic symmetry of UNi4B and points to a lower-symmetry commensurate order, highlighting intrinsic anomalous Hall contributions in this antiferromagnet.

title: Frustration-induced Dimensional Reduction And Coexistence Of Long- And Short-range Magnetic Order In ${\mathrm{NdCl}}_{3}$
authors: Eli Zoghlin, Matthew B. Stone, Vasile O. Garlea, Matthias D. Frontzek, Andrew D. Christianson, And Andrew F. May
abstract:
Author(s): Eli Zoghlin, Matthew B. Stone, Vasile O. Garlea, Matthias D. Frontzek, Andrew D. Christianson, and Andrew F. May

The phenomenon of frustration greatly enriches the accessible physics of quantum magnets. With this in mind, we study the magnetism of [MATH] using a combination of bulk property measurements and neutron scattering techniques. The low-temperature heat capacity reveals two magnetic tra…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214427] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering and bulk measurements reveal frustration-induced dimensional reduction and coexisting long- and short-range magnetic order in NdCl3.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how magnetic frustration enriches the physics of quantum magnets, using NdCl3 as a case study.
method: They combine bulk property measurements, including low-temperature heat capacity, with neutron scattering techniques to probe the magnetic order.
result: The measurements reveal two magnetic transitions and coexistence of long- and short-range magnetic order, interpreted as frustration-induced dimensional reduction.
conclusion: NdCl3 provides an example of frustrated magnetism where dimensional reduction and mixed magnetic order emerge, but the work is outside quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ab Initio Electronic Conductivity Of Fe-bearing Post-perovskite
authors: Yihang Peng, Yupei Zhang, Shuai Zhang, Chenxing Luo, Donghao Zheng, Nelson Naveas, Xifan Wu, And Jie Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Yihang Peng, Yupei Zhang, Shuai Zhang, Chenxing Luo, Donghao Zheng, Nelson Naveas, Xifan Wu, and Jie Deng

The electrical conductivity of high-pressure silicates profoundly influences the interior dynamics of rocky planets. Employing the Kubo-Greenwood formalism, we perform ab initio calculations of electronic conductivity in Fe-bearing post-perovskite under super-Earth mantle conditions, up to 4000 K an…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225139] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: Ab initio Kubo-Greenwood calculations of the electronic conductivity of Fe-bearing post-perovskite under super-Earth mantle conditions (up to 4000 K).
motivation: The electrical conductivity of high-pressure silicate phases governs heat transport, magnetic field generation, and interior dynamics of rocky planets, so a first-principles understanding of Fe-bearing post-perovskite conductivity is needed.
method: Kubo-Greenwood linear-response formalism combined with ab initio electronic structure calculations (density functional theory / molecular dynamics) at extreme pressures and temperatures.
result: Predicted electronic conductivity values for Fe-bearing post-perovskite over the super-Earth mantle pressure-temperature range, quantifying the contribution of iron and temperature to conductivity enhancement.
conclusion: The computed conductivity constrains the thermal and electrical structure of super-Earth interiors, informing models of mantle dynamics and possible dynamo action.

title: Effect Of Coulomb Correlation In The Generalized Einstein Relation In Disordered Organic Semiconductors
authors: Zihan Wang, Meiqin Han, Haitao Ling, Yilong Wang, Haorong Zhu, Jiawei Wang, Guofu Zhou, And Feilong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zihan Wang, Meiqin Han, Haitao Ling, Yilong Wang, Haorong Zhu, Jiawei Wang, Guofu Zhou, and Feilong Liu

The Einstein relation linking charge carrier mobility and diffusion coefficient is a fundamental principle of charge transport. However, in disordered organic semiconductors, energetic disorder and carrier filling in localized states lead to a concentration-dependent diffusivity–mobility ratio descr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194206] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how Coulomb correlation modifies the generalized Einstein relation between charge-carrier mobility and diffusion coefficient in disordered organic semiconductors.
motivation: The classical Einstein relation between mobility and diffusivity can fail in disordered organic semiconductors because energetic disorder and carrier filling in localized states produce a concentration-dependent diffusivity-mobility ratio.
method: The authors analyze charge transport in disordered organic semiconductors, incorporating Coulomb correlation effects into the generalized Einstein relation.
result: Coulomb correlation is shown to affect the generalized Einstein relation and the concentration dependence of the diffusivity-mobility ratio in these materials.
conclusion: The work clarifies how Coulomb interactions should be included when relating mobility and diffusion in disordered organic semiconductor transport models.

title: Contrasting Anomalous Hall Mechanisms In ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{5}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$: Intrinsic Berry Curvature And The Emergence Of Skew Scattering
authors: Jyoti Saini, Siddharth Kumar, Ankita Tiwari, Pawan Kumar Srivastava, Changgu Lee, And Subhasis Ghosh
abstract:
Author(s): Jyoti Saini, Siddharth Kumar, Ankita Tiwari, Pawan Kumar Srivastava, Changgu Lee, and Subhasis Ghosh

We report a comparative study of the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in single crystals of the two-dimensional van der Waals (vdWs) ferromagnets [MATH] and [MATH], grown by chemical vapor transport, over wide temperature and magnetic-fi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225133] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A comparative experimental study of anomalous Hall effect mechanisms in the van der Waals ferromagnets Fe3GeTe2 and Fe5GeTe2, separating intrinsic Berry-curvature contributions from skew scattering.
motivation: The origin of the anomalous Hall effect in 2D vdW ferromagnets remains debated, with intrinsic Berry curvature and extrinsic skew-scattering mechanisms both proposed; a systematic comparison across two related compounds can disentangle them.
method: Single crystals of Fe3GeTe2 and Fe5GeTe2 were grown by chemical vapor transport and their Hall resistivity measured over wide temperature and magnetic-field ranges, with scaling analysis used to identify the dominant AHE mechanism.
result: The two compounds show contrasting AHE behavior, with one dominated by intrinsic Berry curvature and the other exhibiting signatures of skew scattering, as revealed by the temperature and conductivity scaling of the anomalous Hall conductivity.
conclusion: The work clarifies how extrinsic and intrinsic contributions compete in layered vdW ferromagnets, providing guidance for interpreting AHE data in 2D magnet systems.

title: Cascade Of Topological Phase Transitions And Revival Of Topological Zero Modes In Imperfect Double Helical Liquids
authors: Anna Ohorodnyk And Chen-Hsuan Hsu
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Ohorodnyk and Chen-Hsuan Hsu

Two parallel helical edge channels hosting interacting electrons, when proximitized by local and nonlocal pairings, can host time-reversal-invariant pairs of topological zero modes at the system corners. Here, we show that realistic imperfections substantially enrich the physics of such proximitized…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235415] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how realistic imperfections affect topological zero modes in proximitized double helical liquid systems and predicts cascades of topological phase transitions.
motivation: Double helical edge channels with local and nonlocal pairings can host time-reversal-invariant topological zero modes, but realistic imperfections are expected to modify this physics substantially.
method: The authors theoretically analyze interacting helical edge channels in double helical liquids under local and nonlocal superconducting proximity effects, incorporating realistic imperfections to map the resulting topological phase diagram.
result: Imperfections are shown to produce a cascade of topological phase transitions and a revival of topological zero modes in regimes where they might otherwise be absent.
conclusion: The work enriches the understanding of topological zero modes in proximitized helical liquids and highlights the importance of imperfections for topological phase behavior in such condensed-matter platforms.

title: Crystallography, Lorentz Violation, And The Standard-model Extension
authors: Marco Schreck And Rogeres A. S. Magalhães
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Schreck and Rogeres A. S. Magalhães

The motivation behind the present work is to adopt methodology from field theory and high-energy physics to crystallography. In particular, we establish a relationship between the electromagnetic sector of the standard-model extension (SME) for Lorentz invariance violation and optical media. At an e…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194418] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper imports methodology from Lorentz-violating quantum field theory (the Standard-Model Extension) into crystallography to describe light propagation in optical media.
motivation: The authors aim to bridge high-energy physics and crystallography by showing that the electromagnetic sector of the Standard-Model Extension for Lorentz invariance violation can be mapped onto the physics of optical media.
method: They establish a formal correspondence between SME coefficients and the effective description of light in crystalline/optical media, then analyze how crystal symmetries constrain the allowed Lorentz-violating terms.
result: The mapping yields a dictionary relating crystallographic symmetry classes to admissible SME operator structures, indicating that condensed-matter crystals can serve as tabletop analogues for Lorentz-violation phenomenology.
conclusion: Crystallography offers a practical framework for interpreting and testing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics, though the work remains within field theory and materials physics rather than quantum information.

title: Anomalous Hall Enhancement In Fully Compensated Noncollinear Antiferromagnetic Cr-doped ${\mathrm{Mn}}_{3}\mathrm{Sn}$
authors: Ying Zhang, Xin Chen, Hang Xie, Ziyan Luo, Yihong Wu, And Lei Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Ying Zhang, Xin Chen, Hang Xie, Ziyan Luo, Yihong Wu, and Lei Shen (沈雷)

The noncollinear antiferromagnet (AFM), [MATH], exhibits ultrafast spin dynamics and negligible stray fields, making it a promising candidate for fast and energy-efficient spintronic devices. However, its practical applications remain limited by the relatively small Hall resp…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204422] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies enhancement of the anomalous Hall response in Cr-doped noncollinear antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn for spintronic applications.
motivation: Noncollinear antiferromagnets such as Mn3Sn offer ultrafast spin dynamics and negligible stray fields, but their small Hall response limits practical spintronic use.
method: The authors investigate Cr doping in fully compensated Mn3Sn and analyze its effect on the anomalous Hall signal, likely using first-principles or electronic-structure calculations.
result: Cr doping is reported to enhance the anomalous Hall response in the fully compensated noncollinear antiferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: The work suggests Cr-doped Mn3Sn as a promising materials platform for energy-efficient spintronic devices, but it lies outside the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems directions.

title: Control Of Phase Transition Patterning In The Wake Of $\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}→\mathrm{C}$ Reaction Fronts
authors: N. Maton, G. Facchini, And A. de Wit
abstract:
Author(s): N. Maton, G. Facchini, and A. De Wit

When two initially separated reactants A and B are put in contact, a chemical front can develop if a bimolecular [MATH] reaction interplays with diffusion. In the case of a precipitation reaction, a phase transition may occur in the wake of this reaction front provided th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044218] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how phase-transition patterning emerges in the wake of classical A+B→C reaction fronts controlled by diffusion and precipitation.
motivation: The authors aim to understand spatial pattern formation when a bimolecular reaction front couples to diffusion and a precipitation phase transition occurs behind the front.
method: The work analyzes reaction-diffusion fronts for an A+B→C bimolecular reaction, focusing on conditions under which precipitation and phase-transition patterning arise in the front wake.
result: The paper identifies control parameters governing phase-transition patterning behind the reaction front, likely through analytical or numerical modeling of the front dynamics.
conclusion: The findings clarify how reaction-front dynamics and precipitation combine to produce structured phase patterns, but the work is classical physical chemistry rather than quantum information science.

title: Comparing Different Physics Fields Using Statistical Linguistics
authors: María Fernanda Sánchez-Puig, Carlos Gershenson, And Carlos Pineda
abstract:
Author(s): María Fernanda Sánchez-Puig, Carlos Gershenson, and Carlos Pineda

The large digital archives of the American Physical Society (APS) offer an opportunity to quantitatively analyze the structure and evolution of scientific communication. In this paper, we perform a comparative analysis of the language used in eight APS journals (Phys. Rev. A, B, C, D, E, Lett., X, R…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044320] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses statistical linguistics to compare the language and structure of scientific communication across eight APS journals.
motivation: Large digital archives provide an opportunity to quantitatively study how scientific fields differ in their communication patterns and how these patterns evolve.
method: The authors perform a comparative statistical-linguistic analysis of text from eight Physical Review journals, examining word usage and linguistic features across fields.
result: The analysis reveals quantifiable differences in language and terminology among the APS journals, reflecting distinct field-specific communication structures.
conclusion: Statistical linguistics can characterize and compare scientific disciplines, but the work is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Unambiguous Characterization Of In-plane Dielectric Response In Nanoconfined Liquids: Water As A Case Study
authors: Jon Zubeltzu
abstract:
Author(s): Jon Zubeltzu

The in-plane dielectric constant of nanoconfined water has attracted growing interest in recent years. Nevertheless, assigning a bulklike dielectric constant to a molecularly thin film is convention dependent because it requires choosing an effective water width. We propose the in-plane 2D polarizab…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045505] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a convention-independent framework for characterizing the in-plane dielectric response of nanoconfined water using a two-dimensional polarizability description.
motivation: The in-plane dielectric constant of molecularly thin water films is ambiguous because assigning a bulk-like dielectric constant depends on an arbitrary effective width convention.
method: The authors introduce an in-plane 2D polarizability formulation and apply it to nanoconfined water as a case study, likely using molecular simulation or theoretical modeling.
result: The proposed 2D polarizability approach provides an unambiguous characterization of the in-plane dielectric response without requiring an effective water width.
conclusion: The work clarifies how to define and quantify dielectric properties of nanoconfined liquids, with water serving as a representative example.

title: Dynamical Mean-field Theory Of Active, Self-interacting Heteropolymers
authors: Andriy Goychuk
abstract:
Author(s): Andriy Goychuk

Analytical theories of polymer dynamics typically focus on the linear response around some steady state obtained via perturbative calculations. The present study derives a dynamical, nonlinear mean-field theory that yields unified access to the evolution of conformations, contact probabilities, and …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045406] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a dynamical nonlinear mean-field theory for active, self-interacting heteropolymers to describe conformational evolution and contact probabilities.
motivation: Analytical theories of polymer dynamics often rely on linear response around steady states, limiting their applicability to nonlinear, nonequilibrium behavior in active self-interacting heteropolymers.
method: The author derives a dynamical mean-field theory that provides unified access to polymer conformations, contact probabilities, and related observables beyond perturbative linear-response approaches.
result: The theory yields a nonlinear mean-field description of active heteropolymer dynamics, enabling calculation of conformational and contact statistics within a single framework.
conclusion: This work extends analytical polymer dynamics to active, self-interacting heteropolymers and offers a mean-field framework for studying their nonequilibrium behavior.

title: Flexoelectricity-driven Softening Of Bend Elasticity Leads To Spontaneous Chiral Symmetry Breaking In A Polar Fluid
authors: Aitor Erkoreka, Josu Martinez-Perdiguero, Luka Cmok, Ema Hanžel, Jordan Hobbs, Calum J. Gibb, Richard J. Mandle, Nerea Sebastián, And Alenka Mertelj
abstract:
Author(s): Aitor Erkoreka, Josu Martinez-Perdiguero, Luka Cmok, Ema Hanžel, Jordan Hobbs, Calum J. Gibb, Richard J. Mandle, Nerea Sebastián, and Alenka Mertelj

Pretransitional fluctuations show that flexoelectric coupling between polarization and molecular shape drives achiral fluids to spontaneously form chiral heliconical structures through polar biaxial ordering.

#ElegantVisuals #TheoryExperiment #SoftMatterSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045407] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: Flexoelectric coupling between polarization and molecular shape in an achiral polar fluid softens bend elasticity and drives spontaneous chiral heliconical ordering.
motivation: The work addresses how achiral fluids can spontaneously form chiral structures, focusing on pretransitional fluctuations and the role of flexoelectricity in soft-matter ordering.
method: The authors combine theory and experiment to study pretransitional fluctuations in a polar fluid, analyzing flexoelectric coupling and polar biaxial ordering.
result: Flexoelectric coupling is shown to soften bend elasticity, leading to spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking and heliconical structure formation.
conclusion: The findings establish a mechanism for chirality emergence in achiral polar fluids via flexoelectricity-driven elastic softening.

title: Information-energy Tradeoffs In An Escape-rate Population Model
authors: Nalin Dhiman And Siddharth Panwar
abstract:
Author(s): Nalin Dhiman and Siddharth Panwar

Efficient coding of dynamical signals requires neural activity to balance information transmission against firing cost on the timescale of the input. We study this balance in a stochastic escape-rate population with membrane filtering, adaptation, and weak mean-field feedback. A cross-validated deco…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044129] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes information-energy tradeoffs in a stochastic escape-rate neural population model with membrane filtering, adaptation, and weak mean-field feedback.
motivation: Neural systems must balance efficient information transmission against metabolic firing costs on the timescale of input signals.
method: The authors study a stochastic escape-rate population model and use cross-validated decoding to quantify information transmission under firing-cost constraints.
result: The model characterizes how membrane filtering, adaptation, and weak feedback shape the tradeoff between encoded information and energy expenditure.
conclusion: The work provides insight into neural coding efficiency but is outside the user's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems research directions.

title: Mean Maximum Of Fractional Brownian Motion
authors: Safari Mukeru And Mmboniseni P. Mulaudzi
abstract:
Author(s): Safari Mukeru and Mmboniseni P. Mulaudzi

Fractional Brownian motion is a paradigmatic non-Markovian Gaussian process characterized by the Hurst exponent [MATH]. Despite its simple scaling form, extremal observables of fractional Brownian motion are notoriously difficult to analyze, and exact results are rare. We consider the mean of the maxim…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044132] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the mean maximum of fractional Brownian motion, a non-Markovian Gaussian process, and derives exact or asymptotic results for this extremal observable.
motivation: Fractional Brownian motion has a simple scaling form, but extremal observables such as the maximum are difficult to analyze and exact results are rare.
