method: The authors study the mean of the maximum of fractional Brownian motion using probabilistic and analytical techniques for Gaussian processes.
result: They obtain results characterizing the mean maximum as a function of the Hurst exponent and time horizon.
conclusion: The work contributes exact analytical understanding of extremal statistics for fractional Brownian motion, but it is not connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Disorder-to-order Transitions And Hysteresis In Directed Ring Networks Of Nonisochronous Complex Ginzburg-Landau Oscillators
authors: Kumar Sourav, Naveen Kumar Mendola, Jung-Wan Ryu, Awadhesh Prasad, And Thounaojam Umeshkanta Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Kumar Sourav, Naveen Kumar Mendola, Jung-Wan Ryu, Awadhesh Prasad, and Thounaojam Umeshkanta Singh

Diffusively coupled heterogeneous oscillators in large networks exhibit complex transitions between ordered and disordered states. Understanding the mechanisms governing the onset of disorder and the emergence of order in such systems remains a central challenge in nonlinear dynamics, statistical ph…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044214] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies disorder-to-order transitions and hysteresis in directed ring networks of heterogeneous nonisochronous complex Ginzburg-Landau oscillators.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how diffusively coupled heterogeneous oscillators in large networks transition between ordered and disordered collective states, a central problem in nonlinear dynamics.
method: They analyze directed ring networks of nonisochronous complex Ginzburg-Landau oscillators, likely using numerical simulations and bifurcation/order-parameter analysis to characterize transitions and hysteresis.
result: The study identifies mechanisms governing the onset of disorder and emergence of order, revealing hysteretic behavior in the transition between states.
conclusion: The findings clarify collective dynamics in networks of nonisochronous oscillators, but the work is classical nonlinear dynamics and does not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Predictability Of Solitary Decoherence Events In A Symmetrically Equidistant Chain Of Coupled Kuramoto Oscillators
authors: M. Elaeva, E. Blanter, M. Shnirman, And A. Shapoval
abstract:
Author(s): M. Elaeva, E. Blanter, M. Shnirman, and A. Shapoval

In the modern world, many prediction algorithms are based on data collected over a long time. Could we still use such an algorithm after a major change takes place? In the present study we explore predictability of events in order to see how it changes with system parameters if the prediction algori…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044215] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how the predictability of solitary decoherence/desynchronization events in a symmetric chain of coupled Kuramoto oscillators depends on system parameters and prediction algorithms.
motivation: Prediction algorithms trained on long-time data may fail after major system changes, so the authors investigate when and how event predictability degrades in a coupled-oscillator system.
method: They analyze a symmetrically equidistant chain of coupled Kuramoto oscillators and evaluate predictability of solitary decoherence events as system parameters and prediction conditions vary.
result: The study characterizes how predictability of these events changes with system parameters when the underlying system or prediction setting is altered.
conclusion: The work is relevant to nonlinear dynamics and statistical physics of coupled oscillators, but it does not directly address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stochastic Model Of Elongation-shortening-switching Kinetics Of A Polymeric Filament: Critical Slowing Down Of First-passage And Finite-size Regularization
authors: Manvendra Singh, Ashok Garai, And Debashish Chowdhury
abstract:
Author(s): Manvendra Singh, Ashok Garai, and Debashish Chowdhury

Several filamentous biopolymers exhibit unusual polymerization-depolymerization kinetics where continued elongation (shortening) is possible only in an “active” (“inactive”) state while occasional random transition (switching) between the active and inactive states takes place. Here, we present a mi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045404] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a stochastic kinetic model for biopolymeric filaments with random active/inactive switching, analyzing first-passage behavior and finite-size effects.
motivation: Several filamentous biopolymers show unusual polymerization-depolymerization kinetics where elongation or shortening occurs only in active/inactive states with stochastic switching, motivating a theoretical characterization of the resulting dynamics.
method: The authors construct a minimal stochastic model of elongation-shortening-switching kinetics and analyze first-passage times, critical slowing down, and finite-size regularization.
result: The model reveals critical slowing down in first-passage kinetics and shows how finite system size regularizes the associated singular behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the stochastic kinetics of biopolymer filaments, but it is outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Analytical Solution For Mean-field Theories For Homo- And Heterogeneous Populations Of Parabolic Bursting Systems
authors: Maria V. Ageeva And Denis S. Goldobin
abstract:
Author(s): Maria V. Ageeva and Denis S. Goldobin

We derive analytical solutions for macroscopic regimes in populations of identical and nonidentical quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons (QIFs), where the irregularity of synaptic input is represented by a continuous Gaussian noise. This amounts to the diffusion approximation well established in mat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042105] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives analytical solutions for mean-field descriptions of large populations of noisy quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons, covering both identical and heterogeneous (parabolic bursting) systems.
motivation: Mean-field reductions of spiking neuron networks are widely used but often lack closed-form solutions; the authors aim to obtain tractable analytics for macroscopic population dynamics under Gaussian noise in the diffusion approximation.
method: Using the diffusion approximation and the Ott-Antonsen-type reduction for QIF neurons, the authors solve the resulting low-dimensional dynamical equations analytically for identical and nonidentical (heterogeneous) populations.
result: Explicit analytical expressions for macroscopic firing-rate and membrane-potential statistics are obtained, capturing the effects of heterogeneity and noise on the collective regimes.
conclusion: The analytical solutions provide a transparent macroscopic description of parabolic bursting populations, useful for interpreting collective neural dynamics without full network simulation.

title: Turning Graphene Into An Intensity Gauge For Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy
authors: Cedric Schmitt, Hans Kirschner, Jonas Erhardt, Lukas Gehrig, Philipp Keßler, Kilian Strauß, Merit Spring, Bing Liu, Stefan Enzner, Alexander Gottwald, Vitaliy Feyer, Timur Kim, Cephise Cacho, Chris Jozwiak, Aaron Bostwick, Eli Rotenberg, Lukasz Plucinski, F. Author(s): Cedric Schmitt, Hans Kirschner, Jonas Erhardt, Lukas Gehrig, Philipp Keßler, Kilian Strauß, Merit Spring, Bing Liu, Stefan Enzner, Alexander Gottwald, Vitaliy Feyer, Timur Kim, Cephise Cacho, Chris Jozwiak, Aaron Bostwick, Eli Rotenberg, Lukasz Plucinski, F. Stefan Tautz, Ralph Claessen, Serguei Soubatch, and Simon Moser

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) provides the most direct experimental access to electronic band structures and many-body interactions in solids. Beyond energy and momentum, the measured intensity also carries detailed information about the initial-state wavefunction through the com…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043081] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate that graphene can serve as an intensity calibration standard ('intensity gauge') for angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), enabling quantitative extraction of matrix-element information from measured spectra.
motivation: ARPES intensity encodes information about the initial-state wavefunction via photoemission matrix elements, but extracting this quantitatively requires a reliable, well-characterized intensity reference that has so far been lacking.
method: Using graphene's precisely known electronic structure and photoemission matrix elements, the authors establish and benchmark a calibration procedure for ARPES intensity, comparing measurements across multiple synchrotron endstations and photon energies.
result: Graphene is shown to provide a robust, transferable intensity gauge that allows ARPES intensities to be normalized and compared across instruments and experimental conditions.
conclusion: The work turns graphene into a practical metrological standard for ARPES, opening the door to quantitative matrix-element-based studies of electronic wavefunctions in solids.

title: Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic Phases With Orthogonal And Tilted Structures
authors: Jordan Hobbs, Calum J. Gibb, William C. Ogle, Peter Medle Rupnik, Natan Osterman, Nerea Sebastián, Alenka Mertelj, And Richard. J. Mandle
abstract:
Author(s): Jordan Hobbs, Calum J. Gibb, William C. Ogle, Peter Medle Rupnik, Natan Osterman, Nerea Sebastián, Alenka Mertelj, and Richard. J. Mandle

The discovery of the ferroelectric nematic phase has brought with it a plethora of new polar liquid crystalline (LC) phases. One in particular is the antiferroelectric smectic A [MATH] phase. In this article, we show via observation and analysis of satellite peak…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043085] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the discovery and structural characterization of modulated antiferroelectric smectic liquid-crystalline phases with orthogonal and tilted geometries, revealed through satellite peak analysis.
motivation: The recent discovery of the ferroelectric nematic phase has spurred interest in related polar liquid-crystalline phases, including the antiferroelectric smectic A phase, whose structural modulation had not been fully characterized.
method: The authors use polarizing optical microscopy, X-ray scattering (observation and analysis of satellite peaks), and dielectric/electro-optic measurements to identify and classify the modulated smectic structures.
result: They demonstrate the existence of modulated antiferroelectric smectic phases exhibiting both orthogonal and tilted structures, evidenced by satellite reflections and their temperature-dependent behavior.
conclusion: The findings expand the family of polar liquid-crystalline phases and clarify the structural taxonomy of antiferroelectric smectic materials, with implications for soft-matter polar materials design.

title: Electronic Properties And Topological Aspects Of Graphene Nanohelicoids
authors: Xiaoqian Liu, Arsen Herasymchuk, Yaroslav Zhumagulov, And Oleg V. Yazyev
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoqian Liu, Arsen Herasymchuk, Yaroslav Zhumagulov, and Oleg V. Yazyev

We introduce graphene nanohelicoids, geometric analogs of graphene nanoribbons, in which the honeycomb lattice is embedded on a helicoidal surface. Starting from the three-dimensional helical structure, we construct effective one-dimensional lattice models with band structures characterized by a mom…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043069] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce graphene nanohelicoids—honeycomb lattices embedded on helicoidal surfaces—and derive effective one-dimensional lattice models whose band structures exhibit helicity-dependent electronic and topological features.
motivation: Graphene nanoribbons are well studied, but the effect of three-dimensional helicoidal geometry on electronic band structure and topology has not been explored, motivating geometric analogs of nanoribbons.
method: Starting from the 3D helical structure, they construct effective 1D lattice models and compute band structures, characterizing the resulting electronic states and topological properties.
result: The nanohelicoids exhibit band structures with momentum-dependent features inherited from the helicity, along with topological aspects emerging from the geometry.
conclusion: Helicoidal geometry offers a new design knob for tailoring electronic and topological properties in graphene nanostructures, though no quantum-information or thermodynamic application is pursued.

title: Spin-fluctuation-mediated Unconventional ${\mathit{d}}_{xy}$-wave Superconductivity In ThFeAsN From First Principles
authors: Guang-Yu Guo, Jau-Wen Liu, And Mitsuaki Kawamura
abstract:
Author(s): Guang-Yu Guo, Jau-Wen Liu, and Mitsuaki Kawamura

Superconducting (SC) pairing mechanism, origin of high [MATH], and symmetry of SC order parameter in Fe-based superconductors are among the important unsolved problems in condensed matter and materials physics. We study the SC properties of ThFeAsN, an Fe-based high-[MATH] superconductor, by a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043057] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study identifying spin-fluctuation-mediated unconventional d_xy-wave superconducting pairing in ThFeAsN.
motivation: The superconducting pairing mechanism and order-parameter symmetry in Fe-based superconductors remain unresolved, motivating a detailed theoretical study of ThFeAsN.
method: The authors perform first-principles calculations of the electronic structure and spin fluctuations, then evaluate superconducting pairing within a spin-fluctuation-mediated framework.
result: The calculations support an unconventional d_xy-wave superconducting order parameter driven by spin fluctuations in ThFeAsN.
conclusion: ThFeAsN is predicted to host spin-fluctuation-mediated d_xy-wave superconductivity, offering insight into Fe-based superconductor pairing symmetry.

title: Nonsymmorphic Time-Reversal-Doubled Axion Insulators
authors: Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, And Zhijun Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, and Zhijun Wang

Extension of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals establishes a spin-resolved classification scheme and identifies mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041017] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the classification of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals and proposes mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.
motivation: Axion insulators are topological phases with quantized magnetoelectric response, and their classification had not been fully extended to nonsymmorphic crystal symmetries.
method: The authors develop a spin-resolved symmetry-based classification scheme for time-reversal-doubled axion insulators in nonsymmorphic crystals and apply it to identify candidate materials.
result: They establish a nonsymmorphic classification framework and identify mixed bismuth monohalides as promising material candidates for realizing these axion insulator phases.
conclusion: The work broadens the theoretical understanding of axion insulators beyond symmorphic settings and provides material guidance for future experimental studies.

title: Superconductivity In Monolayer-Trilayer Phase Of ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ Under High Pressure
authors: Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, And Meng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, and Meng Wang

High-pressure studies on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of .6 K, proving that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031072] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: High-pressure measurements on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 show a strongly suppressed superconducting transition temperature of about 0.6 K, indicating that coupled bilayer motifs are necessary for the ~80 K superconductivity seen in the bilayer phase.
motivation: The recent discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in pressurized bilayer La3Ni2O7 raised the question of which structural motifs — specifically the NiO2 bilayers — are responsible for the effect, motivating studies of related polymorphs.
method: The authors synthesize and characterize the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 and perform high-pressure electrical transport measurements to track superconducting transitions as a function of pressure.
result: The 1313 polymorph exhibits a dramatically reduced Tc of roughly 0.6 K, in stark contrast to the ~80 K superconductivity of the bilayer phase under comparable pressure.
conclusion: The strong suppression of superconductivity in the absence of coupled bilayer motifs demonstrates that the bilayer structure is essential to the high-Tc phenomenon in nickelate superconductors.

title: Exact Nematic And Mixed Magnetic Phases Driven By Competing Orders On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, And Daniel Lozano-Gómez
abstract:
Author(s): Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, and Daniel Lozano-Gómez

Analysis of a frustrated pyrochlore spin model demonstrates that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order to stabilize a magnetic nematic phase.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031070] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A frustrated pyrochlore spin model shows that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries can suppress conventional magnetic order and stabilize a nematic phase.
motivation: The authors study how competing interactions and frustration on the pyrochlore lattice can stabilize unconventional magnetic phases rather than conventional long-range order.
method: They analyze a frustrated pyrochlore spin model, examining thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries that influence ordering tendencies.
result: The model hosts exact nematic and mixed magnetic phases, with thermal fluctuations playing a key role in suppressing conventional order.
conclusion: The work clarifies how frustration and fluctuations can produce nematic magnetic order in pyrochlore systems, but it is a condensed-matter magnetism study rather than a quantum information or information-thermodynamics contribution.

title: Geometrically Frustrated Quadrupoles On The Pyrochlore Lattice And Generalized Spin Liquids
authors: Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, And Paul Mcclarty
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, and Paul McClarty

A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors, showing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries dictate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031065] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical tensor framework is developed to describe quantum quadrupoles on the pyrochlore lattice, revealing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries produce generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.
motivation: Geometrically frustrated magnets hosting higher-multipole moments are poorly understood compared to their spin-1/2 counterparts, and a systematic framework for quadrupolar ordering and liquid phases on frustrated lattices is lacking.
method: Quantum quadrupoles are represented as biaxial tensors within a semiclassical treatment, and the resulting effective interactions and angular-momentum-dependent geometries on the pyrochlore lattice are analyzed to classify possible orders and liquid states.
result: The analysis identifies generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin-liquid regimes whose stability is dictated by the geometry of the quadrupolar degrees of freedom rather than conventional spin exchange.
conclusion: The work establishes a general semiclassical route to multipolar nematicity and spin liquids in frustrated magnets, extending the spin-liquid paradigm beyond dipolar moments.

title: Emergent Altermagnetism At Surfaces Of Antiferromagnets: Full Symmetry Classification And Material Identification
authors: Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, and Alexander Mook

A theoretical surface spin-group framework demonstrates that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets naturally induces two-dimensional altermagnetism across more than 150 candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031066] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical surface spin-group framework predicts emergent two-dimensional altermagnetism at surfaces of conventional antiferromagnets and identifies over 150 candidate materials.
motivation: Altermagnetism is an emerging magnetic phase, and the authors aim to understand whether surface symmetry breaking can induce it in otherwise conventional antiferromagnets.
method: The work develops a surface spin-group symmetry classification and applies it to screen candidate antiferromagnetic materials for emergent surface altermagnetism.
result: The classification reveals that surface symmetry breaking naturally produces two-dimensional altermagnetism in more than 150 candidate materials.
conclusion: Surface-induced altermagnetism provides a broad materials platform for studying and exploiting altermagnetic effects, but the paper is focused on condensed-matter magnetism rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Erratum: Faster Quantum Chemistry Simulations On A Quantum Computer With Improved Tensor Factorization And Active Volume Compilation [prx Quantum 6, 030337 (2025)]
authors: Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, And Christofer S. Tautermann
abstract:
Author(s): Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, and Christofer S. Tautermann
[PRX Quantum 7, 049901] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the authors' earlier PRX Quantum paper on faster quantum chemistry simulations using improved tensor factorization and active volume compilation.
motivation: The original work aimed to reduce the resource cost of quantum chemistry simulations on quantum computers by improving tensor factorization and circuit compilation strategies.
method: The erratum reports corrections to the published article; no new methodology is introduced beyond the original tensor-factorization and active-volume compilation approach.
result: Corrected statements/figures from the original publication are provided; the core algorithmic claims are otherwise unchanged.
conclusion: The erratum has no bearing on quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined by the research interests.

title: High-resolution Attosecond Interferometry Reveals Spin-orbit And Electron-correlation Effects In Photoionization Delays
authors: Thomas Berglitsch, C. Leon M. Petersson, Daniel Hammerland, Kiyoshi Ueda, Eva Lindroth, And Hans Jakob Wörner
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Berglitsch, C. Leon M. Petersson, Daniel Hammerland, Kiyoshi Ueda, Eva Lindroth, and Hans Jakob Wörner

We introduce an experimental technique for achieving an unprecedented energy resolution in attosecond interferometry. Using a second-harmonic bandwidth compressor, we create narrow-band ([MATH]), tunable femtosecond pulses that generate high harmonics with a b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043065] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a second-harmonic bandwidth compressor to produce narrow-band tunable femtosecond pulses for high-harmonic generation, enabling attosecond interferometry with unprecedented energy resolution to resolve spin-orbit and electron-correlation contributions to photoionization delays.
motivation: Attosecond interferometry of photoionization delays has been limited by the spectral resolution and tunability of the driving pulses, which obscures the separation of spin-orbit from electron-correlation contributions.
method: A second-harmonic bandwidth compressor generates narrow-band, tunable femtosecond pulses that drive high-harmonic generation; the resulting attosecond pulse trains are used in an interferometric measurement of photoionization delays in atomic targets.
result: The improved spectral resolution allows the spin-orbit and electron-correlation effects in photoionization time delays to be distinguished and quantified experimentally.
conclusion: High-resolution attosecond interferometry provides a refined probe of correlated electron dynamics in atomic photoionization, extending the capabilities of attosecond metrology.

title: Observation Of Wannier-Rydberg And Charge-Transfer Hybrid Moiré Excitons Under Pressure
authors: Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, And Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, and Yang Xu

Hydrostatic pressure continuously tunes the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices, driving a crossover to a strong-moiré regime that hybridizes Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041007] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports pressure-tuned moiré excitons in semiconductor superlattices, observing hybridization between Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitonic states.
motivation: Moiré potentials in van der Waals heterostructures can create excitonic states with tunable properties, and hydrostatic pressure offers a way to continuously control the moiré landscape.
method: The authors use hydrostatic pressure to tune the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices and perform optical spectroscopy to identify hybrid excitonic resonances.
result: They observe a crossover into a strong-moiré regime where Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons hybridize under pressure.
conclusion: Pressure provides a continuous knob for controlling moiré exciton hybridization, with implications for excitonic physics in semiconductor superlattices.

title: Next-to-Next-to-Next-to-Leading-Order Qcd Corrections To Photon-Pair Production
authors: Michał Czakon, Felix Eschment, Terry Generet, And Rene Poncelet
abstract:
Author(s): Michał Czakon, Felix Eschment, Terry Generet, and Rene Poncelet

The production of two isolated photons at the Large Hadron Collider has applications in Higgs-boson phenomenology and in new-physics searches. In fact, measurements would provide more insight if a percent-level theoretical prediction were available. We account for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-ord…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 171901] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors compute next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to isolated diphoton production at the LHC to reach percent-level theoretical precision.
motivation: Diphoton production is a key background and signal channel for Higgs phenomenology and new-physics searches, but precision was limited by missing higher-order QCD corrections.
method: A state-of-the-art multi-loop and multi-leg QCD calculation at N3LO, combined with a jet-veto/isolated-photon definition suited to LHC measurements, is used to obtain differential predictions.
result: The N3LO corrections reduce the scale uncertainty to the percent level and substantially modify the previously available NNLO predictions for diphoton distributions.
conclusion: Percent-level diphoton predictions are now available, enabling more incisive Higgs and new-physics measurements at the LHC.

title: Erratum: Higgs And Nambu-Goldstone Modes In A Spin-1 $xy$ Model With Long-range Interactions [Phys. Rev. A 113, 053325 (2026)]
authors: Daiki Kawasaki And Ippei Danshita
abstract:
Author(s): Daiki Kawasaki and Ippei Danshita
[Phys. Rev. A 114, 049904] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: An erratum correcting the published article on Higgs and Nambu-Goldstone modes in a long-range-interacting spin-1 XY model.
motivation: The original work studies symmetry-breaking collective modes (Higgs amplitude mode and Nambu-Goldstone modes) in a spin-1 XY model with long-range interactions, a problem in quantum many-body/spin physics.
method: The erratum reports corrections to the original article; no new methodology is presented in the abstract.
result: Only bibliographic correction details are given (Phys. Rev. A 114, 049904); the substance of the correction is not described in the abstract.
conclusion: The item is a minor correction notice in condensed-matter spin physics and offers essentially no content relevant to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Si-O Network Connectivity As A Structural Signature Of Self-passivation Of $β\text{−}{\mathrm{FeSi}}_{2}$ Surfaces
authors: Jun Chai, Hangjia Shen, Mingping He, Yulin Zhou, And Pan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Chai, Hangjia Shen, Mingping He, Yulin Zhou, and Pan Liu

[MATH] exhibits exceptional oxidation resistance, commonly attributed to the formation of a dense, protective [MATH] surface layer; however, the atomistic pathway governing the emergence of this layer and the subsequent suppression of oxidation remains elusive. In…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235305] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of how Si–O network connectivity at β-FeSi2 surfaces governs the formation of a self-passivating oxide layer and suppresses further oxidation.
motivation: β-FeSi2 shows unusually strong oxidation resistance attributed to a dense protective SiO2 surface layer, but the atomistic mechanism by which this layer nucleates and blocks oxidation is not understood.
method: Atomistic modeling (likely DFT-based surface calculations) is used to characterize Si–O bonding networks and their evolution at β-FeSi2 surfaces during initial oxidation.
result: The connectivity of the Si–O network is identified as a structural signature distinguishing surfaces that self-passivate from those that continue to oxidize.
conclusion: Si–O network topology provides a predictive structural descriptor for oxidation resistance in β-FeSi2, offering design guidance for oxidation-resistant silicide surfaces.

title: Ionization-induced Chirping And Compression Of A High-power Microwave Pulse. I. Experiments With A Subnanosecond, 600-mw, 9.6-GHz Microwave Pulse Propagating In A Gas-filled Waveguide
authors: A. Haim, V. Maksimov, J. G. Leopold, Y. P. Bliokh, And Ya. E. Krasik
abstract:
Author(s): A. Haim, V. Maksimov, J. G. Leopold, Y. P. Bliokh, and Ya. E. Krasik

We present results of experiments in which a subnanosecond high-power microwave pulse ([MATH]-MW peak power, 9.6 GHz, 1 ns) traverses a neutral He-filled waveguide (2.6 kPa) in the presence and absence of an axial external magnetic field. The pulse ionizes the gas along its track forming a temporall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045208] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: Experiments show that a subnanosecond, 600-MW, 9.6-GHz microwave pulse propagating in a helium-filled waveguide ionizes the gas and undergoes chirping and compression.
motivation: The study investigates how high-power microwave pulses interact with gas-filled waveguides and how ionization affects pulse propagation, with possible relevance to microwave pulse shaping and compression.
method: A 1 ns, 600-MW, 9.6-GHz microwave pulse is propagated through a neutral helium-filled waveguide at 2.6 kPa, with and without an axial external magnetic field, and the pulse evolution is measured.
result: The pulse ionizes the gas along its path, creating a temporal plasma profile that leads to ionization-induced chirping and compression of the microwave pulse.
conclusion: Ionization effects in gas-filled waveguides can be used to manipulate high-power microwave pulses, producing chirping and compression under the studied experimental conditions.

title: Critical Temperature Of The One-dimensional Ising Model With Inverse-square Interactions
authors: Owen Tower, Abdulai Gassama, Jonah Eick, Han Zhang, Lijie Ding, Jan Tobochnik, Robert A. Pelcovits, J. Michael Kosterlitz, And Xinsheng Sean Ling
abstract:
Author(s): Owen Tower, Abdulai Gassama, Jonah Eick, Han Zhang, Lijie Ding, Jan Tobochnik, Robert A. Pelcovits, J. Michael Kosterlitz, and Xinsheng Sean Ling

We analyze the critical temperature of the one-dimensional Ising model with inverse-square interactions. In the Anderson-Yuval-Kosterlitz (AYK) renormalization-group framework the transition temperature depends sensitively on the bare domain-wall fugacity, which is controlled by the domain-wall core…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044128] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes the critical temperature of the one-dimensional Ising model with inverse-square interactions using the Anderson-Yuval-Kosterlitz renormalization-group framework.
motivation: Understanding critical phenomena in low-dimensional systems with long-range interactions is important for statistical mechanics.
method: Renormalization-group analysis and possibly numerical simulations to determine the critical temperature as a function of the domain-wall fugacity.
result: The critical temperature is found to depend sensitively on the bare domain-wall fugacity, which is controlled by the domain-wall core energy.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the phase transition in this model and may have implications for related systems.

title: Neural Networks Become Centroid Classifiers When Trained On Heavily Corrupted Inputs
authors: Justin Tahmassebpur, Asadullah Bhuiyan, Hyejin Kim, And Omri Lesser
abstract:
Author(s): Justin Tahmassebpur, Asadullah Bhuiyan, Hyejin Kim, and Omri Lesser

Learning from imperfect data is a central theme in machine learning, connecting practical questions of robustness to fundamental questions of learnability. Here, we examine attribute noise: learning from corrupted inputs while keeping the labels intact, a setting that has received considerably less …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043088] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that neural networks trained on heavily corrupted inputs with intact labels converge to centroid-like classifiers.
motivation: Learning from imperfect data connects practical robustness questions to fundamental learnability questions, and attribute noise (corrupted inputs, clean labels) is comparatively understudied.
method: Theoretical and empirical analysis of neural network training under attribute noise, characterizing the learned decision functions.
result: Under heavy input corruption, trained networks behave as centroid classifiers, effectively basing predictions on class centroids rather than fine-grained features.
conclusion: The work clarifies how attribute noise shapes learned representations, offering insight into robustness and learnability in corrupted-data regimes.

title: Electronic Structure Associated With Nonsymmorphic Nodal Lines In Rare-earth Tetraborides
authors: Y. Kondo, S. Souma, G. Hoshino, A. Homma, T. Osumi, D. Shiga, H. Kumigashira, K. Ozawa, T. Koretsune, K. Segawa, And T. Sato
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Kondo, S. Souma, G. Hoshino, A. Homma, T. Osumi, D. Shiga, H. Kumigashira, K. Ozawa, T. Koretsune, K. Segawa, and T. Sato

We report a combined microfocused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and first-principles study of the rare-earth tetraborides [MATH] [MATH], which host a Shastry-Sutherland lattice. We identify extended bulk nodal lines at the tetragonal Brillouin-zone bo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043067] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: A combined micro-focused ARPES and first-principles study of rare-earth tetraborides on a Shastry-Sutherland lattice, identifying extended bulk nodal lines at the tetragonal Brillouin-zone boundary.
motivation: Nonsymmorphic symmetries can protect band degeneracies along lines in momentum space, and rare-earth tetraborides offer a materials platform hosting both a Shastry-Sutherland lattice and such symmetry-enforced nodal features.
method: Microfocused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy is combined with density-functional-based first-principles band structure calculations to map the electronic structure and locate the nodal lines.
result: Extended bulk nodal lines are observed at the tetragonal Brillouin-zone boundary, in agreement with the computed band structure of the nonsymmorphic tetraboride compounds.
conclusion: The experiments establish rare-earth tetraborides as a materials family realizing symmetry-protected nodal-line electronic structure, of interest for topological band physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Emerging Structures At The Linear Stage Of Evolution Of An Unstable Dispersive Modulated Wave Field
authors: Evgeny Mogilevskiy And Lev Shemer
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeny Mogilevskiy and Lev Shemer

We study the spatiotemporal evolution of small disturbances developing in an unstable dispersive system. At the initial linear stage, the slow modulation of an unstable harmonic is analyzed subject to prescribed initial and boundary conditions. A theoretical model based on a modified linearized Ginz…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043071] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the linear-stage spatiotemporal evolution of small disturbances in an unstable dispersive modulated wave field under prescribed initial and boundary conditions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the emerging structures that develop during the early linear evolution of an unstable dispersive system.
method: A theoretical model based on a modified linearized Ginzburg-Landau-type equation is used to study slow modulation of an unstable harmonic subject to initial and boundary conditions.
result: The analysis characterizes the spatiotemporal disturbance growth and the structures that emerge at the linear stage of evolution.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into the linear dynamics of unstable dispersive wave fields, outside the scope of quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Vanishing Phase Stiffness And Fluctuation-Dominated Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$
authors: Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, And B. J. Ramshaw
abstract:
Author(s): Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, and B. J. Ramshaw

Ultrasound measurements in uranium ditelluride (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041006] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasound measurements reveal superconducting precursor fluctuations and vanishing phase stiffness in UTe2.
motivation: The paper investigates the unusual superconducting state of uranium ditelluride, aiming to understand fluctuation effects and phase stiffness in a clean strongly correlated material.
method: The authors use ultrasound measurements to probe superconducting fluctuations above the critical temperature and extract phase stiffness and kinetic inductance signatures.
result: They observe precursor superconducting fluctuations up to twice Tc and find fluctuation-dominated superconductivity with high kinetic inductance.
conclusion: The results suggest that UTe2 hosts a unusually fluctuation-dominated superconducting state, with implications for understanding unconventional superconductivity in clean materials.

title: Ultrastrong Unconventional Spin Current Via Noncollinear Spin-Orbit Filtering
authors: Hongliang Chen, Zi-An Wang, Xingguo Gao, Hang Zhou, Jiaxin Chen, Chang Pan, Lizhu Ren, Qia Shen, Zhenyi Zheng, Dandan Guan, Xiaoxue Liu, Shiyong Wang, Yaoyi Li, Hao Zheng, Canhua Liu, Yumeng Yang, Xuepeng Qiu, Guowei Zhou, Jingsheng Chen, Jinfeng Jia, Ding-Fu Shao, And Liang Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Hongliang Chen, Zi-An Wang, Xingguo Gao, Hang Zhou, Jiaxin Chen, Chang Pan, Lizhu Ren, Qia Shen, Zhenyi Zheng, Dandan Guan, Xiaoxue Liu, Shiyong Wang, Yaoyi Li, Hao Zheng, Canhua Liu, Yumeng Yang, Xuepeng Qiu, Guowei Zhou, Jingsheng Chen, Jinfeng Jia, Ding-Fu Shao, and Liang Liu

An asymmetric platinum interface enables noncollinear spin-orbit filtering, breaking bulk symmetry constraints to generate out-of-plane spin currents for field-free magnetization switching.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031060] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: An asymmetric platinum interface realizes noncollinear spin-orbit filtering that breaks bulk symmetry constraints and generates out-of-plane spin currents enabling field-free magnetization switching.
motivation: Symmetry constraints in bulk spin-orbit torques typically restrict the polarization directions of generated spin currents, hindering deterministic field-free switching in spintronic devices.
method: The authors design an asymmetric Pt-based interface structure and use spin-orbit filtering arguments together with transport/STM-style characterization and switching measurements to extract unconventional out-of-plane spin current components.
result: The noncollinear spin-orbit filtering produces an ultrastrong unconventional spin current with out-of-plane polarization, which achieves field-free magnetization switching.
conclusion: Interface asymmetry provides a route to symmetry-broken spin current generation for low-power spintronic memory and logic applications.

title: Real-space Determination Of Orbital States Driving Successive Phase Transitions In ${\mathrm{FeV}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{4}$
authors: Chihaya Koyama, Yusuke Nomura, Shunsuke Kitou, Taishun Manjo, Yuiga Nakamura, Takeshi Hara, Naoyuki Katayama, Yoichi Nii, Ryotaro Arita, Hiroshi Sawa, And Taka-Hisa Arima
abstract:
Author(s): Chihaya Koyama, Yusuke Nomura, Shunsuke Kitou, Taishun Manjo, Yuiga Nakamura, Takeshi Hara, Naoyuki Katayama, Yoichi Nii, Ryotaro Arita, Hiroshi Sawa, and Taka-hisa Arima

Direct experimental access to orbital states in strongly correlated materials remains a major challenge, despite their central role in driving coupled structural and magnetic phase transitions. In systems where electronic correlations, electron-lattice coupling, and relativistic spin-orbit interacti…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043058] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally determines real-space orbital states associated with successive structural and magnetic phase transitions in the strongly correlated multiferroic FeV2O4.
motivation: Orbital states are central to coupled structural and magnetic transitions in strongly correlated materials, but direct experimental access remains difficult, especially when correlations, electron-lattice coupling, and spin-orbit interactions compete.
method: The authors use synchrotron X-ray diffraction and related crystallographic/real-space techniques, supported by theoretical analysis, to identify orbital ordering patterns across the phase transitions.
result: They resolve the orbital states that drive successive phase transitions in FeV2O4, clarifying how orbital order couples to lattice and magnetic degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The work provides direct real-space evidence for orbital-state-driven transitions in a strongly correlated oxide, but it is a condensed-matter crystallography study without a quantum-information or information-thermodynamics focus.

title: Dihadron Transverse-Spin Asymmetries In Muon-Deuteron Deep-Inelastic Scattering
authors: G. D. Alexeev et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): G. D. Alexeev et al. (COMPASS Collaboration)

In 2022, the COMPASS collaboration performed semi-inclusive measurements of deep-inelastic muon-scattering on a transversely polarized deuteron ([MATH]) target. From these data, transverse-spin-dependent dihadron asymmetries are extracted using pairs of oppositely charged hadrons. These …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 171903] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The COMPASS collaboration extracts transverse-spin-dependent dihadron asymmetries from 2022 semi-inclusive deep-inelastic muon scattering on a transversely polarized deuteron target.
motivation: Transverse-spin asymmetries in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering probe nucleon spin structure and hadronization mechanisms, in particular the still poorly constrained transversity distribution and dihadron interference fragmentation functions.
method: Semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering of high-energy muons off a transversely polarized deuterium target, with asymmetries computed from azimuthal correlations of oppositely charged hadron pairs.
result: Transverse-spin-dependent dihadron asymmetries are measured over the accessible kinematic range, providing new constraints on the underlying chiral-odd distributions.
conclusion: The data extend the empirical basis for spin-dependent fragmentation and nucleon structure studies, complementing existing proton-target measurements.

title: Reflection-Assisted Discrete Achromatic Diffraction
authors: Seokwoo Kim, Kyungtae Kim, Youngsun Jeon, Heechang Yun, Minseok Choi, Dohyun Kang, Chanbeom Jeon, Yejin Park, Geumseong Lee, And Junsuk Rho
abstract:
Author(s): Seokwoo Kim, Kyungtae Kim, Youngsun Jeon, Heechang Yun, Minseok Choi, Dohyun Kang, Chanbeom Jeon, Yejin Park, Geumseong Lee, and Junsuk Rho

By merging the wavelength-independent geometry of reflection with the momentum control of a periodic lattice, a deep binary grating efficiently routes multiple distinct wavelengths into a single diffraction angle.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 176903] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A deep binary reflection grating achromatically routes several distinct wavelengths to the same diffraction angle by combining wavelength-independent mirror geometry with lattice momentum control.
motivation: Diffractive optical elements normally disperse light strongly with wavelength, which is undesirable for applications requiring common-angle beam steering across multiple colors.
method: The authors design a deep binary grating operating in reflection, exploiting the wavelength independence of reflection geometry together with the momentum provided by a periodic lattice, and characterize its angle-resolved diffraction response.
result: The device routes multiple distinct wavelengths into a single diffraction angle, realizing discrete achromatic diffraction in a compact binary structure.
conclusion: Reflection-based binary gratings offer a practical route to achromatic multi-wavelength beam routing for optics and photonics applications.

title: Measurement Of Jet Quenching In O+o Collisions At $\sqrt{{s}_{\text{NN}}}=200\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{GeV}$ By The Star Experiment At Rhic
authors: B. E. Aboona et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. E. Aboona et al. (STAR Collaboration)

The STAR experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider presents measurements of correlations between charged hadron triggers of high transverse momenta ([MATH]) with recoiling charged hadrons ($3<{p}_{}<7\mathrm…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 172301] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: STAR measures high-pT charged-hadron trigger correlations with recoiling hadrons in O+O collisions at 200 GeV to probe jet quenching.
motivation: Jet quenching is a hallmark of quark-gluon plasma formation, and small collision systems like O+O provide a testing ground for whether medium-induced parton energy loss occurs at small system sizes.
method: Two-particle and triggered-hadron correlation analyses of high transverse momentum charged hadrons with recoiling charged hadrons (3 < pT < 7 GeV) using STAR detector data from O+O collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 200 GeV.
result: Correlation yields and away-side modification patterns are extracted to quantify the extent of jet-like signal modification relative to pp reference, indicating modest but non-zero medium effects in O+O.
conclusion: The measurements constrain the onset and system-size dependence of jet quenching, informing models of parton energy loss in small quark-gluon plasma droplets.

title: Rocking, Rolling, And Jumping: Rigid And Soft Ellipsoids Move In Many Modes
authors: Shih-Yuan Chen And Michelle M. Driscoll
abstract:
Author(s): Shih-Yuan Chen and Michelle M. Driscoll

Rotating a nonspherical object introduces rich and surprising dynamics to a classical mechanics problem. It has been shown that a rolling ellipse in air can rock, roll, or jump along a flat surface. Even for a rolling sphere, deformability can significantly alter its mobility compared to a rigid cou…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 178201] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: A classical mechanics study of how rigid and soft ellipsoidal objects rock, roll, and jump when rotated on a flat surface, revealing multiple locomotion modes depending on shape and deformability.
motivation: Rotating a nonspherical object on a surface produces rich dynamics that are poorly understood, and deformability is known to strongly modify mobility even for spheres, motivating a systematic comparison of rigid versus soft ellipsoids.
method: Experimental and/or theoretical characterization of the dynamics of rigid and soft ellipsoids rolling along a flat surface, classifying the observed rocking, rolling, and jumping modes as a function of shape and elasticity.
result: The authors identify multiple distinct motion modes for ellipsoids and show that softness qualitatively alters the mobility and mode selection compared to rigid counterparts.
conclusion: Deformability is a key control parameter for the locomotion of nonspherical objects, with implications for soft robotics and granular/active matter transport.

title: Most Degenerate Chiral Doublet Bands In Nuclei
authors: W. Z. Xu (许文政) et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): W. Z. Xu (许文政) et al.

A doublet-band structure consisting of two [MATH] bands connected by multiple interband transitions was identified in [MATH], with an average energy difference of only 36 keV between the two bands. It represents the most degenerate doublet-band structure observed so far in nucl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 162503] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors report the most degenerate chiral doublet-band structure observed to date in a nucleus, with two bands separated by an average of only 36 keV and linked by multiple interband transitions.
motivation: Chiral doublet bands are a signature of spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking in triaxial rotating nuclei, and the degree of degeneracy between the partner bands tests how robustly that symmetry is realized.
method: Gamma-ray spectroscopy of the nucleus in question was used to establish the level scheme, identifying two bands connected by multiple interband transitions and extracting their energy staggering.
result: The two partner bands exhibit an average energy difference of only 36 keV, the smallest — i.e. most degenerate — doublet-band spacing reported so far in nuclei.
conclusion: The finding sets a new benchmark for chiral-doublet degeneracy in nuclear structure and provides a stringent test case for models of chirality in triaxial nuclei.

title: Local Relaxation And Scale-Dependent Alignment In Compressible, Magnetized Turbulence
authors: James R. Beattie And Amitava Bhattacharjee
abstract:
Author(s): James R. Beattie and Amitava Bhattacharjee

Patchy alignment pervades magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence, yet its role in the turbulent cascade remains unclear. Using net- and no-net-flux compressible simulations with up to [MATH] grid cells, we uncover two distinct alignment laws. Our constant-flux model of departures from locally …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 165202] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies local relaxation and scale-dependent alignment in compressible, magnetized MHD turbulence using large simulations.
motivation: Patchy alignment is common in MHD turbulence, but its role in the turbulent cascade remains unclear.
method: The authors perform net-flux and no-net-flux compressible MHD simulations with up to very large grid sizes and develop a constant-flux model for departures from local relaxation.
result: They identify two distinct alignment laws and characterize scale-dependent alignment behavior across the simulations.
conclusion: The findings clarify how local relaxation and alignment affect the turbulent cascade in compressible magnetized turbulence.

title: Emulating Atomic Data Of Cd-like Ions Using Gaussian Process Regression
authors: Dipti
abstract:
Author(s): Dipti

In this work, Gaussian process regression (GPR) models are employed to emulate ab initio atomic data for multielectron systems, generated using the multiconfiguration Dirac-Hartree-Fock method. The [MATH] systems serve as a test case, where strongly correlated [MATH] orbitals can lead to significan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042816] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Gaussian process regression is used to emulate ab initio atomic data for Cd-like ions generated by multiconfiguration Dirac-Hartree-Fock calculations.
motivation: Atomic structure calculations for multielectron systems are computationally expensive, motivating surrogate models that can reproduce ab initio data efficiently.
method: The paper trains Gaussian process regression models on multiconfiguration Dirac-Hartree-Fock data for Cd-like ion systems as a test case.
result: The GPR models emulate the atomic data while handling strongly correlated orbitals that can cause significant computational challenges.
conclusion: GPR is shown to be a practical emulation tool for atomic data, but the work is outside the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Core Relaxation And Interchannel Coupling Effects On The Ar $3s$ Photoionization Time Delay In The Vicinity Of The $2p$ Thresholds
authors: Suraj Rai, Aarthi Ganesan, Pranawa C. Deshmukh, And Steven T. Manson
abstract:
Author(s): Suraj Rai, Aarthi Ganesan, Pranawa C. Deshmukh, and Steven T. Manson

The angle-resolved Wigner time delay for Ar [MATH] photoionization has been investigated in the vicinity of the inner-shell [MATH] thresholds (approximately 250 eV) using the relativistic random-phase approximation with and without core relaxation (RRPA-R and RRPA, respectively). The calculations includ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043113] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper calculates angle-resolved Wigner time delays for Ar 3s photoionization near the 2p thresholds using relativistic random-phase approximation with and without core relaxation.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how core relaxation and interchannel coupling affect photoionization time delays near inner-shell thresholds in argon.
method: Relativistic random-phase approximation calculations are performed with and without core relaxation (RRPA-R and RRPA) to obtain angle-resolved Wigner time delays for Ar 3s photoionization around 250 eV.
result: The study reveals the roles of core relaxation and interchannel coupling in shaping the angle-resolved time delay behavior near the 2p thresholds.
conclusion: Core relaxation and interchannel coupling are important for accurately describing photoionization time delays in the vicinity of inner-shell thresholds.

title: Microscopic Nature Of Orbital Disorder In ${\mathrm{LaMnO}}_{3}$
authors: Bodoo Batnaran, Andrew L. Goodwin, Michael A. Hayward, And Volker L. Deringer
abstract:
Author(s): Bodoo Batnaran, Andrew L. Goodwin, Michael A. Hayward, and Volker L. Deringer

We present a revised atomistic picture of the order-disorder transition in the archetypal orbital-ordered perovskite material, [MATH]. Our study uses machine-learning-driven molecular-dynamics simulations which describe the temperature evolution of pair distribution functions in clos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225138] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the microscopic nature of the orbital order-disorder transition in LaMnO3 using machine-learning-driven molecular dynamics and pair distribution function analysis.
motivation: The orbital ordering and disorder transition in the archetypal perovskite LaMnO3 is not fully understood at the atomistic level, motivating a revised microscopic picture.
method: Machine-learning-driven molecular-dynamics simulations are used to model the temperature evolution of pair distribution functions and resolve orbital disorder in LaMnO3.
result: The simulations provide an updated atomistic description of the order-disorder transition, clarifying how orbital disorder manifests in the pair distribution functions.
conclusion: The work refines the structural understanding of orbital ordering in LaMnO3, but it lies outside quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: B-site Disorder Induced Cluster Glass And Magnetoresistance Behaviors In ${\mathrm{LaSrMnRuO}}_{6}$ Double Perovskite
authors: Arun Kumar, S. Leelashree, And P. N. Santhosh
abstract:
Author(s): Arun Kumar, S. Leelashree, and P. N. Santhosh

In this work, magnetic and transport properties of [MATH] are studied in detail. The absence of a superlattice peak at [MATH] in the x-ray diffraction pattern indicates the Mn/Ru disorder at B-site, known as B-site disorder. The ZFC curve exhibits a weak ferromagnetic transi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194419] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the magnetic and transport properties of the double perovskite LaSrMnRuO6, focusing on B-site Mn/Ru disorder, cluster-glass behavior, and magnetoresistance.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how B-site cationic disorder in a double perovskite affects its magnetic ordering, glassy dynamics, and magnetotransport properties.
method: They perform detailed magnetic and transport measurements, including x-ray diffraction, zero-field-cooled/field-cooled magnetization, and magnetoresistance measurements on LaSrMnRuO6 samples.
result: The absence of a superlattice peak indicates Mn/Ru B-site disorder, and the ZFC curve shows a weak ferromagnetic transition consistent with cluster-glass behavior; magnetoresistance is also observed.
conclusion: B-site disorder in LaSrMnRuO6 induces cluster-glass magnetism and affects magnetoresistance, highlighting the role of cationic disorder in double-perovskite properties.

title: Finite-momentum Superconductivity With Singlet-triplet Mixing In An Altermagnetic Metal: A Pairing Instability Analysis
authors: Hui Hu, Zhao Liu, Jia Wang, Xia-Ji Liu, And Yoji Ohashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Hu, Zhao Liu, Jia Wang, Xia-Ji Liu, and Yoji Ohashi

We analyze the pairing instability of an altermagnetic metal on a square lattice driven by an attractive nearest-neighbor interaction. This interaction enables multiple pairing channels, including even-parity extended [MATH]-wave and [MATH]-wave states, as well as two odd-parity [MATH]-wave channels. We veri…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214509] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes pairing instabilities in an altermagnetic metal with attractive nearest-neighbor interactions, identifying finite-momentum superconducting states with mixed singlet-triplet character.
motivation: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, motivating the study of unconventional superconducting pairing channels that may arise from such electronic structure.
method: The authors perform a pairing-instability analysis on a square-lattice altermagnetic metal, considering even-parity extended s-wave and d-wave channels as well as two odd-parity p-wave channels.
result: They find that multiple pairing channels are competitive and that finite-momentum superconductivity with singlet-triplet mixing can emerge from the pairing instability.
conclusion: The work highlights how altermagnetic spin splitting can stabilize unconventional finite-momentum superconducting phases, with implications for superconductivity in magnetic metals.

title: Emergence And Coexistence Of Periodic And Unstructured Motion In Future-avoiding Random Walks
authors: A. Schmaus, K. Stiller, And N. Molkenthin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Schmaus, K. Stiller, and N. Molkenthin

Self-avoiding random walks on graphs can be seen as walkers interacting with their own past history. Here, we consider a complementary class of dynamics, mutual future-avoiding random walks (MFARWs), where stochastically driven walkers are avoiding each other's planned future trajectories. Such syst…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044219] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes mutual future-avoiding random walks on graphs, a dynamics in which stochastically driven walkers avoid each other's planned future trajectories, and characterizes how periodic and unstructured motion emerge and coexist.
motivation: Self-avoiding random walks model walkers interacting with their own past history; the authors propose the complementary notion of walkers interacting with each other's anticipated futures, a scenario relevant to pedestrian and traffic-like dynamics.
method: Classical stochastic random-walk models on graphs are defined and studied, apparently through a combination of analytical modeling and numerical simulation of the resulting collective dynamics.
result: The dynamics are shown to give rise to both periodic (structured) motion and unstructured motion, which can emerge and coexist within the same system depending on parameters.
conclusion: Future-avoiding interactions constitute a distinct universality class of walker dynamics with rich collective behavior, complementary to self-avoiding walks.

title: Noise-controlled Phase Transitions And Memory-state Switching In Connectome-informed Modular Spiking Networks
authors: Siyu Huo
abstract:
Author(s): Siyu Huo

The resting brain must preserve stable representations while flexibly switching among activity patterns. Here we show that noise can tune this balance in a connectome-informed modular spiking network storing multiple spatiotemporal memories through spike-timing-dependent plasticity. With global inhi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044323] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A connectome-informed modular spiking neural network with STDP shows that noise can tune phase transitions and switching among multiple stored spatiotemporal memories.
motivation: The resting brain must keep stable representations while remaining able to flexibly switch between activity patterns, so the authors ask how noise can control this stability-flexibility balance.
method: They build a modular spiking network informed by connectome structure that stores multiple spatiotemporal memories via spike-timing-dependent plasticity, with global inhibition, and analyze noise-driven phase transitions and memory-state switching.
result: Noise is shown to tune transitions between memory states and to control switching among stored spatiotemporal activity patterns.
conclusion: Noise acts as a control parameter for phase transitions and memory switching in connectome-structured spiking networks, offering a mechanism for balancing stability and flexibility in brain dynamics.

title: Space-time Correlations Of Passive Scalars In Colored-noise Flows
authors: Long Wang And Guowei He
abstract:
Author(s): Long Wang and Guowei He

The space-time correlation of a passive scalar advected by a Gaussian colored-noise velocity with wavenumber-dependent correlation times and power-law spatial spectra is investigated in the present paper. Within the inertial-convective subrange, we derive an analytical solution for the space-time co…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045106] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives analytical results for space-time correlations of a passive scalar advected by Gaussian colored-noise velocity fields with power-law spectra.
motivation: Turbulent transport of passive scalars is a classical fluid-dynamics problem, and colored-noise velocity models with wavenumber-dependent correlation times are used to capture finite-time-scale effects absent in white-noise (Kraichnan) models.
method: Analytical derivation of the space-time correlation function within the inertial-convective subrange for Gaussian velocity ensembles with tunable spectral exponents and correlation-time scaling, likely using a Lagrangian or path-integral approach.
result: Closed-form expressions for the scalar space-time correlation are obtained, showing how scaling exponents and correlation-time parameters determine the temporal decay and sweeping behavior.
conclusion: The results characterize how colored noise modifies scalar correlation scaling, providing a classical turbulence benchmark rather than any quantum-information or thermodynamic insight.

title: Enhanced Turbulent Clustering Of Time-varying Particles In Random Flow Fields
authors: Boaz Ofarim And Yuval Dagan
abstract:
Author(s): Boaz Ofarim and Yuval Dagan

Particles suspended in turbulent flows tend to cluster within specific regions of the flow field. Previous research consistently reported that clustering is reduced at both very small and very large Stokes numbers for moderate Reynolds numbers. However, understanding how clustering evolves with vary…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045104] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: This study numerically/analytically examines how clustering of inertial particles in turbulent random flow fields is enhanced when particle properties (e.g., Stokes number or response time) vary in time.
motivation: Prior work shows clustering of particles peaks at moderate Stokes numbers and is suppressed at very small and very large values, but how clustering behaves when particle parameters vary dynamically in time remained unexplored.
method: Particles with time-varying response characteristics are advected in synthetic random turbulent flow fields, and their spatial clustering is quantified statistically as a function of the modulation parameters.
result: Time-varying particles exhibit stronger clustering than their constant-parameter counterparts, with the enhancement depending on the rate and amplitude of variation relative to the flow timescales.
conclusion: Modulating particle properties in time provides a knob to enhance turbulent clustering, relevant to aerosol, droplet, and dust dynamics in turbulent environments.

title: Dynamic Magnetic Response Of Magnetic Multicore Particles: Competing Anisotropies
authors: Vladimir Zverev, Ekaterina Novak, Andrey A. Kuznetsov, And Sofia Kantorovich

Magnetic multicore nanoparticles offer a versatile route to tuning magnetic response via particle geometry and internal structure. In this work, we investigate the dynamic magnetic behavior of ellipsoidal multicore particles, focusing on the interplay between elongation, intercore dipolar interactio…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045405] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: This work studies the dynamic magnetic response of ellipsoidal magnetic multicore nanoparticles, focusing on how elongation, intercore dipolar interactions, and competing anisotropies shape their magnetization dynamics.
motivation: Magnetic multicore nanoparticles can have tunable magnetic properties due to internal structure and geometry, but the interplay between shape anisotropy, core anisotropy, and dipolar interactions is not fully understood.
method: The authors likely use theoretical or computational modeling of ellipsoidal multicore particles with internal magnetic cores, incorporating dipolar interactions and anisotropy terms to compute dynamic magnetic response.
result: The study identifies regimes where elongation and intercore dipolar interactions compete with intrinsic anisotropies, leading to distinct dynamic magnetic behavior.
conclusion: Geometry and internal dipolar coupling provide knobs for tuning the dynamic magnetic response of multicore nanoparticles, with implications for their use in magnetic applications.

title: Two-dimensional Anomalous Diffusion Of Coupled Active-passive Particles In Viscoelastic Media

Several biological systems are not independent; rather, they are coupled to another system, which shows distinct viscoelastic responses and het…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044126] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies two-dimensional anomalous diffusion of coupled active-passive particles in viscoelastic media.
motivation: It aims to understand transport in complex biological and nonequilibrium environments where coupled systems exhibit heterogeneous viscoelastic responses.
method: The authors likely model coupled active and passive particles in a viscoelastic medium and analyze their diffusive dynamics, possibly via mean-squared displacement and anomalous exponents.
result: The study characterizes how coupling between active and passive particles modifies anomalous diffusion in two dimensions under viscoelastic conditions.
conclusion: Coupled active-passive dynamics in viscoelastic media can produce distinct anomalous transport behavior relevant to complex soft and biological systems.

title: Spontaneous Nuclear Fusion
authors: Matej Lipoglavšek And Aleksandra Cvetinović
abstract:
Author(s): Matej Lipoglavšek and Aleksandra Cvetinović

We present the first experimental investigation of deuteron fusion at thermal energy performed underground. Using deuterated palladium targets, we measured spontaneous proton emission attributed to nuclear fusion reactions between deuterons. Protons with energies around 3 MeV, consistent with the ex…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043070] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: An underground experiment reports spontaneous ~3 MeV proton emission from deuterated palladium targets, interpreted as low-energy deuteron-deuteron fusion.
motivation: Claims of anomalous nuclear fusion at thermal energies remain controversial, motivating a careful underground measurement with reduced cosmic-ray background.
method: Deuterated palladium targets are measured in an underground laboratory, with proton emission spectra around 3 MeV analyzed for consistency with fusion reaction kinematics and backgrounds.
result: Spontaneous proton emission near 3 MeV is observed and attributed to deuteron fusion reactions at thermal energies.
conclusion: The authors argue that low-energy deuteron fusion occurs spontaneously in deuterated palladium, though the claim requires independent replication and background scrutiny.

title: Evolution Of Mutating Pathogens In Networked Populations
authors: Aviel Ivry, Reuven Cohen, And Amikam Patron
abstract:
Author(s): Aviel Ivry, Reuven Cohen, and Amikam Patron

Epidemic spreading over population networks has been an important subject of research for several decades, especially during the Covid-19 pandemic. Most epidemic outbreaks are likely to create multiple mutations during their spreading over the population. In this paper, we study the evolution of a p…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043061] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper models how mutating pathogens evolve as they spread through networked host populations, extending epidemic-spreading theory to include mutation dynamics.
motivation: Most epidemic outbreaks accumulate multiple mutations during spread, so understanding how network structure shapes pathogen evolution is important for predicting outbreaks, as highlighted by COVID-19.
method: The authors build on network epidemic-spreading models (e.g., SIR-type dynamics on populations) and add a mutational component, tracking the emergence and competition of pathogen variants across the network, likely via analytical and simulation approaches.
result: They characterize how network topology and spreading dynamics influence the diversity and fixation of mutations during an outbreak.
conclusion: Network structure plays a significant role in mutating-pathogen evolution, with implications for epidemic forecasting and mitigation.

title: Remote Synchronization And Critical-like Breakdown In Star Networks Of Oscillator Populations
authors: Siyu Huo
abstract:
Author(s): Siyu Huo

Remote synchronization, in which indirectly connected nodes synchronize while the mediating hub remains desynchronized, is a counterintuitive form of collective dynamics in complex networks. Most previous studies have treated each node as a single oscillator, whereas nodes in realistic systems often…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043056] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies remote synchronization and critical-like breakdown in star networks where each network node is an oscillator population rather than a single oscillator.
motivation: Remote synchronization is a counterintuitive collective dynamics phenomenon, and realistic systems often contain oscillator populations rather than single oscillators, motivating a population-level network analysis.
method: The paper analyzes star networks of oscillator populations, likely using reduced or mean-field dynamical descriptions to characterize synchronization and desynchronization regimes.
result: It identifies remote synchronization behavior and a critical-like breakdown in star networks of oscillator populations.
conclusion: The work contributes to nonlinear dynamics and complex-network synchronization but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Cosmological And High-Energy Physics Implications From Gravitational-Wave Background Searches In LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA’s O1–O4a Runs
authors: A. G. Abac et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. G. Abac et al. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration, Virgo Collaboration, and KAGRA Collaboration)

Numerous well-motivated particle-physics-based models are constrained using the most recent LIGO-Virgo gravitational-wave data.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041023] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaborations use O1–O4a gravitational-wave background searches to constrain numerous particle-physics and cosmological models.
motivation: Stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds can probe high-energy and early-universe physics beyond the reach of colliders, motivating constraints on well-motivated particle-physics models using current data.
method: Cross-correlation searches for an isotropic stochastic gravitational-wave background across the O1–O4a observing runs are reinterpreted as Bayesian/posterior constraints on model parameters.
result: Upper limits on the background amplitude translate into exclusion bounds on a broad set of cosmological and high-energy physics scenarios.
conclusion: Gravitational-wave background searches provide competitive, model-independent constraints on new physics, with sensitivity expected to improve in future observing runs.

title: Electric-Field-Induced X-Ray Nonreciprocal Dichroism In Hematite

result: The measurements uncover nonreciprocal dichroism signatures consistent with hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles, supported by theory.

result: A dynamic spin nematic liquid-crystal-like state couples to magnetic fields and generates scalar spin chirality, driving anomalous Hall and Nernst effects in the paramagnetic phase.
conclusion: The findings establish a connection between spin nematicity, scalar spin chirality, and anomalous transport in YbMnBi2, with implications for correlated quantum materials.

title: Erratum: Programmable Quantum Anomalous Hall Insulator In Twisted Crystalline Flatbands [Phys. Rev. X 16, 011015 (2026)]
authors: Wenxuan Wang, Yijie Wang, Zaizhe Zhang, Zihao Huo, Gengdong Zhou, Shu Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxia Yang, Qing Dai, X. C. Xie, Kaihui Liu, Zhida Song, And Xiaobo Lu

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 039901] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.

method: The erratum consists solely of a correction notice to the published article; no new methodology, data, or analysis is presented in the abstract.
result: No scientific results are reported beyond the bibliographic correction itself (Phys. Rev. X 16, 039901).
conclusion: The item is a publisher erratum with no substantive content relevant to quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Enduring Mechanical Memory From The Constitutive Response Of Elastically Recoverable Nanostructured Materials
authors: Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, And Ramathasan Thevamaran

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031073] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.

motivation: The authors aim to exploit constitutive memory effects in nanostructured materials for non-electronic computing paradigms.
method: They investigate the mechanical response of elastically recoverable carbon nanotube foams and identify return-point memory behavior.
result: The material exhibits return-point memory, suggesting that mechanical history can be stored and read out through constitutive response.
conclusion: Such nanostructured materials may provide a platform for mechanical computing, but the work is far from quantum information or thermodynamics research.

title: Reversibility, Chaos, And Attractors In Periodically Sheared Elastic Filaments
authors: Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia Du Roure, Anke Lindner, And David Saintillan
