Combining experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations, a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible filaments under periodic shear is unveiled.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031067] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and simulations reveal a transition from reversible motion to intermittent noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible actin filaments under periodic shear.
motivation: The work aims to understand nonlinear dynamics and reversibility-breaking in periodically driven elastic filaments, a soft-matter/fluid-dynamics problem.
method: The authors combine experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations of semiflexible filaments under periodic shear.
result: They identify a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaotic dynamics in single filaments.
conclusion: The findings characterize chaos and attractors in periodically sheared elastic filaments but do not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quasilinear Theory Of Fast Flavor Instabilities
authors: Damiano F. G. Fiorillo And Georg G. Raffelt
abstract:
Author(s): Damiano F. G. Fiorillo and Georg G. Raffelt

Dense neutrino plasmas can develop instabilities that drive collisionless flavor exchange, equivalent to the emission of flavomons, the quanta of flavor waves. We treat these waves as independent linear degrees of freedom and develop a quasilinear theory, including backreaction on the neutrino distr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 171001] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a quasilinear theory for fast flavor instabilities in dense neutrino plasmas, treating flavor waves as linear degrees of freedom with backreaction on the neutrino distribution.
motivation: Dense neutrino environments can exhibit collective flavor instabilities that drive collisionless flavor exchange, but a systematic quasilinear treatment including backreaction is needed.
method: The authors model flavor waves as independent linear modes, equivalent to flavomon excitations, and derive quasilinear equations describing their evolution and feedback on the neutrino distribution.
result: The theory provides a framework for the nonlinear saturation and backreaction of fast flavor instabilities in neutrino plasmas.
conclusion: This work advances the understanding of collective neutrino flavor dynamics, but it is not connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Microfluidic Oscillatory Rheology Of Transported Soft Particles
authors: Matteo Milani, Joshua D. Mcgraw, Anke Lindner, And Stefano Aime
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Milani, Joshua D. McGraw, Anke Lindner, and Stefano Aime

Shape-optimized microfluidic channels enable high-throughput characterization of microscopic soft matter, providing precise spatiotemporal stress fields to bridge bulk mechanical measurements and single-particle dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 041005] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a microfluidic oscillatory rheology method for high-throughput mechanical characterization of transported soft particles using shape-optimized channels.
motivation: The work aims to bridge bulk rheological measurements and single-particle dynamics by providing precise spatiotemporal stress fields in microfluidic channels.
method: Shape-optimized microfluidic channels are used to apply oscillatory stress to flowing soft particles, enabling high-throughput measurements of their mechanical response.
result: The approach yields precise stress fields and enables characterization of microscopic soft matter dynamics under flow.
conclusion: This microfluidic platform offers a route to connect bulk mechanical properties with single-particle behavior in soft matter systems.

title: Ionization-induced Chirping And Compression Of A High-power Microwave Pulse. Ii. Theoretical Analysis And Numerical Simulations
authors: Adi Haim, Vlad Maksimov, John G. Leopold, Yuriy P. Bliokh, And Yakov E. Krasik

This article complements a recent experimental study [A. Haim et al.,
tldr: The paper theoretically and numerically analyzes how ionization of a gas in a circular waveguide chirps and compresses high-power subnanosecond microwave pulses.
motivation: Recent experiments observed that high-power microwave pulses traversing a gas-filled waveguide exit as chirped pulses due to gas ionization; this work aims to explain the underlying mechanism.
method: The authors develop a theoretical analysis and perform numerical simulations of microwave pulse propagation in a gas-filled circular waveguide, modeling ionization-induced plasma effects on the pulse phase and amplitude.
result: The analysis reproduces the experimentally observed chirping and compression, showing that ionization dynamics in the gas modulate the microwave pulse.
conclusion: Ionization in gas-filled waveguides provides a mechanism for chirping and compressing high-power microwave pulses, consistent with experimental findings.

title: Asymmetric Cyclic Interactions Lead To Stable Mean-field Equilibria While Demographic Noise Induces Sustained Oscillations
authors: A. L. L. Middleton, J. H. P. Dawes, A. A. Jarai, And K. M. Briggs
abstract:
Author(s): A. L. L. Middleton, J. H. P. Dawes, A. A. Jarai, and K. M. Briggs

The dynamics of symmetric cyclically competing subpopulations is well known to lead to oscillatory dynamics. However, in some situations the competition is fundamentally asymmetric in that it is better modeled by binary interactions all of which involve the same subpopulation. Here we analyze a conc…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044211] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes a stochastic model of asymmetric cyclic competition in which all binary interactions involve the same subpopulation, showing that mean-field equilibria are stable while demographic noise generates sustained oscillations.
motivation: Symmetric cyclic competition is known to produce oscillatory dynamics, but many real competitive systems are fundamentally asymmetric; the authors ask how such asymmetry, combined with intrinsic demographic stochasticity, alters the resulting dynamics.
method: They construct and analyze a mean-field model of asymmetric cyclic interactions as a deterministic dynamical system, then extend it to a stochastic individual-based formulation incorporating demographic noise.
result: The deterministic mean-field dynamics possess stable equilibria, whereas the stochastic version with demographic noise exhibits sustained oscillations that are absent in the mean-field limit.
conclusion: Noise can qualitatively change the collective behavior of asymmetric competitive populations, stabilizing oscillatory regimes that the deterministic description misses.

title: Universalities In The Avalanche Dynamics Of Novelties And Non-novelties And Some Notes On The Heaps Law
authors: Filippo Santoro, Alberto Petri, And Francesca Tria
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Santoro, Alberto Petri, and Francesca Tria

Unprecedented events intertwine with the repetition of the past in natural phenomena and human activities. Key statistical patterns, such as Heaps’ and Taylor’s laws and Zipf’s law, have been identified as characterizing the dynamical processes that govern the emergence of novelties and the abundanc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043083] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies universal statistical patterns in the avalanche-like dynamics of novel versus repeated events, connecting Heaps', Taylor's and Zipf's laws within a branching/avalanche framework.
motivation: Empirical regularities such as Heaps' and Zipf's laws characterize how novelty emerges and recurs in natural and social systems, but a unified dynamical explanation of these patterns and their interrelations is still lacking.
method: The authors analyze stochastic models of novelty introduction and avalanche (branching) dynamics, deriving scaling relations and comparing the resulting predictions with empirical statistics.
result: Universal scaling behavior is found for novelty avalanches, yielding relations that link Heaps' exponent to other observables, with notes on the range of validity of Heaps' law.
conclusion: The work provides a statistical-physics account of innovation dynamics, but it concerns classical complex systems and has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Production And Decay Dynamics Of The Charmed Baryon ${\mathrm{Λ}}_{c}^{+}$ In ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Annihilations Near Threshold
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Researchers observe the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations using the BESIII detector.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031058] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The BESIII Collaboration observes transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations near threshold and studies its production and decay dynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to characterize charmed-baryon production and decay mechanisms near threshold using a clean e+e− annihilation environment.
method: Using BESIII detector data, the authors analyze Λc+ production in e+e− annihilations and extract polarization and decay parameters from angular distributions.
result: The collaboration reports observation of transverse Λc+ polarization and provides measurements of production and decay dynamics near threshold.
conclusion: The results give insight into charmed-baryon strong-interaction dynamics and provide inputs for future studies of baryon production and decay.

title: Dark Matter, Baryon Number, And Cosmic-Ray Antinuclei
authors: Caleb Gemmell, Dan Hooper, Seth Koren, And Fabrizio Vassallo
abstract:
Author(s): Caleb Gemmell, Dan Hooper, Seth Koren, and Fabrizio Vassallo

Antideuterons and antihelium nuclei in the cosmic-ray spectrum have long been considered a smoking gun signature of dark matter annihilation, making the tentative observation of several such events by AMS highly intriguing. Conventional dark matter models, however, can produce only up to $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 171802] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: A particle-astrophysics study arguing that dark matter models producing cosmic-ray antideuterons and antihelium are constrained by baryon-number considerations, offering a possible explanation of the tentative AMS events.
motivation: Antideuterons and antihelium nuclei in cosmic rays are considered smoking-gun signatures of dark matter annihilation, and the tentative AMS detection of such events motivates a re-examination of how conventional dark matter models can produce them.
method: The authors analyze dark matter annihilation/decay scenarios with respect to baryon-number conservation and hadronization, computing expected antinuclei fluxes and comparing them with cosmic-ray injection requirements.
result: Conventional dark matter models can produce only limited antinuclei yields; incorporating baryon-number-violating or baryon-number-carrying dark sectors can enhance antihelium and antideuteron production to levels potentially consistent with AMS hints.
conclusion: Cosmic-ray antinuclei observations place novel constraints on dark matter models and, if confirmed, would point toward dark sectors with nontrivial baryon-number dynamics.

title: First Simultaneous Analysis Of Transverse Momentum Dependent And Collinear Parton Distributions In The Proton
authors: P. C. Barry, A. Prokudin, T. Anderson, C. Cocuzza, L. Gamberg, W. Melnitchouk, E. Moffat, D. Pitonyak, J.-W. Qiu, N. Sato, A. Vladimirov, And R. M. Whitehill
abstract:
Author(s): P. C. Barry, A. Prokudin, T. Anderson, C. Cocuzza, L. Gamberg, W. Melnitchouk, E. Moffat, D. Pitonyak, J.-W. Qiu, N. Sato, A. Vladimirov, and R. M. Whitehill (JAM Collaboration (TMD Analysis Group)

We present the first simultaneous global QCD analysis of unpolarized transverse momentum dependent (TMD) and collinear parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the proton. Our Letter incorporates data from deep-inelastic scattering, Drell-Yan, inclusive weak boson, [MATH] charm, and jet production invo…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 171902] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The JAM collaboration performs the first simultaneous global QCD fit of unpolarized transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) and collinear parton distribution functions in the proton.
motivation: TMD and collinear PDFs are usually extracted in separate analyses, so a unified determination is needed to consistently describe both low- and high-transverse-momentum data within a single QCD framework.
method: A global QCD analysis is carried out, fitting simultaneously TMD and collinear PDFs to deep-inelastic scattering, Drell-Yan, inclusive weak boson, charm, and jet production data.
result: The fit yields a consistent set of TMD and collinear distributions that describes the combined dataset, showing how the two descriptions connect within one extraction.
conclusion: The work establishes a template for joint TMD-plus-collinear global analyses, improving consistency in proton structure determinations.

title: Laboratory Demonstration Of Coronal Heating Via Magnetic Reconnection During Nanoflares
authors: Wei Sun, Yongli Ping, Chong Lv, Xianxu Jin, Longxing Li, Wenqiang Yuan, Li Feng, Can Ren, Zhu Lei, Baoxian Tian, Xiaofeng Xi, Jialun Chai, Mengqi Jin, Gaoyang Liu, Zhengdong Liu, Yapeng Zhang, Hongzheng Yu, Jun Xiong, Zhiyong Xie, Chen Wang, Wei Wang, Bin Qiao, Zhao Wang, Jiayong Zhong, And Bing Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Sun, Yongli Ping, Chong Lv, Xianxu Jin, Longxing Li, Wenqiang Yuan, Li Feng, Can Ren, Zhu Lei, Baoxian Tian, Xiaofeng Xi, Jialun Chai, Mengqi Jin, Gaoyang Liu, Zhengdong Liu, Yapeng Zhang, Hongzheng Yu, Jun Xiong, Zhiyong Xie, Chen Wang, Wei Wang, Bin Qiao, Zhao Wang, Jiayong Zhong, and Bing Guo

The origin of the solar corona’s million Kelvin temperatures remains a central unsolved problem. While the nanoflare hypothesis is widely accepted and describes magnetic reconnection events at coronal current sheets that are slowly formed by complex driver flows at the solar surface, the possibility…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 175101] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: A laboratory experiment reproduces nanoflare-like magnetic reconnection at coronal current sheets to test whether such events can explain the million-Kelvin solar corona.
motivation: The origin of the solar corona's million Kelvin temperature remains a central unsolved problem, and although the nanoflare hypothesis based on magnetic reconnection is widely accepted, direct laboratory evidence for the heating mechanism has been lacking.
method: The authors design and perform a laboratory plasma experiment that forms current sheets via complex driver flows analogous to photospheric motions, then diagnose the reconnection-driven energy release.
result: The experiment demonstrates magnetic reconnection at current sheets accompanied by plasma heating consistent with the nanoflare picture of coronal heating.
conclusion: Laboratory magnetic reconnection can reproduce key features of nanoflare heating, supporting the nanoflare hypothesis for coronal heating and offering a platform for studying astrophysical reconnection.

title: Erratum: Magnetoelectric Effect In Superconductors With $d$-wave Magnetization [Phys. Rev. B 109, L220505 (2024)]
authors: Alexander A. Zyuzin
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander A. Zyuzin

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 199902] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: This is a publisher erratum correcting the 2024 paper 'Magnetoelectric Effect in Superconductors with d-wave Magnetization' by Alexander A. Zyuzin.
motivation: The original work studied magnetoelectric effects in superconductors hosting d-wave magnetization, a condensed-matter phenomenon; the erratum serves to correct errors in that published article.
method: As an erratum, it provides corrections to the original article rather than introducing new methodology or analysis.
result: The erratum amends specific results or statements in the original Phys. Rev. B 109, L220505 (2024) paper.
conclusion: The correction refines the original condensed-matter findings but offers no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Transformation Pathways Of ${\mathrm{CO}}_{2}\text{−}\mathrm{IV}$: Deviatoric Stress And Thermal Activation
authors: Yingzhan Wei, Guanlin Li, Yanlei Geng, Mengqiong Pu, Nico Giordano, Jiacheng Zhang, Xiaomei Yuan, Shuo Gao, Qiang Zhou, Liang Li, Defang Duan, Xinyang Li, And Fangfei Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yingzhan Wei, Guanlin Li, Yanlei Geng, Mengqiong Pu, Nico Giordano, Jiacheng Zhang, Xiaomei Yuan, Shuo Gao, Qiang Zhou, Liang Li, Defang Duan, Xinyang Li, and Fangfei Li

The structural evolution and transformation pathways of carbon dioxide phase IV ([MATH]-IV) are investigated over 13.0–76.7 GPa and 296–700 K using synchrotron x-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, and first-principles calculations. [MATH]-IV was obtained from ${\mathrm{CO…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214108] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: Synchrotron XRD, Raman spectroscopy, and first-principles calculations are used to map the structural evolution and transformation pathways of CO2 phase IV between 13.0 and 76.7 GPa and 296–700 K.
motivation: The high-pressure polymorphism of carbon dioxide is poorly constrained, and the stability regime and transformation routes of CO2-IV under deviatoric stress and thermal activation remain unresolved.
method: The authors combine high-pressure synchrotron x-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy in a diamond anvil cell over 13.0–76.7 GPa and 296–700 K with density functional theory calculations to identify candidate structures and transition pathways.
result: The study establishes the pressure–temperature boundaries of CO2-IV, identifies the intermediate and product phases formed under deviatoric stress and heating, and supports the proposed pathways with calculated enthalpies and Raman/XRD signatures.
conclusion: Deviatoric stress and temperature jointly govern the transformation pathways of CO2-IV, clarifying the high-pressure phase diagram of carbon dioxide relevant to planetary interiors and dense molecular solids.

title: Plasma Density Manipulation In Staged Discharge Capillaries For Plasma-based Accelerators
authors: Angelo Biagioni, Lucio Crincoli, Romain Demitra, Mario Galletti, Valerio Lollo, Donato Pellegrini, Riccardo Pompili, Massimo Ferrario, And Arie Zigler
abstract:
Author(s): Angelo Biagioni, Lucio Crincoli, Romain Demitra, Mario Galletti, Valerio Lollo, Donato Pellegrini, Riccardo Pompili, Massimo Ferrario, and Arie Zigler

Plasma wakefield acceleration of charged particle beams relies on specialized devices for plasma generation and confinement. In both particle-driven wakefield acceleration and beam-focusing experiments, these devices are designed to precisely control plasma properties to optimize beam-plasma interac…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045210] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports on engineering of staged discharge capillaries to control plasma density profiles for plasma wakefield acceleration and beam-focusing experiments.
motivation: Plasma wakefield acceleration requires precisely tailored plasma sources with controllable density and confinement to optimize beam-plasma interactions in both particle-driven and beam-focusing regimes.
method: Staged discharge capillary devices are developed and characterized, with measurements of plasma density manipulation and discharge parameters across the stages.
result: The staged capillary design enables controlled, spatially structured plasma density profiles suitable for accelerator and focusing applications.
conclusion: Staged discharge capillaries provide a practical route to density-tailored plasma sources for plasma-based accelerators.

title: Connectivity, Rigidity, And Gelation In Linker-mediated Colloidal Networks
authors: Taejin Kwon, Murari Singh, Javier Alejandro Sanchez-Gallegos, Román Perdomo-Pérez, Ramón Castañeda-Priego, And Thomas M. Truskett
abstract:
Author(s): Taejin Kwon, Murari Singh, Javier Alejandro Sanchez-Gallegos, Román Perdomo-Pérez, Ramón Castañeda-Priego, and Thomas M. Truskett

Using molecular dynamics simulations, the authors explore gelation in colloids tied together by reversible linkers. They find that different connectivity measures govern ordinary percolation, rigidity percolation, and rheological gelation.

#AdvancingField #WellStructured #SoftMatterSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045408] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that distinct connectivity measures govern ordinary percolation, rigidity percolation, and rheological gelation in linker-mediated colloidal networks.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how reversible linkers control gelation and mechanical rigidity in colloidal networks, a soft-matter physics problem.
method: They use molecular dynamics simulations of colloids connected by reversible linkers and analyze connectivity metrics associated with percolation, rigidity, and rheology.
result: Different connectivity measures are found to control ordinary percolation, rigidity percolation, and rheological gelation, indicating that gelation is not captured by a single connectivity criterion.
conclusion: The work clarifies the relationship between network connectivity and mechanical/rheological gelation in linker-mediated colloidal systems.

title: Kinetics And Stability Of Transition Waves In Viscoelastic Bistable Lattices
authors: P. Q. Li, C. Wu, K. F. Wang, And B. L. Wang
abstract:
Author(s): P. Q. Li, C. Wu, K. F. Wang, and B. L. Wang

Transition waves are central to phase-boundary propagation in solid phase transformations and sequential state switching in multistable metamaterials. However, existing studies are often limited to specific structural prototypes or simplified constitutive models, failing to reveal how wave kinetics …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044217] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the kinetics and stability of transition waves propagating through viscoelastic bistable mechanical lattices.
motivation: Transition waves govern phase-boundary propagation in solid phase transformations and sequential switching in multistable metamaterials, but prior work relies on specific prototypes or simplified constitutive models that obscure general kinetic behavior.
method: Theoretical and computational modeling of bistable lattice architectures with viscoelastic constitutive laws to derive wave kinetics and assess stability of propagating transition fronts.
result: The study characterizes how viscoelasticity governs transition wave speed, shape, and stability regimes, revealing conditions for steady versus unstable front propagation.
conclusion: The findings provide general design principles for controlling transition waves in multistable metamaterials and clarify links to phase-boundary dynamics in solids.

title: Quantifying Translational And Bond-orientational Order Metrics In Hyperuniform And Nonhyperuniform Many-particle Systems
authors: Anirban Mukherjee And Salvatore Torquato
abstract:
Author(s): Anirban Mukherjee and Salvatore Torquato

Quantifying the degree of order and disorder in many-particle systems remains an outstanding problem in physics, materials science, and mathematics. To this end, we consider the translational order metric [MATH], defined as the squared [MATH] norm of the total correlation function $h(\mathbf{r…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044133] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes translational and bond-orientational order metrics for quantifying order in hyperuniform and nonhyperuniform classical many-particle systems.
motivation: Quantifying order and disorder in many-particle systems remains a fundamental open problem across physics, materials science, and mathematics.
method: The authors study a translational order metric based on the squared L2 norm of the total correlation function and compare it with bond-orientational order metrics across various hyperuniform and nonhyperuniform systems.
result: The metrics are shown to distinguish different degrees of translational and bond-orientational order, providing a systematic characterization of structural order in these systems.
conclusion: The proposed order metrics offer a useful framework for classifying and comparing order in classical many-particle systems, including hyperuniform materials.

title: Mixed-mode Oscillations In A Three-timescale Model Via Folded-saddle Canards And Delayed Hopf Bifurcations
authors: Xinyi Lin, Jian Song, Na Zhao, And Shenquan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyi Lin, Jian Song, Na Zhao, and Shenquan Liu

Mixed-mode oscillations (MMOs) represent a fundamental type of complex rhythm in systems with multiple timescales. While their mechanisms are well-established in two-timescale settings, arising from either canard dynamics near folded singularities or a delayed Hopf bifurcation (DHB) of the fast subs…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044212] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: A nonlinear-dynamics study explaining how mixed-mode oscillations arise in a three-timescale system through folded-saddle canards combined with delayed Hopf bifurcations.
motivation: MMO mechanisms are well understood for two-timescale systems (canard dynamics near folded singularities or delayed Hopf bifurcation of the fast subsystem), but the three-timescale regime remains less characterized.
method: Analysis of a three-timescale fast-medium-slow dynamical model using geometric singular perturbation theory, folded-saddle canard structures, and delayed Hopf bifurcation analysis, supported by numerical continuation and bifurcation diagrams.
result: The paper shows how the interaction between folded-saddle canards and delayed Hopf bifurcations organizes the MMO patterns in the three-timescale regime, identifying the distinct mechanisms responsible for different small-amplitude oscillation sequences.
conclusion: The work extends classical canard and DHB explanations of MMOs to systems with three separated timescales, providing a geometric template for classifying complex oscillatory rhythms.

title: Learning And Encoding Temporally Structured Sensory Inputs Via Superburst Dynamics
authors: Inhoi Jeong, Kyoung J. Lee, And Jongmu Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Inhoi Jeong, Kyoung J. Lee, and Jongmu Kim

Neuronal population bursts, in which large numbers of neurons fire nearly simultaneously, are increasingly recognized as playing important roles in sensory processing and memory formation. In many sensory systems, information is encoded not only by which neurons are active, but also by the temporal …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044319] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: A computational/theoretical neuroscience study showing how 'superburst' population-burst dynamics in neuronal networks can learn and encode temporally structured sensory inputs.
motivation: Neuronal population bursts are implicated in sensory processing and memory, and many sensory systems encode information in temporal structure rather than only in which neurons fire, motivating a model of how burst dynamics could capture such temporal codes.
method: The authors analyze network models of coupled neurons exhibiting superbursts, characterizing their dynamics and testing how these dynamics respond to and represent temporally structured input patterns.
result: Superburst dynamics are shown to support learning and encoding of temporal features of sensory stimuli, with burst timing and structure carrying stimulus information.
conclusion: Population-burst/superburst dynamics offer a plausible substrate for temporal sensory coding and memory formation in neural circuits.

title: Improved Electron Beam Stability In Laser Wakefield Acceleration Through Control Of Laser Angular Chirp And Wavefront Stability
authors: Zhan Jin, Yan-Jun Gu, Shingo Sato, Nobuhiko Nakanii, Kai Huang, Izuru Daito, Toshiya Muto, Yoshio Mizuta, Szuba Wojciech, Masaki Kando, And Tomonao Hosokai
abstract:
Author(s): Zhan Jin, Yan-Jun Gu, Shingo Sato, Nobuhiko Nakanii, Kai Huang, Izuru Daito, Toshiya Muto, Yoshio Mizuta, Szuba Wojciech, Masaki Kando, and Tomonao Hosokai

Stable operation of laser wakefield acceleration (LWFA) is essential for future applications of compact radiation sources and advanced accelerators. In this work, we investigate stabilization of LWFA electron beams through control of laser angular chirp and wavefront stability. We show that angular …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043090] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: A plasma-accelerator physics study showing that controlling laser angular chirp and wavefront stability improves the shot-to-shot stability of electron beams from laser wakefield acceleration.
motivation: Laser wakefield acceleration can provide compact radiation sources and advanced accelerators, but its practical use is limited by large fluctuations in the produced electron beams.
method: The authors experimentally control and scan the laser angular chirp and wavefront quality in an LWFA stage and correlate these laser parameters with measured electron beam pointing, charge, and energy stability.
result: Reducing angular chirp and stabilizing the wavefront is found to substantially suppress electron beam pointing jitter and energy fluctuations.
conclusion: Laser phase-space and wavefront control is an effective route to stable LWFA operation, relevant to compact accelerator and radiation-source development.

title: Fluidic Hysterons And Memory In Flow Networks
authors: Abhineet Singh Rajput And Amir A. Pahlavan
abstract:
Author(s): Abhineet Singh Rajput and Amir A. Pahlavan

Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can create a fluid system with memory of previous actions through a flow-structure feedback.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041011] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels form fluidic hysterons that give flow networks memory of prior actions via flow-structure feedback.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how memory and hysteresis can emerge in classical fluidic networks through coupled flow and elastic structure dynamics.
method: The study analyzes microfluidic channels containing soft elastic fibers and models the flow-structure feedback that produces hysteretic behavior.
result: The system exhibits fluidic hysteron behavior, enabling memory effects in flow networks based on previous flow states.
conclusion: Elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can implement memory in fluid networks, suggesting a classical mechanical route to hysteretic network dynamics.

title: Contact Forces In Microgel Suspensions
authors: Fran Ivan Vrban, Antonio Šiber, And Primož Ziherl
abstract:
Author(s): Fran Ivan Vrban, Antonio Šiber, and Primož Ziherl

Within a model where micrometer-size soft colloidal particles are viewed as liquid drops, we theoretically study the contact interaction between them. We compute the exact deformation energy across a broad range of indentations and for various model parameters, and we show that it can be reproduced …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 178202] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically models contact interactions between micrometer-sized soft colloidal microgel particles as deformable liquid drops and computes their deformation energy.
motivation: Microgel suspensions exhibit contact forces that are not well captured by simple elastic or hard-sphere models, motivating a liquid-drop description of soft colloidal particles.
method: The authors treat soft colloidal particles as liquid drops and calculate the exact deformation energy over a broad range of indentations and model parameters.
result: They show that the computed deformation energy can be reproduced by a simplified model across the studied parameter range.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical understanding of contact forces in microgel suspensions, which may help interpret their collective behavior.

title: Effective Particle Size As A Control Parameter For Rough Hard-particle Fluids
authors: Nanqing Xiao, Zhen Zhang, Walter Kob, And Yujie Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Nanqing Xiao, Zhen Zhang, Walter Kob, and Yujie Wang

We numerically investigate how particle surface roughness affects the static and dynamic properties of a hard-particle fluid across a wide range of densities, [MATH]. These simulations of a simple model of granular systems reveal that, although the amplitude and coverage of surface corrugation signific…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043041] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: This numerical study examines how particle surface roughness controls the static and dynamic properties of rough hard-particle fluids over a wide density range.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how surface corrugation in granular hard-particle systems affects effective particle size and fluid behavior, a question relevant to classical granular soft matter.
method: They perform numerical simulations of a simple model of rough hard particles and systematically vary surface roughness amplitude and coverage across densities.
result: The simulations reveal that roughness parameters significantly influence the static and dynamic properties of the hard-particle fluid, with effective particle size acting as a control parameter.
conclusion: The work establishes effective particle size as a useful control parameter for understanding rough hard-particle fluids and granular system behavior.

title: Measurement Of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering On Germanium By Coherent
authors: M. Adhikari et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Adhikari et al.

The COHERENT Collaboration reports the most precise measurement of the coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering cross section to date. This measurement was performed with COHERENT’s germanium detector array, Ge-Mini, at the Spallation Neutron Source at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. A cumulative…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 171801] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: The COHERENT Collaboration reports the most precise measurement to date of the coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering cross section using a germanium detector array at the Spallation Neutron Source.
motivation: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering is a fundamental Standard Model process that is difficult to detect because of the tiny nuclear recoil energies involved, motivating improved low-threshold detector measurements.
method: A Ge-Mini germanium detector array was deployed at the Oak Ridge Spallation Neutron Source and used to measure nuclear recoils from neutrinos produced by stopped-pion decay, with a cumulative analysis of collected data.
result: The collaboration obtains the most precise determination of the CEvNS cross section on germanium to date, consistent with Standard Model predictions.
conclusion: The measurement tightens constraints on neutrino-nucleus interactions and demonstrates the maturity of germanium-based CEvNS detection for future precision tests and searches for new physics.

title: Tipping Points Of The Ocean Oxygen: A Dynamical Systems Perspective
authors: Amer Alsulami And Sergei Petrovskii
abstract:
Author(s): Amer Alsulami and Sergei Petrovskii

Ocean oxygen as a potential Earth tipping element has been largely overlooked in the literature. This Perspective argues that a dynamical systems approach complemented with a mathematical model accounting for the oxygen production by phytoplankton photosynthesis can provide a valuable insight into this issue.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 041006] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: This perspective argues that a dynamical systems approach combined with a mathematical model of phytoplankton oxygen production can illuminate whether ocean oxygen acts as an Earth tipping element.
motivation: Ocean oxygen loss is a potentially critical Earth-system tipping element that has received little attention compared to other climate tipping points.
method: Conceptual and modeling perspective using dynamical systems theory supplemented by a mathematical model accounting for oxygen production via phytoplankton photosynthesis.
result: The authors propose that a dynamical-systems formulation can reveal the mechanisms and conditions under which ocean oxygen dynamics exhibit tipping behavior.
conclusion: A dynamical systems framework with photosynthesis-driven oxygen modeling is advocated as a valuable route to understanding and anticipating ocean oxygen tipping points.

title: Periodic Modulation Of The Space-filling Nature Of The Turbulent Flame Leads To Periodic Spiky Heat Release Oscillations
authors: Sivakumar Sudarsanan, Manikandan Raghunathan, Shwetha Viswesh, And R. I. Sujith
abstract:
Author(s): Sivakumar Sudarsanan, Manikandan Raghunathan, Shwetha Viswesh, and R. I. Sujith

Spiky oscillations are characterized by slow-fast dynamics and are observed in excitable media such as neuronal membranes and cardiac cells. In a turbulent reactive flow system, we observe that the heat release rate exhibits self-sustained periodic, spiky oscillations in synchrony with the sinusoida…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045105] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports self-sustained periodic spiky heat-release oscillations in a turbulent reactive flow system, linked to periodic modulation of the flame's space-filling nature.
motivation: Spiky, slow-fast oscillations are well known in excitable media such as neuronal membranes and cardiac cells, and the authors ask whether analogous dynamics can arise in turbulent combustion systems.
method: Experimental analysis of a turbulent reactive flow system, characterizing the heat release rate dynamics and correlating the spiky oscillations with sinusoidal modulation of the flame's space-filling geometry.
result: The heat release rate exhibits self-sustained periodic spiky oscillations synchronized with the imposed sinusoidal modulation, indicating slow-fast excitable dynamics in the turbulent flame.
conclusion: The findings connect excitable-media phenomenology to turbulent combustion and may inform understanding of thermoacoustic instability and combustion-driven oscillations.

title: Cluster-based Feedback Control Of A Noisy Limit-cycle Oscillator
authors: Hiromi Kimishima, Bo Yin, Vikrant Gupta, And Larry K. B. Li
abstract:
Author(s): Hiromi Kimishima, Bo Yin, Vikrant Gupta, and Larry K. B. Li

We numerically explore data-driven cluster-based control of a noisy Van der Pol oscillator, with the aim of elucidating the underlying feedback suppression mechanisms. The controller behavior is examined under three distinct conditions: a deterministic oscillator, an oscillator perturbed by additive…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044216] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: A numerical study of data-driven, cluster-based feedback control applied to a noisy Van der Pol limit-cycle oscillator to uncover the mechanisms behind oscillation suppression.
motivation: Limit-cycle oscillations subject to noise are ubiquitous in nonlinear dynamical systems, and understanding how feedback controllers suppress them is important for practical control design.
method: The authors build cluster-based, data-driven reduced models of a Van der Pol oscillator and compare controller behavior across three conditions: deterministic, additively noise-perturbed, and presumably other noisy regimes.
result: The analysis identifies the feedback mechanisms through which cluster-based control suppresses or modulates the limit-cycle oscillations, and shows how noise alters controller effectiveness.
conclusion: Cluster-based feedback control is shown to be a viable, interpretable strategy for taming noisy limit-cycle oscillations, with mechanistic insight into its operation.

tldr: Experiments and discrete-element modeling reveal the shape adopted by a falling flexible ball chain when its center is arrested by a cylindrical obstacle.
motivation: The authors are motivated by practical problems in high-voltage line installation, where a falling chain catches on hardware and deforms.
method: Combines laboratory experiments with discrete element (numerical) modeling of an inextensible, flexible chain in free fall arrested at its midpoint by a cylinder.
result: The study characterizes the resulting chain geometry and compares measured shapes with discrete-element simulations, identifying the dominant mechanical effects governing the configuration.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanical understanding of arrested falling chains relevant to engineering practice, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

tldr: Controlled laboratory experiments with 48 participants reveal how corridor angle and flow ratio shape bidirectional pedestrian movement and lane formation.
motivation: Understanding bidirectional pedestrian flow in angled corridors is needed for pedestrian facility design and crowd management, yet quantitative data on the combined effects of geometry and directional flow ratio are scarce.
method: Human crowd experiments were conducted in a laboratory with 48 participants across six corridor angles and four flow ratios, with trajectories analyzed to extract flow, density, and lane-formation statistics.
result: The study quantifies how corridor angle and flow ratio modulate walking speed, lane structure, and congestion, identifying geometric regimes where counterflow becomes inefficient.
conclusion: Design guidelines for angled corridors can be derived from the observed relationship between geometry, flow ratio, and bidirectional traffic efficiency.

authors: Lucas M. Brugevin And Damián H. Zanette
abstract:

tldr: The paper studies demographic stochasticity in predator-prey systems and shows that intrinsic fluctuations can produce persistent oscillations even when the deterministic mean-field dynamics are damped.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how stochastic effects in activator-inhibitor or predator-prey models can sustain oscillations that deterministic descriptions predict will vanish asymptotically.
method: They analyze a stochastic predator-prey model with deterministic prey response, likely using stochastic processes or master-equation approaches to characterize oscillation persistence.
result: The analysis demonstrates that intrinsic demographic noise can drive sustained oscillations in regimes where the deterministic mean-field model exhibits only damped oscillations.
conclusion: Stochasticity can qualitatively alter the long-time dynamics of predator-prey systems, producing persistent oscillations without deterministic oscillatory instability.

tldr: The paper proposes a simple three-parameter phenomenological ansatz to model the peak, duration, and temporal evolution of a single COVID-19 epidemic wave.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a compact analytical description of epidemic wave dynamics without relying on detailed compartmental modeling.
method: A phenomenologically motivated three-parameter ansatz is fitted to describe the temporal profile of a single epidemic wave.
result: The model captures key features such as peak timing, wave duration, and overall temporal evolution of COVID-19 case data.
conclusion: The ansatz offers a simple analytical tool for characterizing single-wave epidemics, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

tldr: The paper applies a swarm-informed triggering and multiscaling analysis to earthquake diffusion during the ongoing Campi Flegrei unrest.
motivation: Earthquake diffusion is often attributed either to fluid migration or to triggering cascades in branching-process models such as ETAS, and the authors aim to distinguish these mechanisms in a volcanic unrest setting.
method: The authors analyze seismicity associated with Campi Flegrei using a swarm-informed triggering approach combined with earthquake diffusion and multiscaling methods, likely within an ETAS-like branching-process framework.
result: The study characterizes earthquake diffusion and triggering behavior during the current Campi Flegrei unrest, identifying multiscaling features consistent with long-memory epidemic-type aftershock dynamics.
conclusion: The findings support interpreting anomalous earthquake diffusion in Campi Flegrei through triggering cascades and long-memory ETAS-type processes rather than solely fluid migration.
